sourceDefinition: , aor. , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) which is the most common form, (Msb,) and , (S, TS, Mgh, Msb,) and , (K,) so in the copies of the K in the place of ; (TA;) and A^abiqa , aor. ; (IDrd, Msb, K;) inf. n. A_ibaAqN (S, Mgh, Msb) and A^aboqN and A^abaqN , (K,) or the first of these is a simple subst., and the second and third are the inf. ns.; (Msb;) He (a slave) ran away, or fled, (T, S, Mgh, Msb,) or went away, (K,) from his master, (T, Msb,) without [ being induced to do so by ] fear, or severity of work: (Msb, K:) thus the signification is restricted in the 'Eyn: (Msb:) and in this case, the law ordains that the slave shall be restored; but if the act arise from severity of work or from fear, he is not to be restored: (Lth, TA:) in the Kur xxxvii. 140, it is said of Jonas, (T, Bd,) because he fled from his people without the permission of his Lord: (Bd:) and it is also, tropically, said of a fish: (Mgh:) or he (a slave) hid himself, and then went away: (M, K:) as also ↓ tA^b~q : (M:) or this signifies, simply, he hid, or concealed, himself: or he confined, restricted, limited, restrained, or withheld, himself: (S, K:) or it has both of the last two significations: (Sgh:) and he abstained from a thing, as from a sin, or crime. (IAar, K *.) A poet says, (S,) namely, 'Ámir Ibn—Kaab, (AZ,) or 'Ámán Ibn-Kaab, or, as some say, Ghámán, (AA,) ↓ A^alaA qaAlato bahaAni wa lamo taA^ab~aqo kabirota walaA yaliyqu bika Aln~aEiymu [ Now surely Baháni said, and she did not hide herself, or did not restrain herself, Thou hast grown old, and enjoyment doth not befit thee ]: (S:) or she did not hide herself [or her mind], but said openly: (TA:) or she did not go far [from the person whom she addressed, or from the truth]; so says AZ, taking it from A_ibaAqN as relating to a slave: (TA:) or she did not abstain from her speech, as from a sin, or crime: (IAar:) or she did not disdain, or scorn. (TA.) AHát says that he asked As respecting ↓ tA^b~q , and he answered that he knew it not. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (Lth, S, M, &c.,) aor. , (Lth, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. A_ivomN , (S, K,) or A^avamN , the former being a simple subst., (Msb,) and maA^ovamN , (S, K,) He fell into what is termed A_ivomN [i. e. a sin, or crime, &c.]; (Lth, T, S, M, Msb, * K *;) [ he sinned; committed a sin, or crime; ] he did what was unlawful: (M, * K:) and ↓ taA^oviymN signifies the same as A_ivomN : (K:) it may be either an inf. n. of ↓ A^avama , which [says ISd] I have not heard, or, as Sb holds it to be, a simple subst. like tanobiytN : (M:) and is said to be used in the sense of A_ivom in the Kur lii. 23 [and lvi. 24]. (TA.) [It should be added also, that ↓ tA^ovaAmN , like tako*aAbN , is syn. with tA^oviymN and A_ivomN ; and, like tA^vym , may be an inf. n. of ↓ A^av~ama , or a simple subst.: see an ex. voce baruwqN .] In the dial. of some of the Arabs, the first letter of the aor. is with kesr, as in tiEolamu and niEolamu ; and as the hemzeh in A_ivomN is with kesr, the radical hemzeh [in the aor.] is changed into Y ; so that they say A_iyvamu and tiyvamu [for A=vamu and taA^ovamu .] (TA.) In the saying, lawo qulota maA fiY qawomahaA lamo tiyvami yafoDulahaA fiY HasabK wamiysami the meaning is, [ Shouldst thou say, thou wouldst not sin, or do wrong, in so saying,] There is not, among her people, any one who excels her [ in grounds of pretension to respect, and in impress, or character, of beauty ]. (M.) -A2- A^avamahu All~`hu fiY ka*aA , aor. (S, K) and , (S,) or , (K,) but there is no other authority than the K for this last, nor is there any reason for it, as the medial radical letter is not faucial, nor is the final, and in the Iktitáf el-Azáhir the aor. is said to be and , (MF, TA,) [ God reckoned him to have sinned, or committed a crime or the like, in such a thing; or] God reckoned such a thing against him as an A_ivom : (S, K:) or A^avamahu , aor. (Fr, T, M, Msb) and , (Msb,) inf. n. A^avomN (Fr, T, Msb) and A^avaAmN (Fr, T, TA) and A_ivaAmN , (Fr, TA,) He (God) requited him, (Fr, T,) or punished him, (M,) for what is termed A_ivomN [i. e. sin, or crime, &c.]: (Fr, T, M:) [see also A^avaAmN below:] or he (a man) pronounced him to be A=vm [i. e. a sinner, or the like ]: (Msb:) [or] ↓ A=vamahu , aor. yaw^ovimuhu , has this last signification, said of God; and also signifies He found him to be so. (T.) ― -b2- You say also, A^avamati Aln~aAqapu Alma$oYa , aor. , inf. n. A^avomN , The she-camel was slow. (M.)

sourceDefinition: He abstained from what is termed A_ivomN [i. e. sin, or crime, &c.]; (T, S, M, Msb, K;) like taHar~aja meaning “ he preserved himself from what is termed HarajN : ” (Msb:) or he did a work, or deed, whereby he escaped from what is termed A_ivomN : (TA:) and he repented of what is so termed, (M, K,) and begged forgiveness of it; as though he removed the A_ivom itself by repentance and by begging forgiveness; or sought to do so by those two means. (M.) You say also, tA^v~m mino ka*aA He abstained from such a thing as a sin, or crime; syn. taH~anava , q. v. (S, K, in art. Hnv .)

(T.) ― -b2- [Sometimes it is prefixed to a noun or pronoun denoting its object: ― -b3- and sometimes it means (assumed tropical:) The punishment of a sin &c.: see explanations of a passage in the Kur v. 32, voce baA='a .] ― -b4- Wine: (Aboo-Bekr El-Iyádee, T, S, M, K:) sometimes used in this sense; (S;) but tropically; not properly: (IAmb:) I think, [says ISd,] because the drinking thereof is what is thus termed. (M.) ― -b5- [And for a like reason,] (assumed tropical:) Contention for stakes, or wagers, in a game of hazard; syn. qimaArN ; (M, K;) which is a man's destruction of his property. (M.) (M.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaw^uwnu , inf. n. A^awonN , He was, or became, at rest, or at ease; he rested in a journey. (IAar, T.) ― -b2- A^unotu , aor. and inf. n. as above, I enjoyed a life of ease and plenty; a state of freedom from trouble or inconvenience, and toil or fatigue; a state of ease, repose, or tranquillity. (AZ, T, S, M, K.) ― -b3- I was, or became, grave, staid, steady, sedate, or calm. (S, K.) ― -b4- I was, or became, gentle; or I acted gently: (T, S, M, Msb, K:) and I acted, or proceeded, with moderation, without haste or hurry, in pace or journeying: (M:) I went gently, softly, or in a leisurely manner: (S, K:) A^awonN [the inf. n.] is formed by substitution [of A^ for h ] from hawonN . (S.) You say, A^unotu biAl$~aYo'i , and EalaY Al$~aYo'i , I was gentle, or I acted gently, with the thing; (M;) and fiY AlA^amori in the affair. (Msb.) And A^uno EalaY nafosika Act thou gently with thyself, or be thou gentle, in pace or journeying: and proceed thou with moderation, without haste or hurry: (T, S:) said in the latter sense to one who has become unsteady, or irresolute. (T.) [In like manner,] you say, EalaY qadorika ↓ A^aw~ino , meaning Ait~ay^ido EalaY naHowika [app. Act thou with moderation, gentleness, deliberation, or in a leisurely manner, according to thine ability, or to the measure of thine ability; for qadorN and naHowN are both syn. with miqodaArN ]. (T, K.) And fiY sayorikumo ↓ A^aw~inuwA Proceed ye with moderation in your course or pace or journeying. (ISk, T.) And fiY ↓ taA^aw~ana AlA^amori He paused, or was patient, in the affair. (M.) -A2- A^awonN also signifies The being weary, or fatigued; like A^ayonN . (M.) [Whether, in this sense, it have a verb, is doubtful: see its syn. here mentioned.] ― -b2- Also The putting oneself to trouble, or inconvenience, for the sake of what one may expend upon himself and his family. (M.) And hence, accord. to one [whose name is imperfectly written in the TA], the word ↓ maw^uwnapN , [as being originally maA^owunapN ,] of the measure mafoEulapN : but others say that it is of the measure faEuwlapN , from maA^anotu . (TA.) -A3- ↓ A=na A^awonuka and A^awaAnuka [and A^ayonuka ] signify the same. (M.) [See art. Ayn .]

sourceDefinition: (T, S, M, Msb, K) and ↓ A_iwaAnN , (T, M, Msb, K,) the latter mentioned by Ks on the authority of Aboo-Jámi', but the former is the usual mode of pronouncing it, (T,) and ↓ A^awonN , (M,) A time; a season: pl. And fulaAnN yaSonaEu *`lika AlA^amora A=winapF , (S, K, *) and A=yinapF , (K, [in the CK A=y^inapF ,]) Such a one does that thing sometimes, leaving it undone sometimes. (S, K. *) And A^atayotuhu A=ynapF baEoda A=yinapK I came to him times after times. (AA, T.) And A=winapF signifies Time after time. (TA, from a trad.) In the saying (of Aboo-Zubeyd, L), TalabuwA SuloHanaA walaAta A^awaAnK (M,) or A_iwaAnK , (L,) [ They sought our reconciliation with them, but it was not the time that reconciliation should be sought], accord. to Abu-l- 'Abbás, the tenween of the last word is not a sign of the genitive case, but is, as in the instance of A_i*K , because of the suppression of a proposition to which the word should be prefixed, as when you say, jiy^otu A^awaAna qaAma zayodN I came at the time that Zeyd stood. (M, L.) ― -b2- [Hence, A^awaAnay^i*K At that time or season; then; like Hiynay^i*K .]

definition: The second letter of the alphabet: called baA='N and baA ;
sourceDefinition: The second letter of the alphabet: called baA='N and baA ; (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np ;) the latter of which forms is used in spelling; like as are its analogues, as tA [and vA ] and HA [and xA and rA ] and TA [and ZA and fA and hA ] and yA ; because in this case they are not generally regarded as nouns, but as mere sounds: (Sb, M:) [these are generally pronounced with imáleh, i. e. bé, té, &c., with the exception of HA , xA , TA , and ZA ; and when they are regarded as nouns, their duals are bayaAni , tayaAni , &c.:] the pl. of baA='N is baA='aAtN ; and that of baA is A^abowaA='N (TA ubi suprà.) It is one of the letters termed majohuwrah [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; and of those termed $afahiy~ap [or labial]; and of those termed *uloq [or pronounced with the extremity of the tongue or the lips]: Kh says that the letters of the second and third classes above mentioned [the latter of which comprises the former] are those composing the words rub~a mano laf~a ; and on account of their easiness of utterance, they abound in the composition of words, so that no perfect quinqueliteral-radical word is without one or more of them, unless it is of the class termed muwal~ad , not of the classical language of the Arabs. (TA at the commencement of bAb AlbA=' .) ― -b2- In the dial. of Mázin, it is changed into m ; (TA ubi suprà;) as in bak~apu , which thus becomes mak~apu [the town of Mekkeh]. (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np .) -A2- bi is a preposition, or particle governing the gen. case; (S, Mughnee, K;) having kesr for its invariable termination because it is impossible to begin with a letter after which one makes a pause; (S;) or, correctly speaking, having a vowel for its invariable termination because it is impossible to begin with a quiescent letter; and having kesr, not fet-h, to make it accord with its government [of the gen. case], and to distinguish between it and that which is both a noun and a particle. (IB.) It is used to denote adhesion (Sb, T, S, M, Mughnee, K) of the verb to its objective complement, (S,) or of a noun or verb to that to which it is itself prefixed; (TA;) and adjunction, or association: (Sb, T:) and some say that its meaning of denoting adhesion is inseparable from it; and therefore Sb restricted himself to the mention of this meaning: (Mughnee:) or Sb says that its primary meaning is that of denoting adhesion and mixture. (Ibn-Es-Sáïgh, quoted in a marginal note in a copy of the Mughnee.) It denotes adhesion [&c.] in the proper sense; (Mughnee, K;) as in A^amosakotu bizayodK , (M, Mughnee, K,) meaning I laid hold upon, or seized, [Zeyd, or] somewhat of the body of Zeyd, or what might detain him, as an arm or a hand, or a garment, and the like; whereas A^amosakotuhu may mean I withheld him, or restrained him, from acting according to his own free will: (Mughnee:) and it denotes the same in a tropical sense; (Mughnee, K;) as in mararotu bizayodK [ I passed by Zeyd ]; (S, Mughnee, K;) as though meaning I made my passing to adhere to Zeyd; (S;) or I made my passing to adhere to a place near to Zeyd: accord. to Akh, it is for mararotu EalaYi zayodK ; but mararotu bihi is more common than mararotu Ealayohi , and is therefore more properly regarded as the original form of expression: (Mughnee:) accord. to F, the vowel of this preposition is kesr [when it is prefixed to a noun or a pronoun]; or, as some say, it is fet-h when it is with a noun properly so called; as in mar~a bazayodK : so in the K; this being the reverse of what they have prescribed in the case of [the preposition] l : but in the case of b , no vowel but kesr is known. (MF.) It denotes the same in the saying bihi daA='N [ In him is a disease; i. e. a disease is cleaving to him ]: and so [accord. to some] in A^aqosamotu bA@ll~`hi [ I swore, or, emphatically, I swear, by God; and similar phrases, respecting which see a later division of this paragraph]. (L.) So, too, in A^a$oraka bA@ll~`hi , because meaning He associated another with God: and in wak~alotu bifulaAnK , meaning I associated a wakiyl [or factor &c.] with such a one. (T.) [And so in other phrases here following.] Ealayoka bizayodK Keep thou to Zeyd: or take thou Zeyd. (TA voce EalaY .) Ealayoka bika*aA Keep thou to such a thing: (El-Munáwee:) or take thou such a thing. (Ham p. 216.) fabahaA wanaEomato Keep thou to it, fbhA meaning faEalayoka bihaA , (Mgh in art. nEm ,) [or let him keep to it, i. e. faEalayohi bihaA ,] or thou hast taken to, or adopted and followed, or adhered to, the established way, or the way established by the Prophet, i. e. fabiA@ls~un~api A^axa*ata , (Mgh,) or he hath taken to, &c., i. e. fabiA@ls~un~api A^axa*a , (IAth, TA in art. nEm ,) or by this practice, or action, is excellence attained, or he will attain excellence, i. e. fabih`*ihi AlxaSolapi A^awi AlfaEolapi yunaAlu AlfaDolu , or yanaAlu AlfaDola ; (IAth ubi suprà;) and excellent is the practise, the established way, or the way established by the Prophet, wnEmt meaning waniEomati AlxaSolapu Als~un~apu , (Mgh,) or and excellent is the practice, or the action, i. e. waniEomati AlxaSolapu , (S and K in art. nEm ,) or waniEomati AlxaSolapu A^uwi AlfaEolapu : (IAth ubi suprà:) and it also occurs in a trad., where the meaning is [He who hath done such a thing hath adhered to the ordinance of indulgence; and excellent is the practice, or action, &c.: for here fbhA is meant to imply] fabiA@lr~axoSapi A^axa*a . (TA in the present art. See also art. nEm .) ― -b2- It is also used to render a verb transitive; (Mughnee, K;) having the same effect as hemzeh [prefixed], in causing [what would otherwise be] the agent to become an objective complement; as in *ahabotu bizayodK syn. with A^a*ohabotuhu [ I made Zeyd to go away; or I took him away ]; (Mughnee;) and hence, [in the Kur ii. 16,] *ahaba A@ll~`hu binuwrihimo [ God taketh away their light ]; (Mughnee, K;) which refutes the assertion of Mbr and Suh, that *ahabotu bizayodK means [ I went away with Zeyd; i. e.] I accompanied Zeyd in going away. (Mughnee.) J says that any verb that is not trans. you may render so by means of bi and A [prefixed] and reduplication [of the medial radical letter]: you say, TaAra bihi and A^aTaArahu and Tay~arahu [as meaning He made him to fly, or to fly away ]: but IB says that this is not correct as of common application; for some verbs are rendered trans. by means of hemzeh, but not by reduplication; and some by reduplication, but not by hemzeh; and some by b , but not by hemzeh nor by reduplication: you say, dafaEotu zayodFA biEamorKw [as meaning I made ' Amr to repel Zeyd, lit. I repelled Zeyd by ' Amr ], but not A^adofaEotuhu nor daf~aEotuhu . (TA.) ― -b3- It also denotes the employing a thing as an aid or instrument; (S, M, * Mughnee, K; *) as in katabotu biAlqalami [ I wrote with the reed-pen ]; (S, Mughnee, K;) and najarotu biAlqaduwmi [ I worked as a carpenter with the adz ]; (Mughnee, K;) and Darabotu bAls~ayofi [ I struck with the sword ]. (M.) And hence the bi in bisomi A@ll~`hi , (Mughnee, K,) accord. to some, because the action [before which it is pronounced] is not practicable in the most perfect manner but by means of it: (Mughnee:) but others disallow this, because the name of God should not be regarded as an instrument: (MF, TA:) and some say that the b here is to denote beginning, as though one said, A^abotadaA^u bisomi A@ll~`hi [ I begin with the name of God ]. (TA.) ― -b4- It also denotes a cause; as in A_in~akumo Zalamotumo A^anofusakumo biA@t~ixaA*ikumu A@loEijola [ Verily ye have wronged yourselves by, i. e. because of, your taking to yourselves the calf as a god (Kur ii. 51)]; and in fakul~FA A^axa*onaA bi*anobihi [ And every one of these we have punished for, i. e. because of, his sin (Kur xxix. 39)]; (Mughnee, K) and in lano yadoxula A^aHadakumu Aljan~apa biEamalihi [ Not any of you shall enter Paradise by, or for, or because of, his works ]. (TA from a trad.) And so in laqaytu bizayodK AlA^asada I met, or found, by reason of my meeting, or finding, Zeyd, the lion: (Mughnee:) or the b in this instance denotes comparison; [i. e. I met, or found, in Zeyd the like of the lion; ] as also in raA^ayotu bifulaAnK Alqamara [ I saw in such a one the like of the moon ]. (TA.) Another ex. of the same usage is the saying [of a poet], qado suqiyato A=baAluhumo biAln~aAri waAln~aAru qado ta$ofiY mina AlA^uwaAri [ Their camels had been watered because of the brand that they bore: for fire, or the brand, sometimes cures of the heat of thirst ]; i. e., because of their being branded with the names [or marks] of their owners, they had free access left them to the water. (Mughnee. See also another reading of this verse voce naArN .) [In like manner] it is used in the sense of mino A^ajoli [which means bisababi (Msb in art. Ajl )] in the saying of Lebeed, gulobN ta$a*~ara biAl*~uHuwli kaA^an~ahaA jin~u AlbadiY~i rawaAsiyAF A^aqodaAmuhaA (S) Thick-necked men, like lions, who threatened one another because of rancorous feelings, as though they were the Jinn of the valley El-Bedee, [or of the desert, (TA in art. bdw ,)] their feet standing firm in contention and obstinate altercation. (EM pp. 174 and 175.) It is also used to denote a cause when prefixed to A^an~a and to maA as in *`lika biA^an~ahumo kaAnuwA yakofuruwna biA=yaAti A@ll~`hi [ That was because they used to disbelieve in the signs of God ]; and in *`lika bimaA EaSawoA [ That was because they disobeyed ]: both instances in the Kur ii. 58. (Bd.) ― -b5- It is also used to denote concomitance, as syn. with maEa ; (Mughnee, K;) as in Ai$otarayotu Alfarasa bilijaAmihi wasarojihi [ I bought the horse with his bit and bridle and his saddle ]; (TA;) and in lam~aA raA=niY biAls~alaAHi haraba , i. e. When he saw me advancing with the weapon, [he fled;] or when he saw me possessor of a weapon; (Sh, T;) and in AihobiTo bisalaAmK [ Descend thou with security, or with greeting (Kur xi. 50)]; and in waqado daxaluwA biA@lokufori [ They having entered with unbelief (Kur v. 66)]; (Mughnee, K;) bAlkfr being a denotative of state. (Bd.) Authors differ respecting the b in the saying, fasab~iHo biHamodi rab~ika , in the Kur [xv. 98 and ex. 3]; some saying that it denotes concomitance, and that Hmd is prefixed to the objective complement, so that the meaning is, sab~iHohN HaAmidFA lahu [ Declare thou his (thy Lord's) freedom from everything derogatory from his glory, praising Him ], i. e. declare thou his freedom from that which is not suitable to Him, and ascribe to Him that which is suitable to Him; but others say that it denotes the employing a thing as an aid or instrument, and that Hmd is prefixed to the agent, so that the meaning is, sab~iHohu bimaA Hamida bihi nafosahu [ declare thou his (thy Lord's) freedom from everything derogatory from his glory by means of ascribing to Him that wherewith He hath praised himself ]: and so, too, respecting the saying, suboHaAnaka A@ll~`hum~a wabiHamodika ; some asserting that it is one proposition, the, being redundant; but others saying, it is two propositions, the w being a conjunction, and the verb upon which the b is dependent being suppressed, so that the meaning is, [ I declare thy freedom from everything derogatory from thy glory, 0 God, ] wabiHamodika sab~aHotuka [ and with the praising of Thee, or by means of the praise that belongeth to Thee, I declare thy freedom &c.]. (Mughnee. [Other explanations of these two phrases have been proposed; but those given above are the most approved.]) You also say, EalaY~a bihi , meaning Bring thou him, [i. e.] come with him, to me. (Har p. 109.) DaAqato Ealayohimu A@loA^aroDu bimaA raHubato , in the Kur ix. 119, means biruHobihaA [i. e. The earth became strait to them, with, meaning notwithstanding, its amplitude, or spaciousness ]. (Bd.) Sometimes the negative lA intervenes between bi [denoting concomitance] and the noun governed by it in the gen. case; [so that bilaA signifies Without; ] as in jiy^otu bilaA zaAdK [ I came without travelling-provision ]. (Mughnee and K in art. lA .) ― -b6- It is also syn. with fiY before a noun signifying a place or a time; (Mughnee, * K, * TA;) as in jalasotu biAlmasojidi [ I sat in the mosque ]; (TA;) and walaqado naSarakumu A@ll~`hu bibadorK [ And verily God aided you against your enemies at Bedr (Kur iii. 119)]; and naj~ayonaAhumo bisaHarK [ We saved them a little before daybreak (Kur liv. 34)]: (Mughnee, K, TA:) and so in biA^ay~ikumu A@lomafotuwnu (T, K,) in the Kur [lxviii. 6], (TA,) accord. to some, (T, Mughnee,) i. e. In which of you is madness; or in which of the two parties of you is the mad: (Bd:) or the b is here redundant; (Sb, Bd, Mughnee;) the meaning being which of you is he who is afflicted with madness. (Bd. [See also a later division of this paragraph.]) ― -b7- It also denotes substitution; [meaning Instead of, or in place of; ] as in the saying [of the Hamásee (Mughnee)], falayota liY bihimu qawomFA A_i*aA rakibuwA $an~awA AlA_igaArapa furosaAnFA warukobaAnaA [ Then would that I had, instead of them, a people who, when they mounted their beasts, poured the sudden attack, they being horsemen and camel-riders ]; (Ham p. 8, Mughnee, K;) i. e., badalFA bihimo (TA:) but some read $ad~uwA AlA_igaArapa , [and so it is in some, app., the most correct, of the copies of the Mughnee,] for $ad~uwA liloA_igaAripi [ hastened for the making a sudden attack ]. (Ham, Mughnee.) So, too, in the saying, AiEotaDotu bih`*iA Alv~awobi xayorFA minohu [ I received, in the place of this garment, or piece of cloth, one better than it ]; and laqiytu bizayodK baHorFA [ I found, in the place of Zeyd, a man of abundant generosity or beneficence ]; and h`*aA bi*aAki [ This is instead, or in the place, of that; but see another explanation of this last phrase in what follows]. (The Lubáb, TA.) ― -b8- It also denotes requital; or the giving, or doing, in return; (Mughnee, K;) and in this case is prefixed to the word signifying the substitute, or thing given or done in exchange [or return; or to the word signifying that for which a substitute is given, or for which a thing is given or done in exchange or return]; (Mughnee;) as in the saying, Ai$otarayotuhu biA^alofi dirohamK [ I purchased it for a thousand dirhems ]; (Mughnee, K; *) [and in the saying in the Kur ix. 112, A_in~a A@ll~`ha A@$otarY mina A@lomuw^ominiyna A^anofusahumo waA^amowaAlahumo biA^an~a lahumu A@lojan~apa Verily God hath purchased of the believers their souls and their possessions for the price of their having Paradise; ] and kaAfaA^otu A_iHosaAnahu biDiEofK [ I requited his beneficence with a like beneficence, or with double, or more ], (Mughnee,) or kaAfA^otuhu biDiEofi A_iHosaAnihi [ I requited him with the like, or with double the amount, or with more than double the amount, of his beneficence ], (K,) but the former is preferable; (TA;) [and xadama biTaEaAmi biTonihi (S and A &c. in art. wgd ) He served for, meaning in return for, the food of his belly; ] and h`*aA bi*aAka walaA EatobN EalaY Alz~amani [ This is in return for that, (an explanation somewhat differing from one in the next preceding division of this paragraph,) and no blame is imputable to fortune ]: and hence, AudoxuluwA A@ljan~apa bimaA kunotumo taEomaluwna [ Enter ye Paradise in return for that which ye wrought (Kur xvi. 34)]; for the b here is not that which denotes a cause, as the Moatezileh assert it to be, and as all [of the Sunnees] hold it to be in the saying of the Prophet, lano yadoxula A^aHadukumu Aljan~apa biEamalihi [before cited and explained]; because what is given instead of something is sometimes given gratuitously; and it is evident that there is no mutual opposition between the trad. and the verse of the Kur-án. (Mughnee.) ― -b9- It is also syn. with Eano ; and is said to be peculiar to interrogation; as in faA@soA^alo bihi xabiyrFA [ And ask thou respecting Him, or it, one possessing knowledge (Kur xxv. 60)]; (Mughnee, K;) and accord. to IAar in the Kur lxx. 1; (T;) and in the saying of ' Alkameh, faA_ino tasoA^aluwniY biAln~isaA='i faA_in~aniy baSiyrN biA^adowaA='i Aln~isaA='i xabiyru [ And if ye ask me respecting the diseases of women, verily I am knowing in the diseases of women, skilful ]: (A' Obeyd, TA:) or it is not peculiar to interrogation; as in wayawoma ta$aq~aqu A@ls~amaA='u biA@logamaAmi [ And the day when the heavens shall be rent asunder from the clouds (Kur xxv. 27)]; (Mughnee, K) and maA gar~aka birab~ika (K) i. e. What hath beguiled thee from thy Lord, and from believing in him? in the Kur lxxxii. 6; and so in the same, lvii. 13: (TA: [but see art. gr :]) or, accord. to Z, the b in bAlgmAm means by, as by an instrument; (Mughnee;) or it means because of, or by means of, the rising of the clouds therefrom: (Bd:) and in like manner the Basrees explain it as occurring in faA@soA^alo bihi xabiyrFA , as denoting the cause; and they assert that it is never syn. with Eano ; but their explanation is improbable. (Mughnee.) ― -b10- It is also syn. with EalaYi ; as in A_ino tiA^omanohu biqinoTaArK (Mughnee, K *) or bidiynaArK (S) [ If thou give him charge over a hundredweight or over a deenár (Kur iii. 68)]; like as EalaY is sometimes put in the place of bi as after the verb raDiYa : (S, TA:) and so in lawo tusaw~aY bihimu A@loA^aroDu [ That the ground were made even over them ], in the Kur [iv. 45], (TA,) i. e. that they were buried; (Bd) and in mararotu bizayodK [ I passed by Zeyd ], accord. to Akh, as before mentioned; (Mughnee, in the first division of the art. on this preposition;) and in zayodN biAls~aToHi [ Zeyd is on the roof ]; (TA;) and in a verse cited in this Lex. voce vaEolabN . (Mughnee.) ― -b11- It also denotes part of a whole; (Msb in art. bED Mughnee, K;) so accord. to As and AAF and others; (Msb, Mughnee;) as syn. with mino (Msb, TA:) IKt says; the Arabs say, $aribotu bimaA='i ka*aA , meaning minohu [ I drank of such a water ]; and AZ mentions, as a saying of the Arabs, saqaAka A@ll~`hu mino maA='i ka*aA , meaning bihi [ May God give thee to drink of such a water ], thus making the two prepositions syn.: (Msb: [in which five similar instances are cited from poets; and two of these are cited also in the Mughnee:]) and thus it signifies in EayonFA ya$orabu bihaA EibaAdu A@ll~`hi [ A fountain from which the servants of God shall drink, in the Kur lxxvi. 6; and the like occurs in lxxxiii. 28]; (Msb, Mughnee, K;) accord. to the authorities mentioned above; (Mughnee;) or the meaning is, with which the servants of God shall satisfy their thirst ( yarowaY bihaA ); (T, Mughnee;) or, accord. to Z, with which the servants of God shall drink wine: (Mughnee:) if the b were redundant, [as some assert it to be, (Bd,)] the meaning would be, that they shall drink the whole of it; which is not right: (Msb:) thus, also, it is used in waA@mosaHuwA biruw^u=sikumo [in the Kur v. 8], (Msb, Mughnee, K,) accord. to some; (Mughnee;) i. e. [ And wipe ye] a part of your heads; and this explanation has been given as on the authority of EshSháfi'ee; but he is said to have disapproved it, and to have held that the b here denotes adhesion: (TA:) this latter is its apparent meaning in this and the other instances: or, as some say, in this last instance it is used to denote the employing a thing as an aid or instrument, and there is an ellipsis in the phrase, and an inversion; the meaning being, AimosaHuwA ruw^u=sakumo biAlmaA='i [ wipe ye your heads with water ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b12- It is also used to denote swearing; (Mughnee, K;) and is the primary one of the particles used for this purpose; therefore it is peculiarly distinguished by its being allowable to mention the verb with it, (Mughnee,) as A^uqosimu biA@ll~`hi laA^afoEalan~a [ I swear by God I will assuredly do such a thing]; (Mughnee, K) and by its being prefixed to a pronoun, as in bika laA^afoEalan~a [ By thee I will assuredly do such a thing]; and by its being used in adjuring, or conjuring, for the purpose of inducing one to incline to that which is desired of him, as in bA@ll~`hi halo qaAma zayodN , meaning I adjure thee, or conjure thee, by God, to tell me, did Zeyd stand? (Mughnee.) [See also the first explanation of this particle, where it is said, on the authority of the L, that, when thus used, it denotes adhesion.] ― -b13- It is also syn. with A_ilay as denoting the end of an extent or interval; as in A^aHosana biY , meaning He did good, or acted well, to me: (Mughnee, K:) but some say that the verb here imports the meaning of laTafa [which is trans. by means of b , i. e. he acted graciously, or courteously, with me ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b14- It is also redundant, (S, Mughnee, K,) to denote corroboration: (Mughnee, K:) and is prefixed to the agent: (Mughnee:) first, necessarily; as in A^aHosino bizayodK ; (Mughnee, K;) accord. to general opinion (Mughnee) originally A^aHosana zayodN , i. e. SaAra *aA HusonK [ Zeyd became possessed of goodness, or goodliness, or beauty ]; (Mughnee, K; *) or the correct meaning is Hasuna zayodN [ Good, or goodly, or beautiful, or very good &c., is Zeyd! or how good, or goodly, or beautiful, is Zeyd! ], as in the B: (TA:) secondly, in most instances; and this is in the case of the agent of kafaY ; as in kafaY biA@ll~`hi $ahiydFA [ God sufficeth, being witness, or as a witness (Kur xiii., last verse; &c.)]; (Mughnee, K [and a similar ex. is given in the S, from the Kur xxv. 33;]) the b here denoting emphatic praise; but you may drop it, saying, kafaY A@ll~`hu $ahiydFA : (Fr, TA:) thirdly, in a case of necessity, by poetic licence; as in the saying, A^alamo yaA^otiyka waAlA^anobaA='u tanomiY bimaA laAqato labuwnu baniY ziyaAdi [ Did not what the milch camel of the sons of Ziyád experienced come to thee ( yaA^otiyka being in like manner put for yaA^otika ) when the tidings were increasing? ]. (Mughnee, K.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the objective complement of a verb; as in walaA tuloquwA biA^ayodykumo A_ilaY A@lt~aholukapi [ And cast ye not yourselves ( bA^ydykm meaning biA^anofusikumo ) to perdition (Kur ii. 191)]; and in wahuz~iY A_ilayoki biji*oEi Aln~axolapi [ And shake thou towards thee the trunk of the palm-tree (Kur xix. 25)]: but some say that the former means and cast ye not yourselves ( A^anofusakumo being understood) with your hands to perdition; or that the meaning is, by means, or because, of your hands: (Mughnee:) and ISd says that huz~iY , in the latter, is made trans. by means of b because it is used in the sense of juz~iY : (TA in art hz :) so, too, in the saying, naDoribu biAls~ayofi wa narjuw biAlfarajo [ We smite with the sword, and we hope for the removal of grief ]: (S, Mughnee:) and in the trad., kafay biAlmaro'i ka*ibFA A^ano yuHad~iva bikul~i maA samiEa [ It suffices the man in respect of lying that he relate all that he has heard ]. (Mughnee.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the inchoative; as in biHasobika [when you say, biHasobika dirohamN , meaning A thing sufficing thee is a dirhem; a phrase which may be used in two ways; as predicating of what is sufficient, that it is a dirhem; and as predicating of a dirhem, that it is sufficient; in which latter case, bHsbk is an enunciative put before its inchoative, so that the meaning is, a dirhem is a thing sufficing thee, i. e. a dirhem is sufficient for thee; as is shown in a marginal note in my copy of the Mughnee: in the latter way is used the saying, mentioned in the S, biHasobika qawolu Als~awo'i A thing sufficing thee is the saying what is evil: and so, app., each of the following sayings, mentioned in the TA on the authority of Fr; Hasobuka biSadiyqinaA A person sufficing thee is our friend; and naAhiyka biA^axiynaA A person sufficing thee is our brother: the b is added, as Fr says, to denote emphatic praise]: so too in xarajotu faA_i*iA bizayodK [ I went forth, and lo, there, or then, was Zeyd ]; and in kayofa bika A_i*aA kaAna ka*aA [ How art thou, or how wilt thou be, when it is thus, or when such a thing is the case? ]; and so, accord. to Sb, in biA^y~ikumu A@lomafotuwnu [mentioned before, in explanation of bi as syn. with fiY ]; but Abu-l-Hasan says that bA^y~km is dependent upon AisotiqoraAr suppressed, denoting the predicate of Aalmftwn ; and some say that this is an inf. n. in the sense of finonapN ; [so that the meaning may be, bA^ay~ikumu Almafotuwnu musotaqir~N In which of you is madness residing? ]; or, as some say, bi is here syn. with fiY [as I have before mentioned], (Mughnee.) A strange case is that of its being added before that which is originally an inchoative, namely, the noun, or subject, of layosa , on the condition of its being transferred to the later place which is properly that of the enunciative; as in the reading of some, wujuwhakumo ] layosa A@lbir~a biA^ano tuwal~uwA [ qabala A@loma$oriqi wa A@lomagoribi [ Your turning your faces towards the east and the west is not obedience (Kur ii. 172)]; with Albr~ in the accus. case. (Mughnee.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the enunciative; and this is in two kinds of cases: first, when the phrase is not affirmative; and cases of this kind may be followed as exs.; as layosa zayodN biqaAy^imK [ Zeyd is not standing ]; and wamaA A@ll~`hu bigaAfilK Eam~aA taEomaluwna [ And God is not heedless of that which ye do (Kur ii. 69, &c.)]: secondly, when the phrase is affirmative; and in cases of this kind, one limits himself to what has been heard [from the Arabs]: so say Akh and his followers; and they hold to be an instance of this kind the phrase, jazaA='u say~iy^apK bimivolihaA [ The recompense of an evil action is the like thereof (Kur x. 28)]; and the saying of the Hamásee, wamanoEukahaA bi$aYo'K yusotaTaAEu [ And the preventing thee from having her (referring to a mare) is a thing that is possible ]: but it is more proper to make bmvlhA dependent upon AisotiqoraAr suppressed, as the enunciative; [the meaning being, jazaA='u say~ay^apK musotaqir~N bimivolihaA , or yasotaqir~u bimivolihaA , i. e. the recompense of an evil action is a thing consisting in the like thereof ]; and to make b$Y' dependent upon mnEkhA ; the meaning being, wa manoEukahaA bi$aYo'K m~aA yusotaTaAEu [i. e. and the preventing thee from having her, by something, is possible: see Ham p. 102 ]: Ibn-Málik also [holds, like Akh and his followers, that bi may be redundant when prefixed to the enunciative in an affirmative proposition; for he] says, respecting biHasobika zayodN , that zyd is an inchoative placed after its enunciative, [so that the meaning is, Zeyd is a person sufficing thee, ] because zayodN is determinate and Hasobuka is indeterminate. (Mughnee. [See also what has been said above respecting the phrase biHasobika dirohamN , in treating of bi as added before the inchoative.]) It is also redundantly prefixed to the denotative of state of which the governing word is made negative; as in famaA rajaEato bixaAy^ibapK rikaAbN Hakiymu bonu Almusay~abi munotahaAhaA [ And travelling-camels (meaning their riders) returned not disappointed, whose goal, or ultimate object, was Hakeem the son of El-Museiyab ]; and in famaA A@nobaEavota bimazow^udK wa laA wakali [ And thou didst not, being sent, or roused, go away frightened, nor impotent, committing thine affair to another ]: so says Ibn-Málik: but AHei disagrees with him, explaining these two exs. as elliptical; the meaning implied in the former being, biHaAjapK xaAy^ibapK [ with an object of want disappointed, or frustrated ]; and in the second, bi$axoSK mazow^uwdK , i. e. ma*oEuwrK [ with a person frightened ]; the poet meaning, by the mzw^wd , himself, after the manner of the saying, raA^ayotu minohu A^asadFA ; and this is plain with respect to the former ex., but not with respect to the second; for the negation of attributes of dispraise denoted as intensive in degree does not involve the negation of what is simply essential in those attributes; and one does not say, laqiytu minohu A^asadFA , or baHorFA , [or raA^ayotu minohu A^asadFA , as above, or baHorFA ,] but when meaning to express an intensive degree of boldness, or of generosity. (Mughnee.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the corroborative nafosN and EayonN : and some hold it to be so in yatarab~ana biA^anofusihin~a [as meaning Shall themselves wait (Kur ii. 228 and 234)]: but this presents matter for consideration; because the affixed pronoun in the nom. case, [whether expressed, as in this instance, in which it is the final syllable na , or implied in the verb,] when corroborated by nafos , should properly be corroborated first by the separate [pronoun], as in qumotumo A^anotumo A^anofusukumo [Ye stood, ye, yourselves]; and because the corroboration in this instance is lost, since it cannot be imagined that any others are here meant than those who are commanded to wait: [the preferable rendering is, shall wait to see what may take place with themselves: ] bA^nfshn~ is added only for rousing them the more to wait, by making known that their minds should not be directed towards the men. (Mughnee.) Accord. to some, it is also redundantly prefixed to a noun governed in the gen. case [by another preposition]; as in fA^aSobaHona laA yasoA^alonahu Eano biA^abihi And they became in a condition in which they asked him not respecting his father; which may perhaps be regarded by some as similar to the saying, yaDoHakona Eano kaAlbaradi Almunoham~i but in this instance, ka is generally held to be a noun, syn. with mivol ]. (The Lubáb, TA.) ― -b15- Sometimes it is understood; as in All~`h lAfEln~ [i. e. All~`hi laA^afoEalan~a and All~`ha laA^afoEalan~a By God, I will assuredly do such a thing; in the latter as well as the former, for a noun is often put in the accus. case because of a preposition understood; or, accord. to Bd, in ii. 1, a verb significant of swearing is understood]: and in xayorK [for bixayorK In a good state ], addressed to him who says, kayofa A^aSobaHota [How hast thou entered upon the time of morning? or How hast thou become?]. (TA.) ― -b16- [It occurs also in several elliptical phrases; one of which ( fabihaA wa niEomato ) has been mentioned among the exs. of its primary meaning: some are mentioned in other arts.; as biA^abiY and binafosiY , in arts. Abw and nfs : and there are many others, of which exs. here follow.] Mohammad is related, in a trad., to have said, after hitting a butt with an arrow, A^anaA bhaA A^anaA bhaA , meaning A^anaA SaAHibuhaA [ I am the doer of it! I am the doer of it! ]. (Sh, T.) And in another trad., Mohammad is related to have said to one who told him of a man's having committed an unlawful action, laEal~aka bi*`liki , meaning laEal~aka SaAHibu AlA^amori [ May-be thou art the doer of that thing ]. (T.) And in another, he is related to have said to a woman brought to him for having committed adultery or fornication, mano biki , meaning mano SaAHibuki [ Who was thine accomplice? ]: (T:) or mani AlfaAEilu biki [ Who was the agent with thee? ]. (TA.) A^anaA bika walaka , occurring in a form of prayer, means I seek, or take, refuge in Thee; or by thy right disposal and facilitation I worship; and to Thee, not to any other, I humble myself. (Mgh in art. bwA .) One says also, mano liY bika*aA , meaning Who will be responsible, answerable, amenable, or surety, to me for such a thing? (Har p. 126: and the like is said in p. 191.) And similar to this is the saying, kaA^an~iY bika , meaning kaA^an~iy A^aboSuru bika [It is as though I saw thee ]; i. e. I know from what I witness of thy condition to-day how thy condition will be to-morrow; so that it is as though I saw thee in that condition. (Idem p. 126.) [You also say, kaA^an~aka bihi , meaning Thou art so near to him that it is as though thou sawest him: or it is as though thou wert with him: i. e. thou art almost in his presence.] ― -b17- The Basrees hold that prepositions do not supply the places of other prepositions regularly; but are imagined to do so when they admit of being differently rendered; or it is because a word is sometimes used in the sense of another word, as in $aribona bimaA='i AlbaHori meaning rawiyna , and in A^aHosana biY meaning laTafa ; or else because they do so anomalously. (Mughnee.) -A3- [As a numeral, b denotes Two. ]

rawSourceText: The second letter of the alphabet: called baA='N and baA ; (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np ;) the latter of which forms is used in spelling; like as are its analogues, as tA [and vA ] and HA [and xA and rA ] and TA [and ZA and fA and hA ] and yA ; because in this case they are not generally regarded as nouns, but as mere sounds: (Sb, M:) [these are generally pronounced with imáleh, i. e. bé, té, &c., with the exception of HA , xA , TA , and ZA ; and when they are regarded as nouns, their duals are bayaAni , tayaAni , &c.:] the pl. of baA='N is baA='aAtN ; and that of baA is A^abowaA='N (TA ubi suprà.) It is one of the letters termed majohuwrah [or vocal, i. e. pronounced with the voice, and not with the breath only]; and of those termed $afahiy~ap [or labial]; and of those termed *uloq [or pronounced with the extremity of the tongue or the lips]: Kh says that the letters of the second and third classes above mentioned [the latter of which comprises the former] are those composing the words rub~a mano laf~a ; and on account of their easiness of utterance, they abound in the composition of words, so that no perfect quinqueliteral-radical word is without one or more of them, unless it is of the class termed muwal~ad , not of the classical language of the Arabs. (TA at the commencement of bAb AlbA=' .) ― -b2- In the dial. of Mázin, it is changed into m ; (TA ubi suprà;) as in bak~apu , which thus becomes mak~apu [the town of Mekkeh]. (TA in bAb AlAlf Ally~np .) -A2- bi is a preposition, or particle governing the gen. case; (S, Mughnee, K;) having kesr for its invariable termination because it is impossible to begin with a letter after which one makes a pause; (S;) or, correctly speaking, having a vowel for its invariable termination because it is impossible to begin with a quiescent letter; and having kesr, not fet-h, to make it accord with its government [of the gen. case], and to distinguish between it and that which is both a noun and a particle. (IB.) It is used to denote adhesion (Sb, T, S, M, Mughnee, K) of the verb to its objective complement, (S,) or of a noun or verb to that to which it is itself prefixed; (TA;) and adjunction, or association: (Sb, T:) and some say that its meaning of denoting adhesion is inseparable from it; and therefore Sb restricted himself to the mention of this meaning: (Mughnee:) or Sb says that its primary meaning is that of denoting adhesion and mixture. (Ibn-Es-Sáïgh, quoted in a marginal note in a copy of the Mughnee.) It denotes adhesion [&c.] in the proper sense; (Mughnee, K;) as in A^amosakotu bizayodK , (M, Mughnee, K,) meaning I laid hold upon, or seized, [Zeyd, or] somewhat of the body of Zeyd, or what might detain him, as an arm or a hand, or a garment, and the like; whereas A^amosakotuhu may mean I withheld him, or restrained him, from acting according to his own free will: (Mughnee:) and it denotes the same in a tropical sense; (Mughnee, K;) as in mararotu bizayodK [ I passed by Zeyd ]; (S, Mughnee, K;) as though meaning I made my passing to adhere to Zeyd; (S;) or I made my passing to adhere to a place near to Zeyd: accord. to Akh, it is for mararotu EalaYi zayodK ; but mararotu bihi is more common than mararotu Ealayohi , and is therefore more properly regarded as the original form of expression: (Mughnee:) accord. to F, the vowel of this preposition is kesr [when it is prefixed to a noun or a pronoun]; or, as some say, it is fet-h when it is with a noun properly so called; as in mar~a bazayodK : so in the K; this being the reverse of what they have prescribed in the case of [the preposition] l : but in the case of b , no vowel but kesr is known. (MF.) It denotes the same in the saying bihi daA='N [ In him is a disease; i. e. a disease is cleaving to him ]: and so [accord. to some] in A^aqosamotu bA@ll~`hi [ I swore, or, emphatically, I swear, by God; and similar phrases, respecting which see a later division of this paragraph]. (L.) So, too, in A^a$oraka bA@ll~`hi , because meaning He associated another with God: and in wak~alotu bifulaAnK , meaning I associated a wakiyl [or factor &c.] with such a one. (T.) [And so in other phrases here following.] Ealayoka bizayodK Keep thou to Zeyd: or take thou Zeyd. (TA voce EalaY .) Ealayoka bika*aA Keep thou to such a thing: (El-Munáwee:) or take thou such a thing. (Ham p. 216.) fabahaA wanaEomato Keep thou to it, fbhA meaning faEalayoka bihaA , (Mgh in art. nEm ,) [or let him keep to it, i. e. faEalayohi bihaA ,] or thou hast taken to, or adopted and followed, or adhered to, the established way, or the way established by the Prophet, i. e. fabiA@ls~un~api A^axa*ata , (Mgh,) or he hath taken to, &c., i. e. fabiA@ls~un~api A^axa*a , (IAth, TA in art. nEm ,) or by this practice, or action, is excellence attained, or he will attain excellence, i. e. fabih`*ihi AlxaSolapi A^awi AlfaEolapi yunaAlu AlfaDolu , or yanaAlu AlfaDola ; (IAth ubi suprà;) and excellent is the practise, the established way, or the way established by the Prophet, wnEmt meaning waniEomati AlxaSolapu Als~un~apu , (Mgh,) or and excellent is the practice, or the action, i. e. waniEomati AlxaSolapu , (S and K in art. nEm ,) or waniEomati AlxaSolapu A^uwi AlfaEolapu : (IAth ubi suprà:) and it also occurs in a trad., where the meaning is [He who hath done such a thing hath adhered to the ordinance of indulgence; and excellent is the practice, or action, &c.: for here fbhA is meant to imply] fabiA@lr~axoSapi A^axa*a . (TA in the present art. See also art. nEm .) ― -b2- It is also used to render a verb transitive; (Mughnee, K;) having the same effect as hemzeh [prefixed], in causing [what would otherwise be] the agent to become an objective complement; as in *ahabotu bizayodK syn. with A^a*ohabotuhu [ I made Zeyd to go away; or I took him away ]; (Mughnee;) and hence, [in the Kur ii. 16,] *ahaba A@ll~`hu binuwrihimo [ God taketh away their light ]; (Mughnee, K;) which refutes the assertion of Mbr and Suh, that *ahabotu bizayodK means [ I went away with Zeyd; i. e.] I accompanied Zeyd in going away. (Mughnee.) J says that any verb that is not trans. you may render so by means of bi and A [prefixed] and reduplication [of the medial radical letter]: you say, TaAra bihi and A^aTaArahu and Tay~arahu [as meaning He made him to fly, or to fly away ]: but IB says that this is not correct as of common application; for some verbs are rendered trans. by means of hemzeh, but not by reduplication; and some by reduplication, but not by hemzeh; and some by b , but not by hemzeh nor by reduplication: you say, dafaEotu zayodFA biEamorKw [as meaning I made ' Amr to repel Zeyd, lit. I repelled Zeyd by ' Amr ], but not A^adofaEotuhu nor daf~aEotuhu . (TA.) ― -b3- It also denotes the employing a thing as an aid or instrument; (S, M, * Mughnee, K; *) as in katabotu biAlqalami [ I wrote with the reed-pen ]; (S, Mughnee, K;) and najarotu biAlqaduwmi [ I worked as a carpenter with the adz ]; (Mughnee, K;) and Darabotu bAls~ayofi [ I struck with the sword ]. (M.) And hence the bi in bisomi A@ll~`hi , (Mughnee, K,) accord. to some, because the action [before which it is pronounced] is not practicable in the most perfect manner but by means of it: (Mughnee:) but others disallow this, because the name of God should not be regarded as an instrument: (MF, TA:) and some say that the b here is to denote beginning, as though one said, A^abotadaA^u bisomi A@ll~`hi [ I begin with the name of God ]. (TA.) ― -b4- It also denotes a cause; as in A_in~akumo Zalamotumo A^anofusakumo biA@t~ixaA*ikumu A@loEijola [ Verily ye have wronged yourselves by, i. e. because of, your taking to yourselves the calf as a god (Kur ii. 51)]; and in fakul~FA A^axa*onaA bi*anobihi [ And every one of these we have punished for, i. e. because of, his sin (Kur xxix. 39)]; (Mughnee, K) and in lano yadoxula A^aHadakumu Aljan~apa biEamalihi [ Not any of you shall enter Paradise by, or for, or because of, his works ]. (TA from a trad.) And so in laqaytu bizayodK AlA^asada I met, or found, by reason of my meeting, or finding, Zeyd, the lion: (Mughnee:) or the b in this instance denotes comparison; [i. e. I met, or found, in Zeyd the like of the lion; ] as also in raA^ayotu bifulaAnK Alqamara [ I saw in such a one the like of the moon ]. (TA.) Another ex. of the same usage is the saying [of a poet], qado suqiyato A=baAluhumo biAln~aAri waAln~aAru qado ta$ofiY mina AlA^uwaAri [ Their camels had been watered because of the brand that they bore: for fire, or the brand, sometimes cures of the heat of thirst ]; i. e., because of their being branded with the names [or marks] of their owners, they had free access left them to the water. (Mughnee. See also another reading of this verse voce naArN .) [In like manner] it is used in the sense of mino A^ajoli [which means bisababi (Msb in art. Ajl )] in the saying of Lebeed, gulobN ta$a*~ara biAl*~uHuwli kaA^an~ahaA jin~u AlbadiY~i rawaAsiyAF A^aqodaAmuhaA (S) Thick-necked men, like lions, who threatened one another because of rancorous feelings, as though they were the Jinn of the valley El-Bedee, [or of the desert, (TA in art. bdw ,)] their feet standing firm in contention and obstinate altercation. (EM pp. 174 and 175.) It is also used to denote a cause when prefixed to A^an~a and to maA as in *`lika biA^an~ahumo kaAnuwA yakofuruwna biA=yaAti A@ll~`hi [ That was because they used to disbelieve in the signs of God ]; and in *`lika bimaA EaSawoA [ That was because they disobeyed ]: both instances in the Kur ii. 58. (Bd.) ― -b5- It is also used to denote concomitance, as syn. with maEa ; (Mughnee, K;) as in Ai$otarayotu Alfarasa bilijaAmihi wasarojihi [ I bought the horse with his bit and bridle and his saddle ]; (TA;) and in lam~aA raA=niY biAls~alaAHi haraba , i. e. When he saw me advancing with the weapon, [he fled;] or when he saw me possessor of a weapon; (Sh, T;) and in AihobiTo bisalaAmK [ Descend thou with security, or with greeting (Kur xi. 50)]; and in waqado daxaluwA biA@lokufori [ They having entered with unbelief (Kur v. 66)]; (Mughnee, K;) bAlkfr being a denotative of state. (Bd.) Authors differ respecting the b in the saying, fasab~iHo biHamodi rab~ika , in the Kur [xv. 98 and ex. 3]; some saying that it denotes concomitance, and that Hmd is prefixed to the objective complement, so that the meaning is, sab~iHohN HaAmidFA lahu [ Declare thou his (thy Lord's) freedom from everything derogatory from his glory, praising Him ], i. e. declare thou his freedom from that which is not suitable to Him, and ascribe to Him that which is suitable to Him; but others say that it denotes the employing a thing as an aid or instrument, and that Hmd is prefixed to the agent, so that the meaning is, sab~iHohu bimaA Hamida bihi nafosahu [ declare thou his (thy Lord's) freedom from everything derogatory from his glory by means of ascribing to Him that wherewith He hath praised himself ]: and so, too, respecting the saying, suboHaAnaka A@ll~`hum~a wabiHamodika ; some asserting that it is one proposition, the, being redundant; but others saying, it is two propositions, the w being a conjunction, and the verb upon which the b is dependent being suppressed, so that the meaning is, [ I declare thy freedom from everything derogatory from thy glory, 0 God, ] wabiHamodika sab~aHotuka [ and with the praising of Thee, or by means of the praise that belongeth to Thee, I declare thy freedom &c.]. (Mughnee. [Other explanations of these two phrases have been proposed; but those given above are the most approved.]) You also say, EalaY~a bihi , meaning Bring thou him, [i. e.] come with him, to me. (Har p. 109.) DaAqato Ealayohimu A@loA^aroDu bimaA raHubato , in the Kur ix. 119, means biruHobihaA [i. e. The earth became strait to them, with, meaning notwithstanding, its amplitude, or spaciousness ]. (Bd.) Sometimes the negative lA intervenes between bi [denoting concomitance] and the noun governed by it in the gen. case; [so that bilaA signifies Without; ] as in jiy^otu bilaA zaAdK [ I came without travelling-provision ]. (Mughnee and K in art. lA .) ― -b6- It is also syn. with fiY before a noun signifying a place or a time; (Mughnee, * K, * TA;) as in jalasotu biAlmasojidi [ I sat in the mosque ]; (TA;) and walaqado naSarakumu A@ll~`hu bibadorK [ And verily God aided you against your enemies at Bedr (Kur iii. 119)]; and naj~ayonaAhumo bisaHarK [ We saved them a little before daybreak (Kur liv. 34)]: (Mughnee, K, TA:) and so in biA^ay~ikumu A@lomafotuwnu (T, K,) in the Kur [lxviii. 6], (TA,) accord. to some, (T, Mughnee,) i. e. In which of you is madness; or in which of the two parties of you is the mad: (Bd:) or the b is here redundant; (Sb, Bd, Mughnee;) the meaning being which of you is he who is afflicted with madness. (Bd. [See also a later division of this paragraph.]) ― -b7- It also denotes substitution; [meaning Instead of, or in place of; ] as in the saying [of the Hamásee (Mughnee)], falayota liY bihimu qawomFA A_i*aA rakibuwA $an~awA AlA_igaArapa furosaAnFA warukobaAnaA [ Then would that I had, instead of them, a people who, when they mounted their beasts, poured the sudden attack, they being horsemen and camel-riders ]; (Ham p. 8, Mughnee, K;) i. e., badalFA bihimo (TA:) but some read $ad~uwA AlA_igaArapa , [and so it is in some, app., the most correct, of the copies of the Mughnee,] for $ad~uwA liloA_igaAripi [ hastened for the making a sudden attack ]. (Ham, Mughnee.) So, too, in the saying, AiEotaDotu bih`*iA Alv~awobi xayorFA minohu [ I received, in the place of this garment, or piece of cloth, one better than it ]; and laqiytu bizayodK baHorFA [ I found, in the place of Zeyd, a man of abundant generosity or beneficence ]; and h`*aA bi*aAki [ This is instead, or in the place, of that; but see another explanation of this last phrase in what follows]. (The Lubáb, TA.) ― -b8- It also denotes requital; or the giving, or doing, in return; (Mughnee, K;) and in this case is prefixed to the word signifying the substitute, or thing given or done in exchange [or return; or to the word signifying that for which a substitute is given, or for which a thing is given or done in exchange or return]; (Mughnee;) as in the saying, Ai$otarayotuhu biA^alofi dirohamK [ I purchased it for a thousand dirhems ]; (Mughnee, K; *) [and in the saying in the Kur ix. 112, A_in~a A@ll~`ha A@$otarY mina A@lomuw^ominiyna A^anofusahumo waA^amowaAlahumo biA^an~a lahumu A@lojan~apa Verily God hath purchased of the believers their souls and their possessions for the price of their having Paradise; ] and kaAfaA^otu A_iHosaAnahu biDiEofK [ I requited his beneficence with a like beneficence, or with double, or more ], (Mughnee,) or kaAfA^otuhu biDiEofi A_iHosaAnihi [ I requited him with the like, or with double the amount, or with more than double the amount, of his beneficence ], (K,) but the former is preferable; (TA;) [and xadama biTaEaAmi biTonihi (S and A &c. in art. wgd ) He served for, meaning in return for, the food of his belly; ] and h`*aA bi*aAka walaA EatobN EalaY Alz~amani [ This is in return for that, (an explanation somewhat differing from one in the next preceding division of this paragraph,) and no blame is imputable to fortune ]: and hence, AudoxuluwA A@ljan~apa bimaA kunotumo taEomaluwna [ Enter ye Paradise in return for that which ye wrought (Kur xvi. 34)]; for the b here is not that which denotes a cause, as the Moatezileh assert it to be, and as all [of the Sunnees] hold it to be in the saying of the Prophet, lano yadoxula A^aHadukumu Aljan~apa biEamalihi [before cited and explained]; because what is given instead of something is sometimes given gratuitously; and it is evident that there is no mutual opposition between the trad. and the verse of the Kur-án. (Mughnee.) ― -b9- It is also syn. with Eano ; and is said to be peculiar to interrogation; as in faA@soA^alo bihi xabiyrFA [ And ask thou respecting Him, or it, one possessing knowledge (Kur xxv. 60)]; (Mughnee, K;) and accord. to IAar in the Kur lxx. 1; (T;) and in the saying of ' Alkameh, faA_ino tasoA^aluwniY biAln~isaA='i faA_in~aniy baSiyrN biA^adowaA='i Aln~isaA='i xabiyru [ And if ye ask me respecting the diseases of women, verily I am knowing in the diseases of women, skilful ]: (A' Obeyd, TA:) or it is not peculiar to interrogation; as in wayawoma ta$aq~aqu A@ls~amaA='u biA@logamaAmi [ And the day when the heavens shall be rent asunder from the clouds (Kur xxv. 27)]; (Mughnee, K) and maA gar~aka birab~ika (K) i. e. What hath beguiled thee from thy Lord, and from believing in him? in the Kur lxxxii. 6; and so in the same, lvii. 13: (TA: [but see art. gr :]) or, accord. to Z, the b in bAlgmAm means by, as by an instrument; (Mughnee;) or it means because of, or by means of, the rising of the clouds therefrom: (Bd:) and in like manner the Basrees explain it as occurring in faA@soA^alo bihi xabiyrFA , as denoting the cause; and they assert that it is never syn. with Eano ; but their explanation is improbable. (Mughnee.) ― -b10- It is also syn. with EalaYi ; as in A_ino tiA^omanohu biqinoTaArK (Mughnee, K *) or bidiynaArK (S) [ If thou give him charge over a hundredweight or over a deenár (Kur iii. 68)]; like as EalaY is sometimes put in the place of bi as after the verb raDiYa : (S, TA:) and so in lawo tusaw~aY bihimu A@loA^aroDu [ That the ground were made even over them ], in the Kur [iv. 45], (TA,) i. e. that they were buried; (Bd) and in mararotu bizayodK [ I passed by Zeyd ], accord. to Akh, as before mentioned; (Mughnee, in the first division of the art. on this preposition;) and in zayodN biAls~aToHi [ Zeyd is on the roof ]; (TA;) and in a verse cited in this Lex. voce vaEolabN . (Mughnee.) ― -b11- It also denotes part of a whole; (Msb in art. bED Mughnee, K;) so accord. to As and AAF and others; (Msb, Mughnee;) as syn. with mino (Msb, TA:) IKt says; the Arabs say, $aribotu bimaA='i ka*aA , meaning minohu [ I drank of such a water ]; and AZ mentions, as a saying of the Arabs, saqaAka A@ll~`hu mino maA='i ka*aA , meaning bihi [ May God give thee to drink of such a water ], thus making the two prepositions syn.: (Msb: [in which five similar instances are cited from poets; and two of these are cited also in the Mughnee:]) and thus it signifies in EayonFA ya$orabu bihaA EibaAdu A@ll~`hi [ A fountain from which the servants of God shall drink, in the Kur lxxvi. 6; and the like occurs in lxxxiii. 28]; (Msb, Mughnee, K;) accord. to the authorities mentioned above; (Mughnee;) or the meaning is, with which the servants of God shall satisfy their thirst ( yarowaY bihaA ); (T, Mughnee;) or, accord. to Z, with which the servants of God shall drink wine: (Mughnee:) if the b were redundant, [as some assert it to be, (Bd,)] the meaning would be, that they shall drink the whole of it; which is not right: (Msb:) thus, also, it is used in waA@mosaHuwA biruw^u=sikumo [in the Kur v. 8], (Msb, Mughnee, K,) accord. to some; (Mughnee;) i. e. [ And wipe ye] a part of your heads; and this explanation has been given as on the authority of EshSháfi'ee; but he is said to have disapproved it, and to have held that the b here denotes adhesion: (TA:) this latter is its apparent meaning in this and the other instances: or, as some say, in this last instance it is used to denote the employing a thing as an aid or instrument, and there is an ellipsis in the phrase, and an inversion; the meaning being, AimosaHuwA ruw^u=sakumo biAlmaA='i [ wipe ye your heads with water ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b12- It is also used to denote swearing; (Mughnee, K;) and is the primary one of the particles used for this purpose; therefore it is peculiarly distinguished by its being allowable to mention the verb with it, (Mughnee,) as A^uqosimu biA@ll~`hi laA^afoEalan~a [ I swear by God I will assuredly do such a thing]; (Mughnee, K) and by its being prefixed to a pronoun, as in bika laA^afoEalan~a [ By thee I will assuredly do such a thing]; and by its being used in adjuring, or conjuring, for the purpose of inducing one to incline to that which is desired of him, as in bA@ll~`hi halo qaAma zayodN , meaning I adjure thee, or conjure thee, by God, to tell me, did Zeyd stand? (Mughnee.) [See also the first explanation of this particle, where it is said, on the authority of the L, that, when thus used, it denotes adhesion.] ― -b13- It is also syn. with A_ilay as denoting the end of an extent or interval; as in A^aHosana biY , meaning He did good, or acted well, to me: (Mughnee, K:) but some say that the verb here imports the meaning of laTafa [which is trans. by means of b , i. e. he acted graciously, or courteously, with me ]. (Mughnee.) ― -b14- It is also redundant, (S, Mughnee, K,) to denote corroboration: (Mughnee, K:) and is prefixed to the agent: (Mughnee:) first, necessarily; as in A^aHosino bizayodK ; (Mughnee, K;) accord. to general opinion (Mughnee) originally A^aHosana zayodN , i. e. SaAra *aA HusonK [ Zeyd became possessed of goodness, or goodliness, or beauty ]; (Mughnee, K; *) or the correct meaning is Hasuna zayodN [ Good, or goodly, or beautiful, or very good &c., is Zeyd! or how good, or goodly, or beautiful, is Zeyd! ], as in the B: (TA:) secondly, in most instances; and this is in the case of the agent of kafaY ; as in kafaY biA@ll~`hi $ahiydFA [ God sufficeth, being witness, or as a witness (Kur xiii., last verse; &c.)]; (Mughnee, K [and a similar ex. is given in the S, from the Kur xxv. 33;]) the b here denoting emphatic praise; but you may drop it, saying, kafaY A@ll~`hu $ahiydFA : (Fr, TA:) thirdly, in a case of necessity, by poetic licence; as in the saying, A^alamo yaA^otiyka waAlA^anobaA='u tanomiY bimaA laAqato labuwnu baniY ziyaAdi [ Did not what the milch camel of the sons of Ziyád experienced come to thee ( yaA^otiyka being in like manner put for yaA^otika ) when the tidings were increasing? ]. (Mughnee, K.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the objective complement of a verb; as in walaA tuloquwA biA^ayodykumo A_ilaY A@lt~aholukapi [ And cast ye not yourselves ( bA^ydykm meaning biA^anofusikumo ) to perdition (Kur ii. 191)]; and in wahuz~iY A_ilayoki biji*oEi Aln~axolapi [ And shake thou towards thee the trunk of the palm-tree (Kur xix. 25)]: but some say that the former means and cast ye not yourselves ( A^anofusakumo being understood) with your hands to perdition; or that the meaning is, by means, or because, of your hands: (Mughnee:) and ISd says that huz~iY , in the latter, is made trans. by means of b because it is used in the sense of juz~iY : (TA in art hz :) so, too, in the saying, naDoribu biAls~ayofi wa narjuw biAlfarajo [ We smite with the sword, and we hope for the removal of grief ]: (S, Mughnee:) and in the trad., kafay biAlmaro'i ka*ibFA A^ano yuHad~iva bikul~i maA samiEa [ It suffices the man in respect of lying that he relate all that he has heard ]. (Mughnee.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the inchoative; as in biHasobika [when you say, biHasobika dirohamN , meaning A thing sufficing thee is a dirhem; a phrase which may be used in two ways; as predicating of what is sufficient, that it is a dirhem; and as predicating of a dirhem, that it is sufficient; in which latter case, bHsbk is an enunciative put before its inchoative, so that the meaning is, a dirhem is a thing sufficing thee, i. e. a dirhem is sufficient for thee; as is shown in a marginal note in my copy of the Mughnee: in the latter way is used the saying, mentioned in the S, biHasobika qawolu Als~awo'i A thing sufficing thee is the saying what is evil: and so, app., each of the following sayings, mentioned in the TA on the authority of Fr; Hasobuka biSadiyqinaA A person sufficing thee is our friend; and naAhiyka biA^axiynaA A person sufficing thee is our brother: the b is added, as Fr says, to denote emphatic praise]: so too in xarajotu faA_i*iA bizayodK [ I went forth, and lo, there, or then, was Zeyd ]; and in kayofa bika A_i*aA kaAna ka*aA [ How art thou, or how wilt thou be, when it is thus, or when such a thing is the case? ]; and so, accord. to Sb, in biA^y~ikumu A@lomafotuwnu [mentioned before, in explanation of bi as syn. with fiY ]; but Abu-l-Hasan says that bA^y~km is dependent upon AisotiqoraAr suppressed, denoting the predicate of Aalmftwn ; and some say that this is an inf. n. in the sense of finonapN ; [so that the meaning may be, bA^ay~ikumu Almafotuwnu musotaqir~N In which of you is madness residing? ]; or, as some say, bi is here syn. with fiY [as I have before mentioned], (Mughnee.) A strange case is that of its being added before that which is originally an inchoative, namely, the noun, or subject, of layosa , on the condition of its being transferred to the later place which is properly that of the enunciative; as in the reading of some, wujuwhakumo ] layosa A@lbir~a biA^ano tuwal~uwA [ qabala A@loma$oriqi wa A@lomagoribi [ Your turning your faces towards the east and the west is not obedience (Kur ii. 172)]; with Albr~ in the accus. case. (Mughnee.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the enunciative; and this is in two kinds of cases: first, when the phrase is not affirmative; and cases of this kind may be followed as exs.; as layosa zayodN biqaAy^imK [ Zeyd is not standing ]; and wamaA A@ll~`hu bigaAfilK Eam~aA taEomaluwna [ And God is not heedless of that which ye do (Kur ii. 69, &c.)]: secondly, when the phrase is affirmative; and in cases of this kind, one limits himself to what has been heard [from the Arabs]: so say Akh and his followers; and they hold to be an instance of this kind the phrase, jazaA='u say~iy^apK bimivolihaA [ The recompense of an evil action is the like thereof (Kur x. 28)]; and the saying of the Hamásee, wamanoEukahaA bi$aYo'K yusotaTaAEu [ And the preventing thee from having her (referring to a mare) is a thing that is possible ]: but it is more proper to make bmvlhA dependent upon AisotiqoraAr suppressed, as the enunciative; [the meaning being, jazaA='u say~ay^apK musotaqir~N bimivolihaA , or yasotaqir~u bimivolihaA , i. e. the recompense of an evil action is a thing consisting in the like thereof ]; and to make b$Y' dependent upon mnEkhA ; the meaning being, wa manoEukahaA bi$aYo'K m~aA yusotaTaAEu [i. e. and the preventing thee from having her, by something, is possible: see Ham p. 102 ]: Ibn-Málik also [holds, like Akh and his followers, that bi may be redundant when prefixed to the enunciative in an affirmative proposition; for he] says, respecting biHasobika zayodN , that zyd is an inchoative placed after its enunciative, [so that the meaning is, Zeyd is a person sufficing thee, ] because zayodN is determinate and Hasobuka is indeterminate. (Mughnee. [See also what has been said above respecting the phrase biHasobika dirohamN , in treating of bi as added before the inchoative.]) It is also redundantly prefixed to the denotative of state of which the governing word is made negative; as in famaA rajaEato bixaAy^ibapK rikaAbN Hakiymu bonu Almusay~abi munotahaAhaA [ And travelling-camels (meaning their riders) returned not disappointed, whose goal, or ultimate object, was Hakeem the son of El-Museiyab ]; and in famaA A@nobaEavota bimazow^udK wa laA wakali [ And thou didst not, being sent, or roused, go away frightened, nor impotent, committing thine affair to another ]: so says Ibn-Málik: but AHei disagrees with him, explaining these two exs. as elliptical; the meaning implied in the former being, biHaAjapK xaAy^ibapK [ with an object of want disappointed, or frustrated ]; and in the second, bi$axoSK mazow^uwdK , i. e. ma*oEuwrK [ with a person frightened ]; the poet meaning, by the mzw^wd , himself, after the manner of the saying, raA^ayotu minohu A^asadFA ; and this is plain with respect to the former ex., but not with respect to the second; for the negation of attributes of dispraise denoted as intensive in degree does not involve the negation of what is simply essential in those attributes; and one does not say, laqiytu minohu A^asadFA , or baHorFA , [or raA^ayotu minohu A^asadFA , as above, or baHorFA ,] but when meaning to express an intensive degree of boldness, or of generosity. (Mughnee.) It is also redundantly prefixed to the corroborative nafosN and EayonN : and some hold it to be so in yatarab~ana biA^anofusihin~a [as meaning Shall themselves wait (Kur ii. 228 and 234)]: but this presents matter for consideration; because the affixed pronoun in the nom. case, [whether expressed, as in this instance, in which it is the final syllable na , or implied in the verb,] when corroborated by nafos , should properly be corroborated first by the separate [pronoun], as in qumotumo A^anotumo A^anofusukumo [Ye stood, ye, yourselves]; and because the corroboration in this instance is lost, since it cannot be imagined that any others are here meant than those who are commanded to wait: [the preferable rendering is, shall wait to see what may take place with themselves: ] bA^nfshn~ is added only for rousing them the more to wait, by making known that their minds should not be directed towards the men. (Mughnee.) Accord. to some, it is also redundantly prefixed to a noun governed in the gen. case [by another preposition]; as in fA^aSobaHona laA yasoA^alonahu Eano biA^abihi And they became in a condition in which they asked him not respecting his father; which may perhaps be regarded by some as similar to the saying, yaDoHakona Eano kaAlbaradi Almunoham~i but in this instance, ka is generally held to be a noun, syn. with mivol ]. (The Lubáb, TA.) ― -b15- Sometimes it is understood; as in All~`h lAfEln~ [i. e. All~`hi laA^afoEalan~a and All~`ha laA^afoEalan~a By God, I will assuredly do such a thing; in the latter as well as the former, for a noun is often put in the accus. case because of a preposition understood; or, accord. to Bd, in ii. 1, a verb significant of swearing is understood]: and in xayorK [for bixayorK In a good state ], addressed to him who says, kayofa A^aSobaHota [How hast thou entered upon the time of morning? or How hast thou become?]. (TA.) ― -b16- [It occurs also in several elliptical phrases; one of which ( fabihaA wa niEomato ) has been mentioned among the exs. of its primary meaning: some are mentioned in other arts.; as biA^abiY and binafosiY , in arts. Abw and nfs : and there are many others, of which exs. here follow.] Mohammad is related, in a trad., to have said, after hitting a butt with an arrow, A^anaA bhaA A^anaA bhaA , meaning A^anaA SaAHibuhaA [ I am the doer of it! I am the doer of it! ]. (Sh, T.) And in another trad., Mohammad is related to have said to one who told him of a man's having committed an unlawful action, laEal~aka bi*`liki , meaning laEal~aka SaAHibu AlA^amori [ May-be thou art the doer of that thing ]. (T.) And in another, he is related to have said to a woman brought to him for having committed adultery or fornication, mano biki , meaning mano SaAHibuki [ Who was thine accomplice? ]: (T:) or mani AlfaAEilu biki [ Who was the agent with thee? ]. (TA.) A^anaA bika walaka , occurring in a form of prayer, means I seek, or take, refuge in Thee; or by thy right disposal and facilitation I worship; and to Thee, not to any other, I humble myself. (Mgh in art. bwA .) One says also, mano liY bika*aA , meaning Who will be responsible, answerable, amenable, or surety, to me for such a thing? (Har p. 126: and the like is said in p. 191.) And similar to this is the saying, kaA^an~iY bika , meaning kaA^an~iy A^aboSuru bika [It is as though I saw thee ]; i. e. I know from what I witness of thy condition to-day how thy condition will be to-morrow; so that it is as though I saw thee in that condition. (Idem p. 126.) [You also say, kaA^an~aka bihi , meaning Thou art so near to him that it is as though thou sawest him: or it is as though thou wert with him: i. e. thou art almost in his presence.] ― -b17- The Basrees hold that prepositions do not supply the places of other prepositions regularly; but are imagined to do so when they admit of being differently rendered; or it is because a word is sometimes used in the sense of another word, as in $aribona bimaA='i AlbaHori meaning rawiyna , and in A^aHosana biY meaning laTafa ; or else because they do so anomalously. (Mughnee.) -A3- [As a numeral, b denotes Two. ]

definition: , (Lth, T, S, M, &c.
sourceDefinition: , (Lth, T, S, M, &c.,) aor. and , (S, M, Msb,) the latter anomalous, because a reduplicative verb [of this kind] having the aor. with kesr is not trans., except in certain instances, of which this is one; the other instances being Eal~ahu , in relation to drinking, aor. and , and nam~a AlHadiyva , aor. and , and $ad~ahu , aor. and , and Hab~ahu , aor. ; the last having but one form [of aor.]; (S;) inf. n. bat~N : (Lth, T, S, M, A, &c.:) and ↓ Abt~hu , (M,) inf. n. A_ibotaAtN : (Mgh, K:) He cut it off, severed it, separated it, or disunited it, (Lth, T, S, M, A, * Mgh, * Msb, K, *) entirely, or utterly; (Lth, T, M;) namely, a thing; (M;) a rope, or cord; (Lth, T;) and a tie, or bond, of union between two persons. (M.) ― -b2- [ bat~ahu and ↓ Abt~hu , accord. to the TA, app. signify also He, or it, caused him (a man) to become unable to proceed in his journey, his camel that bore him breaking down, or stopping from fatigue, or perishing: for Anbt~ as signifying “he became so” is there said to be quasi-pass. of those two verbs when it has this sense. Hence,] bat~ahu Als~afaru [ The journey caused him to become cut off, &c.]. (A.) And saAqa daAb~atahu Hat~ay bat~ahaA [ He urged on his beast so that, or until, he caused it to become cut off, &c.]: (A:) and baEiyrahu ↓ A^abat~a He caused his camel to become cut off, &c., ( qaTaEapu ,) by travel: (M, TA:) this is not said but of a man who has forced on his camel at a hard pace, or by laborious journeying. (TA.) ― -b3- bat~a TalaAqa A@moraA^atihi , (T, Msb, TA,) or TalaAqa AlmaroA^api , (Mgh,) and ↓ A^abat~ahu , (Lth, T, Mgh, Msb,) He made the divorce of his wife, or of the woman, to be absolutely separating, (Lth, T, Mgh, Msb, TA,) so as to cut her off from return. (Msb.) Lth, with whom AZ agrees, has erred in asserting that bat~a is intrans. and ↓ A^abat~ trans.: (T, TA:) both are trans. and intrans., (T, Msb, TA,) as En-Nawawee asserts in the Tahdheeb el-Asmà wa-1-Loghát. (TA.) You say, AlT~aloqapu AlwaAHidapu tabut~u , and ↓ tubit~u , i. e. The single divorce cuts the matrimonial tie, or bond, of the woman, ( taqoTaEu EiSomapa Aln~ikaAHi , T, Mgh, *) when the period during which she must wait before contracting a new marriage has ended. (T.) [See also bat~N .] ― -b4- bat~a Ealayohi AlqaDaA='a , (T, S, M, A,) inf. n. bat~N ; (M;) and ↓ A^abat~ahu ; (T, S, M;) He (the judge, T) decided the judgment, or sentence, against him. (T, S, * M.) ― -b5- bat~a Ealayohi Al$~ahaAdapa , and ↓ A^abat~ahaA , He decided against him by the testimony, [or pronounced the testimony decisive against him,] and compelled, or constrained, him to admit it. (M.) ― -b6- bat~a $ahaAdatahu , and ↓ A^abat~ahaA , He gave his testimony decisively. (Msb.) ― -b7- A^abut~u A^an~ahu qaAla I know, or declare, decidedly, not [merely] thinking it, that he said thus. (Saheeh of Muslim.) ― -b8- bat~a Aln~iy~apa He made the intention decided; or fixed it decidedly. (A.) It is said in a trad., laA SiyaAma limano AlS~yaAmi mina All~ayoli ↓ lamo yubit~a , (T, S, Mgh,) or lamo yabut~a , accord. to different recitals, (Mgh,) i. e. There is no fasting to him [meaning his fasting is null] who does not decisively impose it upon himself, by intention, from the night: (S, * Mgh:) or, who does not form the intention of fasting before daybreak, and thus cut it off from the time in which there is no fasting, namely, the night: the intention is termed bat~N [and A_ibotaAtN ] because it makes a division between non-fasting and fasting: (T, TA:) lamo yubit , from AlA_ibaAtapu , is a mistake; but lm yubay~it , from Alt~aboyiytu , [see bay~ata ,] is correct. (Mgh.) And it is said in another trad., nikaAHa h`*ihi Aln~isaA='i ↓ A^abit~uwA , i. e. Decide ye the affair respecting the marriage of these women, and confirm it by its [proper] conditions: an oblique prohibition of the kind of marriage termed nikaAHu AlmutoEapi , because it is a marriage not [absolutely or lawfully] decided, [being] made definite as to duration. (TA.) ― -b9- bat~a also signifies He made to have, or take, effect; he executed, or performed; (Har p. 210;) and so ↓ Abt~ , as in the phrase, Abt~ yamiynahu He made his oath to have, or take, effect; he executed, or performed, it. And taSad~aqa ↓ fulaAnN SadaqapF bataAtFA , and SadaqapF bat~apF batolapu , (T, S,) Such a one bestowed an alms, or a gift for the sake of God, cut off from his property; (T, TA;) and therefore, (TA,) parted from himself. [&c.], (TA,) and [pl. of pauc.] A^abut~N . (M.)
