definition: ― -b3- Also A king: (S, A, K:) because he is secluded: (S, A:) or because he prevents those who have access to him.
sourceDefinition: : see maHoSuwrN , in two places: ― -b2- and see HaSirN , in four places. ― -b3- Also A king: (S, A, K:) because he is secluded: (S, A:) or because he prevents those who have access to him. (TA.) -A2- A prison; (S, A, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ HiSaArN . (TA.) So [accord. to some] in the Kur xvii. 8. (S, ISd.) -A3- A mat woven of reeds [or of rushes ] (Msb, K) or of palm-leaves; (IDrd and K voce ta*ar~aEa , &c.;) syn. baAriy~apN ; (Msb, K;) vulgarly ↓ HaSiyrapN : (Msb:) or a thing woven, [ safiyfapN , in the L and TA erroneously written sqyfh ,] made of barodiY~ [or papyrus ] and of A^asal [or rushes ], and then spread upon the ground like a carpet: (TA:) pl. HuSurN (Msb, TA) and, by contraction, HuSorN . (TA.) Hence the prov., A^asiyrN EalaY HaSiyrK [ A captive upon a mat ]. (TA.) And banaAtu AlHaSiyri Bugs; syn. baq~N . (TA in art. bq .) ― -b2- Anything woven. (K.) ― -b3- A garment, or piece of cloth, ornamented and variegated, which, when spread out, captivates hearts in a manner peculiar to it, by its beauty. (K.) So, accord. to some, in the trad. of Hodheyfeh, tuEoraDu Alfitanu EalaY Alquluwbi EaroDa AlHaSiyri [expl. in art. ErD , conj. 1]. (B.) ― -b4- A bed; or a thing spread to lie upon; as though it were a mat: so, accord. to El-Hasan, in the Kur xvii. 8, referred to above. (TA.) ― -b5- A sitting-place; syn. majolisN : (K, and so in two copies of the A:) MF thinks it to be a mistake for maHobisN [ a prison, or place of confinement ]. (TA.) ― -b6- The surface of the ground: (Msb, K:) whence, accord. to some, it is applied to that which is spread upon the ground [i. e. a mat]: (TA:) pl. [of pauc.] A^aHoSirapN and [of mult.] HuSurN . (K.) ― -b7- Water. (K.) [Perhaps because its surface, when rippled by the wind, is likened to a thing woven: see nasaja .] ― -b8- The diversified wavy marks, streaks, or grain, ( firinod ,) of a sword, (K, TA,) resembling the tracks of ants: (TA:) or its HaSiyraAni are its two sides. (K, * TA.) ― -b9- A road, or way. (IAar, K.) ― -b10- A row of men, and of other things. (K.) ― -b11- A certain vein extending across upon the side of a beast, towards the belly: (K:) so, accord. to some, in the trad. of Hodheyfeh mentioned above: (TA:) or a portion of flesh so situate; (K;) i. e., from the shoulder-blade to the flank; as also ↓ HaSiyrapN , explained in the K as a portion of flesh lying across in the side of a horse, which one sees when he is made lean by scanty food: (TA:) or the former signifies the sinew that is between the part called the SifaAq and the part where the false ribs end; (K, TA;) which is the end of the side: (TA:) or the part that is between the vein that appears in the side of the camel and horse, lying across, and what is above it, to the part where the side terminates: (As, S:) or the HSyr of the side is what appears of the upper parts of the ribs. (Ibn-Es-Seed.) ― -b12- Also The side itself. (Az, S, K.) Hence the phrase, daAb~apN EariyDu AlHaSiyrayoni A beast having wide sides. (A, TA.) And A^awojaEa A@ll~`hu HaSiyrayohi [ May God make his sides to ache; meaning] may he be severely beaten. (A, TA.) A certain elegant scholar says, A^av~ara HaSiyru AlHaSiyri fiY HaSiyri AlHaSiyri The mat of the prison made marks upon the side of the king. (MF.)

sourceDefinition: Straitened: [ encompassed, or surrounded: ] besieged, or beset, in a fortress. (TA.) Confined, kept close, imprisoned, detained, retained, restrained, withheld, or prevented; (Akh, S, TA;) as also ↓ HaSiyrN . (Ibn-Es-Seed.) Detained, restrained, withheld, or prevented, from journeying &c.; as also ↓ HaSiyrN and ↓ muHoSarN : (TA:) [or this last signifies made to restrain himself: see 1.] See also HaSirN . ― -b2- Suffering suppression of the feces, or constipation of the bowels: (Ibn-Buzurj, Mgh, K:) [distinguished from maA^osuwrN : (see HuSorN :) or] it also signifies suffering suppression of the urine. (Ibn-Buzurj.) -A2- A camel having upon him [or furnished with ] a HiSaAr . (K.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) aor. , (S, Msb,) inf. n. HafaA='N , (ISk, Zj, IB, Mgh, Msb,) like salaAmN , (Msb,) with fet-h, not HifaA='N , as in the S, (IB,) [for] this latter is a simple subst., (Msb,) He walked barefoot, without sandal and without boot; (ISk, Zj, S, IB, Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ AHtfY : (K:) [but Mtr says,] this latter, occurring in the sense of the former in a trad. of 'Omar, I have not found [elsewhere]. (Mgh.) And HafiYa mino naEolayohi and xuf~ahi , inf. n. HifowapN and HifoyapN and HifaAyapN , [or all these are simple substs., He was, or became, bare of his sandals and his boot. ] (TA.) ― -b2- And HafiYa , inf. n. HafFA , (S, Mgh, Msb, K, &c.,) His foot, i. e. a man's, (S, Msb, K,) and a camel's, (K,) or his solid hoof, (S, Ham p. 476,) or this also, (K,) was, or became, attenuated [ in the sole ], (S, Msb, K,) or chafed, abraded, or worn, (Ham ubi suprà, and PS,) by much walking or treading or travel: (S, Msb, Ham:) or it (the foot of a man [and the hoof of a horse or the like]) became attenuated [&c.] by much walking or treading or travel: (Mgh:) and HafiYa said of a horse, his hoof became abraded, or grazed. (S.) -A2- HafiYa bihi , inf. n. HafaAwapN (S, Mgh, K) and HifaAwapN and HifaAyapN and tiHofaAyapN , (K, TA,) with kesr; (TA; [in the CK taHofaAyap ; both extr.;]) and bh ↓ tHf~Y , (S, K,) and ↓ AHtfY bh ; (K;) He showed him much honour, (S, Mgh, K,) and kindness, or goodness and affection and gentleness, and regard for his circumstances; (S;) regarded him, or behaved towards him, with affection, or benevolence and solicitude; (Mgh;) and manifested joy, or pleasure; (K;) and asked, or inquired, much respecting his state, or condition; (S, K;) and was careful, or solicitous, respecting his case: (S:) or HafiYa Eanohu signifies he asked, or inquired, much respecting him: (Har p. 284:) and ↓ AHfY he exceeded the usual bounds in making much inquiry respecting another, and in carefulness, or solicitude, respecting his case: (Har p. 348:) and ↓ taHaf~K signifies the speaking and meeting in a good, or pleasing, manner; and exceeding the usual bounds in returning a salutation, and in asking, or inquiring: accord. to Zj, HafiYabihi , inf. n. HifowapN , means he acted towards him with kindness, or goodness and affection and gentleness, and regard for his circumstances: accord. to As, HafiYa bihi , aor. , inf. n. HafaAwapN , he employed himself in the accomplishment of that which he needed, or required, and made his abode pleasant: (TA:) and HafaAwapN signifies also the being importunate, pressing, urgent, or persevering, (K, TA,) in asking. (TA.) Hence the prov., maA^orubapN laA HafaAwapN [or maA^orabapN , and maA^orabN , explained in art. Arb ]. (S, K.) ― -b2- Hafiytu A_ilayohi biAlwaSiy~api , or Hafayotu , (accord. to different copies of the S,) I exceeded the usual bounds to him in the injunction, or charge: mentioned by A'Obeyd: (S:) and Alyh ↓ tHf~Y he exceeded the usual bounds to him in the injunction, or charge. (TA.) -A3- HafaA bihi , (K,) and HafaAhu , (TA,) inf. n. HafowN , He (God) honoured him. (K, TA.) ― -b2- And HafaAhu He (a man) gave to him. (K.) ― -b3- And He denied him, or refused him, or refused to give him; (IAar, K;) inf. n. HafowN . (IAar.) Thus it bears two contr. significations. (K.) You say, A^ataAniY faHafawotuhu He came to me and I denied him, &c. (IAar.) And Hafawotuhu mino kul~i xayorK , aor. , inf. n. HafowN , I debarred him from, or prevented him from obtaining, all good. (As, S.) -A4- HafaA $aAribahu : see 4.

definition: He, or it, writhed, or twisted, about, (K, TA,) and turned over and over;
sourceDefinition: He, or it, writhed, or twisted, about, (K, TA,) and turned over and over; (TA;) as also ↓ tHy~z : (K:) or was restless, or unquiet, not remaining still, upon the ground. (Lth, TA.) You say, tHw~zt AlHay~apu , and ↓ tHyz~t , The serpent writhed, or twisted, about. (Both in the S; and the latter in the K in art. Hyz .) And maA laka tataHaw~azu taHaw~uza AlHay~api , and taHay~uza AlHay~api ↓ tataHay~azu , Wherefore dost thou writhe about like the writhing about of the serpent? the latter verb, accord. to Sb, is of the measure tafayoEala , from Huzotu Al$~aYo'a . (S.) ― -b2- He removed, withdrew, or retired to a distance, (A'Obeyd, S, K,) and drew back, (S,) Eanohu [or minohu ] from him or it; (TA;) as also ↓ tHy~z ; (A'Obeyd, S;) and ↓ AnHAz . (A.) You say, daxala Ealayohi famaA taHaw~aza lahu Eano firaA$ihi He went in to him and he did not move for him from his bed, or mattress. (TK.) And El-Katámee says, (S, TA,) describing an old woman of whom he sought hospitality, and who eluded him, (TA,) min~iY xa$oyapF A^ano A^aDiyfahaA ↓ taHay~azu AlA^afoEaY maxaAfapa DaAribi ↓ kamaA A@noHaAzati She (this old woman) retires and draws back from me for fear of my alighting at her abode as a guest [ like as the viper turns away in fear of a beater ]: or, as some relate the verse, taHaw~azu . (S.) ― -b3- He tarried, or loitered: he was slow in rising; as also tHw~s : he desired to rise, and it was tedious to him to do so; as also ↓ tHy~z . (TA.) AA says, taHaw~aza taHaw~uza AlHay~api , [as though meaning, He was slow in rising like as the rising of the serpent is slow: for he adds,] and it is slow in rising when it desires to rise. (S.)

definition: AnHAz Alqawomu The company of men left their appointed station, (S, K, TA,) and place of fighting, (TA,) and turned away to another place.
sourceDefinition: AnHAz Alqawomu The company of men left their appointed station, (S, K, TA,) and place of fighting, (TA,) and turned away to another place. (S, * K, * TA.) You say also, AnHAz Eanohu He turned away from him: (S, K:) and AnHAz A_ilayohi he turned to, or towards, him; and he joined himself to him. (Har pp. 122 and 326.) sourceDefinition: i. q. Hay~izN , as pointed out in two places below. (S, Msb, &c.) ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) A thing that is in one's possession or occupation; a thing that is one's property: so in the saying of a certain woman, waA^aHomiY Hawozapa AlgaAy^ibi (assumed tropical:) And I guard from encroachment the property of the absent: meaning her faroj , which was the property of her husband by the marriage-contract: whence it appears that, if this saying be the only ground upon which Az has asserted that one of the significations of HawozapN is the faroj of a woman, [as is also said in the K,] his assertion requires consideration; for a woman's frj is her own when she has no husband; and when she is married, it is her husband's property. (L, TA.) You say also, SaArafiY Hawozatihi , and ↓ fiY Hawozihi , [and ↓ fY Hay~izihi ,] It became in his possession, or occupation. (L, TA.) And fulaAnN maAniEN Hawozatahu (assumed tropical:) Such a one defends, or guards, from encroachment, or invasion, or attack, what is in his Hay~iz [or place; meaning, in his possession or occupation ]. (TA.) In like manner, a poet says, HamaY HawozaAtihi faturikona qaforFA He guarded from encroachment his tracts of pasture-land [ so that they were left deserted ]. (Fr, TA.) And it is said in a trad., faHamaY HawozapF AlA_isolaAmi (tropical:) And he defended, or protected, or guarded, from encroachment, or invasion, or attack, the limits, [meaning, what the limits comprised, i. e., the territory, ] and the tracts, or regions, of El-Islám [meaning, of the Muslims ]. (TA.) Hawozapu Almuloki signifies [in like manner] bayoDatuhu [i. e. (assumed tropical:) The seat of regal power: or the heart, or principal part, of the kingdom ]. (S, K.) ― -b3- (assumed tropical:) Nature; or natural disposition, temper, or other quality or property; (K, TA;) whether good or evil. (TA.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) of the measure fayoEilN , (Mgh, Msb,) from AlHawozu , (S, * Mgh,) as signifying “ the drawing, collecting, or gathering, together, ” (Mgh,) originally HayowizN , (TA,) and also...
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) of the measure fayoEilN , (Mgh, Msb,) from AlHawozu , (S, * Mgh,) as signifying “ the drawing, collecting, or gathering, together, ” (Mgh,) originally HayowizN , (TA,) and also contracted into HayozN , (S, Msb, TA,) like hay~inN and hayonN , and lay~inN and layonN ; (S, TA;) [The continent, or container, or receptacle, of anything; like bayoDapN ; as also ↓ HawozapN , q. v.:] any place in which a thing is: (Mgh:) in scholastic theology, the imaginary portion of space occupied by a thing having extent, as a body; or by a thing not having extent, as an indivisible atom: in philosophy, the inner surface of a container, which is contiguous [ in every part ] to the outer surface of the thing contained: and [hence,] AlHay~izu AlTabiyEiY~u [ the proper natural place of a thing; ] that in which the nature of a thing requires it to be. (KT.) ― -b2- A quarter, tract, region, or place, considered relatively, or as part of a whole; or a part, or portion, of a place; syn. naAHiyapN ; (S, Mgh, Msb;) as also ↓ HawozapN : (S, Msb, K:) so the authors on practical law mean by Hay~izN ; such, for instance, as a room, or an apartment, of a house: (Mgh:) pl. A^aHoyaAzN , (S, Msb, TA,) which is extr., (TA,) being from the contracted form [ HayozN ]: (Msb:) by rule it should be A^aHowaAzN , (Az, Msb, TA,) like A^amowaAtN , pl. of may~itN [and mayotN ]: (Az, TA:) or by rule [if from the uncontracted form Hay~izN ] it should be HayaAy^izu , with hemz, accord. to Sb; or HayaAwizu , with w , accord. to Abu-l-Hasan. (TA.) Hay~izu Ald~aAri , (S, Msb, TA,) as also Ald~Ari ↓ Hawozu , (TA,) signifies What is annexed to the house, (S, TA,) or appertains thereto, (Msb,) of the maraAfiq (S, Msb, TA) and manaAfiE (TA) and nawaAHK ; (Msb;) [i. e., of the conveniences thereof, such as the privy and the kitchen and the like, and other parts or apartments; ] such are termed collectively A^aHoyaAzu Ald~aAri ; (Msb;) and each part or apartment ( naAHiyap ), by itself, is termed Hay~izN . (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence the saying,] A^anaA fiY Hay~izihi wakanafihi (tropical:) [ I am in his quarter and protection ]. (A, TA.) ― -b4- [And hence also the saying,] fiY Hay~izi Alt~awaAtiru (tropical:) In the manner, and place, of [ that kind of transmission which is termed ] AltwAtr [which is “ transmission by such a number of persons as cannot be supposed to have agreed to a falsehood: ” as explained in the Mz, 3rd nwE ]. (Mgh.) ― -b5- And SaAra fiY Hay~izihi : see HawozapN . ― -b6- [And EalaY Hay~izihi By himself or itself. ]

sourceDefinition: i. q. SihorN , (Lth, Mgh, K, &c.,) as meaning A man married among a people: (Lth, Mgh:) [such a man is said to be that people's xatan :] or any relation on the side of the wife; (S, IAar, Mgh, Msb, K;) such as a man's wife's father, (Lth, IAar, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and wife's mother, (Lth, Mgh,) and wife's brother, (IAar, S, Mgh, Msb, K,) and the like; (K;) so it signifies with the Arabs: (S, Mgh, Msb:) thus Aboo-Bekr was the Prophet's xtn , and so was 'Omar: (Mgh, TA:) and [it is said that] with the vulgar it signifies a man's daughter's husband: (S, Mgh, Msb:) but it is used in this sense by a rájiz; and, in a trad., 'Alee is called the Prophet's xtn : (TA:) accord. to Az, it signifies a man's wife's father: (Msb:) and xatanapN is applied to the female; and means a man's wife's mother: (Az, Mgh, Msb, K, TA:) the pl. is A^axotaAnN : (Az, S, Mgh, Msb, K:) accord. to As, (Mgh,) the A^axotaAn are [the relations ] on the side of the wife; and the A^aHomaA=' , on the side of the husband; and the A^aSohaAr , on either side: (Mgh, Msb:) or a man's AxtAn are his wife's relations; and a woman's AxtAn are her husband's relations: and a man's AxtAn are also said to be his daughters' husbands and sisters' husbands and paternal aunts' husbands and maternal aunts' husbands, and the husbands of any women whom, by reason of relationship, it is unlawful for him to marry, and any relations on the side of these husbands to whom marriage is unlawful, of men and of women. (Mgh.)

definition: Circumcision, of a boy, (S, * Mgh, * Msb, * K, TA,) and of a girl;
sourceDefinition: Circumcision, of a boy, (S, * Mgh, * Msb, * K, TA,) and of a girl; (TA;) a subst. from 1 in the first of the senses explained above; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ xitaAnapN . (S, Msb, K.) You say, ↓ A^uToHirato xitaAnatuhu His circumcision was made to be extirpative. (S, TA.) ― -b2- And A feast, or banquet, to which people are invited on account of a circumcision. (JK, S, TA.) You say, kunotu fiY xitaAni fulaAnK I was at the feast, or banquet, &c., of such a one. (TA.) ― -b3- See also 1, third sentence. ― -b4- Also The part, of the male, which is the place of circumcision; (T, S, Mgh, K;) and of the female likewise; (T, Mgh, TA;) the part, of the faroj , which is the place of circumcision. definition: The perforation, bore, or hole, (S, A, K,) of a needle;
sourceDefinition: The perforation, bore, or hole, (S, A, K,) of a needle; [i. e. its eye; ] (S, A; [see also xurotapN ;] and of the ear, (S,) or in the ear, [but see xurotapN ,] &c.; (A, K;) and of the faA^os , [i. e. hoe, or adz, or axe,] (S, A, TA,) meaning, of the handle thereof; (A, TA;) as also xurapN ; (Fr, TA in art. xrw ;) [see again xurotapN ;] and ↓ xarotN signifies the same: (A, K:) pl. [of pauc.] A^axoraAtN (S, A) and [of mult.] xuruwtN . (S.) You say A^aDoyaqu mino xuroti AlA_iborapi [ Narrower than the eye of the needle ]. (A.) And maDaAyiqu kaA^axoraAti AlA_ibari [ Narrow passes like the eyes of needles ]. (A.) The xurot of a sandal is The hole, or perforation, of the *uw^aAbap [q. v.], into which the thong [ called the $iraAk ] enters. (An anon. Arabic MS. in my possession.) ― -b2- Also The rings at the heads [or extremities ] of [ camels' plaited fore-girths of the kind called ] nusuwE ; and so [the pls.] xuratN (K) and A^axoraAtN : (S, K:) and ↓ xurotapN signifies one of these; (K;) i. e. the ring in which is [ inserted the end of ] the nisoEap . (TA.) [Hence the phrase,] qaliqa xurotu fulaAnK [lit. The rings of the fore-girths of the camels of such a one became unsteady; meaning] (tropical:) the state of such a one became disordered, or perverted. (A, TA.) And similar to this are the phrases, raAda xurotu Alqawomi and raAdato A^axoraAtuhumo , [in the TA zAd and zAdt , but the comparison evidently shows that the verbs should be rAd and rAdt ,] said of a people when they do not receive or entertain hospitably him who alights at their place of abode: so says IAar on the authority of Es-Saloolee. (TA.) ― -b3- See also xurotapN . ― -b4- Also A small rib, at, or near, the breast; and so ↓ xarotN : (K:) pl. A^axoraAtN , which Lth explains as meaning the ribs at, or near, the breast, collectively. (TA.) ― -b5- And [the pl.] A^axoraAtN signifies The obscure roads or ways, and the narrow passes, of a desert. (TA.)

(TA in art. Hrt .)

definition: Two stars, (K,) of the stars of the Lion, two whips' lengths apart, [(see sawoTN ,) in ] the two shoulder-blades of the Lion, (TA,) also called zuborapu AlA^asadi , (K,) [ composing the Eleventh...
sourceDefinition: Two stars, (K,) of the stars of the Lion, two whips' lengths apart, [(see sawoTN ,) in ] the two shoulder-blades of the Lion, (TA,) also called zuborapu AlA^asadi , (K,) [ composing the Eleventh Mansion of the Moon: (see zuborapN : and see also manaAzilu Alqamari , in art. nzl :)] the word is mentioned here in the K, as though it were of the measure faEaAlaAni ; but accord. to Kr and others, it is dual of xaraApN , belonging to art. xrw , in which it is again mentioned in the K: (TA:) accord. to ISd, however, only the dual form is known, and the radical t and the augmentative t [by which latter is meant p ] are in the dual alike: (TA in art. xrw :) Zj asked Th respecting the xrAtAn , and he answered, IAar says that they are two stars, of those of the Lion; and Aboo-Nasr, the companion of As, says that they are two stars in the zbrp of the Lion, i. e. in the middle thereof; but in my opinion they are two stars after [i. e. to the eastward of ] the jabohap and the qalob : Zj disapproved of this, and replied, I say that they are two stars in that part of the breast which is the stabbing-place, derived from xurotu AlA_iborapi , “ the eye of the needle: ” but Th rejoined, that this was an error, because the word is the dual of xaraApN ; and he cited some verses in which a poet speaks of certain stars in the Lion, and, among them, of AlxaraApu . (MF, TA.)

definition: The wooden thing that is inserted in the bone of the nose of the camel, (S, A, K,) to which the nose-rein is tied, in order that he may be quickly submissive: (TA:) the burap is of brass, (S, TA,) or of silver;
sourceDefinition: The wooden thing that is inserted in the bone of the nose of the camel, (S, A, K,) to which the nose-rein is tied, in order that he may be quickly submissive: (TA:) the burap is of brass, (S, TA,) or of silver; (TA;) and the xizaAmap is of hair: (S:) or the thing that is put in the nose; and the brp is the thing that is put in the flesh: (Lh:) or what is in the bone, when it is wood, or a stick; and the EiraAn is what is in the flesh, above the nose: (As:) a wooden thing, or stick, that is put in the bone of the nose of the camel: (Msb:) n. un. with p : (S, Msb:) pl. A^axi$~apN . (A, Msb.) [Hence the saying,] jaEala Alxi$aA$a fiY A^anofihi waqaAdahu A_ilaY AlT~aAEapi biEunofihi (tropical:) [ He put the x$A$ in his nose, and drew him to obedience by his violence ]. (A, TA.) [And hence, also,] it signifies gaDabN , (IAar, K,) as used in the saying, Har~aka xi$aA$ahu , [lit., He put in motion his xi$aA$ : meaning, (assumed tropical:) he roused, or excited, his anger; or] he made him angry. (IAar.) -A2- Alxi$aA$u , and ↓ Alxa$aA$u , (S, K,) the latter form being sometimes used, (S,) which indicates that the former is the more chaste, but, accord. to MF, several authorities say the contrary, (TA,) and ↓ Alxu$aA$u , (K,) or AlA^aroDi ↓ xa$aA$u , (A 'Obeyd, Msb,) and xi$aA$u AlA^aroDi , (Msb,) The creeping things of the earth: n. un. with p , which is syn. with AlHa$arapu and AlhaAm~apu : (Msb:) the Ha$araAt (A' Obeyd, S, K) of the earth, (A' Obeyd, K,) and its hawaAm~ , and [ other ] creeping things, (A 'Obeyd,) such as sparrows and the like: (A 'Obeyd, K: *) or xi$aA$u AlA^aroDi , and AlT~ayori , signify the small ones of beasts or creeping things [ of the earth ], and of birds: (A:) IAar is related to have said that it is ↓ xi$oxaA$N , contr. to what is said by the lexicologists in general: and these things are said to have their appellation from their entering into the earth and concealing themselves; but this assertion is not valid: (ISd:) in a trad., for mn x$A$ AlArD , one relation substitutes ↓ mino xa$iy$ihaA , which has the same meaning: and some say that it is ↓ xu$ayo$ , a contracted dim. of x$A$ ; or ↓ xu$ay~i$ , without contraction: (TA:) and ↓ Alxa$aA$u signifies the bad [meaning ignoble ] kinds of birds; this being with fet-h only: (As:) or birds that do not prey: (IAar, TA voce EuqaAbN :) xi$aA$N , with kesr, also signifies the serpent of the mountain; which does not suffer one to survive; and the A^afoEaY is the serpent of the plain; (El-Fak'asee, K;) which like wise does not suffer one to survive: (K:) or a great and abominable vuEobaAn : or a serpent like the A^aroqam , but smaller: or a small, tawny serpent, smaller than the Arqm : (TA:) or a white serpent, which seldom hurts, between the Huf~aAv and the Arqm : (Aboo-Kheyreh:) or such as is light, or active, and small in the head, of serpents: explained also as signifying the serpent, without restriction: (TA:) and, (K,) or as some say, (TA,) such as has no power of defence, [ maA laA difaAEa lahu , as in the CK and a MS copy of the K, for which we find in some copies of the K, and in the TA, mA lA dimaAga lahu such as has no brains, which is doubtless a mistake,] of beasts or creeping things of the earth, and of birds, (K,) such as the ostrich, and the [ bustard called ] HubaAraY , and the karawaAn [ or stonecurlew ], and [ the bird called ] mulaAEibu Zil~ihi , and the [ harmless kinds of ] serpent: (TA:) or what is small in the head, and slender, of beasts or creeping things: and the kite; and [the bird called ] mulaAEibu Zil~ihi : (Aboo-Muslim:) the pl. is x$~A=' [app. xu$~aA='u , originally xu$a$aA='u , unless a mistake for A^axi$~aA='u , originally A^axo$i$aA='u ]. (TA.)

(TA.) [See also A^afoyuwnN .]

definition: , aor. , inf. n. xalofN , He came after, followed, succeeded, or remained after, another, or another that had perished or died. (TA.) Hence, in the Kur [vii. 168 and xix. 60], faxalafa mino...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. xalofN , He came after, followed, succeeded, or remained after, another, or another that had perished or died. (TA.) Hence, in the Kur [vii. 168 and xix. 60], faxalafa mino baEodihimo xalofN (TA) And there hath succeeded them, or come after them, [ a posterity, or] an evil posterity. (Bd in xix. 60.) And xalafahu He came after him, (S, A in art. dbr , Mgh, Msb, TA,) or behind him, (A ubi suprà, Mgh,) or following him nearly; (A ubi suprà;) inf. n. as above, (Mgh, TA,) and xilofapN also: (Mgh:) or he remained after him: (K:) and ↓ jaA='a xilaAfahu likewise signifies [the same as jA=' xalofahu ; an inf. n. of xaAlafa being thus used as an adv. n.; i. e.] he came after him. (TA.) You say also, xalafa All~ayolu Aln~ahaAra , inf. n. xalofN and xilofapN , The night followed, or came after, the day. (MA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xalafotuhu , [aor. as above,] inf. n. xalofN , [perhaps a mistranscription for xalafa ,] I was, after him, a substitute for him: (TA:) [ I supplied his place: and I superseded him. ] And xalafahu , (aor. as above, TA,) inf. n. xilaAfapN (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) and xalafN (TA) and xil~iyqaY , (S, * K, * TA,) which last is an inf. n. of the intensive kind, (Sgh, MF, TA,) He was, or became, his xaliyfap [i. e. successor, or vice-agent, &c.], (S, Mgh, Msb, K,) or his substitute; (TA;) fiY qawomihi [ among, or in respect of, his people ], (S, TA,) and A^aholihi [ his family ]; relating to good and to evil; wherefore one says, A^awoSaY lahu biAlxilaAfapi [ he charged him by his will with the being his successor, or vice-agent, &c.]; (TA;) or EalaY A^aholihi wamaAlihi [ over his family and his property ]: (Msb:) and ↓ Axtflhu signifies the same; (Lh, Ibn-'Abbád, K;) he was, or became, his xaliyfap (Ibn-'Abbád, TA) after him. (Ibn-'Abbád, TA.) And xalafa fulaAnFA [alone] He was, or became, the xaliyfapN of such a one among, or in respect of, his family (K, TA) and his children. (TA.) And xalafahu rab~uhu fiY A^aholihi (K, TA) and waladihi , (TA,) inf. n. xilaAfapN , (K,) His Lord was [for him] a xaliyfap [or supplier of his place] to his family (K, TA) and his children. (TA. [In the CK, Axlf is made to signify the same; but this is in consequence of an omission.]) And one says, xalafa A@ll~`hu Ealayoka May God be to to thee a xaliyfap [or supplier of the place ] (S, Msb, K) of thy father; (S, Msb,) or of the one whom thou hast lost: (S, Msb, K:) thus one says to one who has lost by death his father (S, Msb, K) or mother (K) or paternal uncle (S, Msb) or any other who cannot be replaced: (Msb, K:) and xalafa A@ll~`hu Ealayoka xayorFA , (K,) or bixayorK , (AZ, Msb, K,) or both, (L,) and xalafa A@ll~`hu laka bixayorK , (AZ, Msb,) and A@ll~`hu Ealayoka xayorFA ↓ A^axolafa and laka xayorFA : (K: [in which it is implied that these phrases mean May God supply to thee well the place of him whom thou hast lost: but it is implied in the Msb that the two of them there mentioned mean May God restore to thee good in the place of that which has gone from thee: and it appears from what here follows that all of these phrases have the latter meaning, whether or not they have the former meaning also:]) to him who has lost property or a child or a thing [of any other kind] of which the replacement may be asked, (S,) or to him of whom that which may be replaced has perished, or died, (K,) one says, A@ll~`hu Ealayoka ↓ A^axolafa (S, Msb, K) May God restore to thee the like of that which has gone from thee, (S, Msb,) or may God restore to thee what has gone from thee; (K in a later part of the art.;) and All~`h laka ↓ Axlf ; and xalafa All~`h lk : or xalafa All~`h Ealayoka is allowable in relation to property and the like; and yaxolafu , like yamonaEu is allowable as its aor., though extr., (K,) as it has no faucial letter to occasion the fet-h: (TA:) and one says also, xalafa A@ll~`hu laka bixayorK meaning May God give thee good in the place of that which has gone from thee; (TA;) and Ealayoka xayorFA ↓ Axlf , (Msb, TA,) meaning the same; (TA;) and [so] laka xayorFA ↓ Axlf and bixayorK : and A@ll~`hu Ealayoka maAlaka ↓ Axlf and laka maAlaka [ May God restore, or replace, to thee thy property ]. (Msb.) xalafa A^abaAhu , (K,) aor. (TA,) means He became behind his father; (K;) and if so, its inf. n. is xalofN : (TA:) or it means he became in the place of his father; (K;) and if so, its inf. n. is xalafN : (TA:) and xalafa makaAna A^abiyhi , inf. n. xilaAfapN (K) and xalafN , (TA,) he became in the place of his father, exclusively of every other. (K.) You say also, xalafati AlfaAkihapi baEoDuhaA baEoDFA , (JK, K,) inf. n. xalofN , (JK, TA,) or xalafN , (TA, [the former being there altered to the latter (which is the more probably correct), or the latter to the former,]) and xilofapN , (JK, TA,) The fruit replaced other fruit; or became substituted for other fruit. (JK, * K,* TA. [In the CK, SaAra xalofFA is erroneously put for SaArato xalafFA .]) And xalafa fulaAnN EalaY fulaAnapa , inf. n. xilaAfapN , [like Eaqaba EalayohaA ,] Such a man took as his wife such a woman after another husband [and thus supplied his place]. (Z, TA.) ― -b3- xalafa ulaAnFA , (aor. , TA,) He took, or seized, such a one from behind him; (JK, * K;) as also ↓ Axtlfhu . (TA.) And hence, (TA,) xalafa lahu biAls~ayofi (JK, TA) He came to him from behind him, and smote his neck, or struck off his head, with the sword. (TA.) ― -b4- xalafa fulaAnN biEaqibiY [is explained as meaning] Such a one stayed, or abode, after me. (Msb in art. Eqb ) [But] ― -b5- xalafa biEaqabi fulaAnK is said by some to mean A_ilaY ↓ xaAlafahu A^aholihi [q. v.]: accord. to As, however, it means He parted with such a one on the condition of doing a certain thing, and then came behind him [or behind his back ] and did another thing after parting with him: and Az says that this is a more correct explanation than the former one. (TA.) [Hence, app.,] one says also, A_in~a A@moraA^apa fulaAnK taxolufu zawojahaA biAln~izaAEi A_ilaY gayorihi A_i*aA gaAba EanohaA [ Verily the wife of such a one is unfaithful to her husband by yearning towards another when he is absent from her: or deceives her husband behind his back by yearning towards another; for it is implied, by an ex. given, that A*A gAb EnhA is added by way of explanation]. (TA.) xalafahu also signifies He spoke of him, or mentioned him, [ behind his back, or] when he was not present: so in the phrase, xalafahu bixayorK or bi$ar~K [ He spoke of him behind his back well or ill ]. (TA.) And one says, yaxolufu Aln~aAsa mino waraAy^ihimo [meaning He defames men behind their backs ]: the action signified hereby is like giybapN , and may be [ by making signs ] with the side of the mouth, and with the eye, and with the head. (TA in art. hmz .) ― -b6- xalafa Eano A^aSoHaAbihi , (K, TA,) aor. , He remained behind, or after, his companions; did not go forth with them; as also A^aSoHaAbihi ↓ qaEada xilaAfa [similar to a phrase mentioned near the beginning of this art.]; (TA;) i. q. ↓ txl~f ; (K in explanation of the former phrase;) which is syn. with taA^ax~ara ; (S, K;) as in the phrase txl~f Ean~iY [which means He remained behind me, or after me ]; (S;) [for] txl~f Eanohu means baqiYa xalofahu ; (Mgh;) and [in like manner] you say, txl~f Eani lAqawomi He remained behind, or after, the people, or party, not going with them; [ he held back, or hung back, from them; ] and ↓ qaEadotu xilaAfahu [i. e. I remained ] behind him, or after him; (Msb;) and ↓ xAlf Ean~aA He remained behind us, or after us; syn. ↓ txl~f . (TA, from a trad.) It is said in the Kur [xvii. 78], A_il~aA qaliylFA ↓ wa A_i*aA laA yalobavuwna xilaAfaka , i. e. [ But in that case they should not have remained ] after thee [ save a little while ]: (JK, TA: *) so accord. to one reading [instead of xalofaka , which means the same]. (TA.) And in like manner, rasuwli A@ll~`hi ↓ fariHa Almuxal~afuwna bimaqoEadihimo xilaAfa , in the Kur [ix. 82], means [ Those who were left behind rejoiced in their remaining ] behind the Apostle of God: (S, TA:) or the meaning here is, muxaAlafapa rswl All~`h [i. e. in disagreement with the Apostle of God ]: (JK, S:) thus says Lh; but IB disagrees with him; saying that xlAf here means baEoda ; and cites six exs. in which it has this meaning, from poets. (TA.) ― -b7- [Hence,] xalafa fulaAnN Eano kul~i xayorK (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one was, or became, kept back from all good; i. e., ] did not prosper, or was not successful. (TA. [It is there added, that it is explained in the A as tropical, and as meaning tagay~ara wafasada : but this is perhaps a mistake, occasioned by the accidental omission of waxalafa All~abanu or the like, of which this is a correct explanation: or the phrase thus explained in the TA, as from the A, may correctly mean He became altered for the worse, and corrupt; agreeably with other explanations of the verb below.]) ― -b8- xalafa , aor. , also signifies He (a man) retired, withdrew, or went away or apart. (JK.) And xalafato nafosahu Eani AlT~aEaAmi , aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (assumed tropical:) His soul turned away from, avoided, or shunned, the food, in consequence of disease. (JK, TA.) ― -b9- And He fled. (Ham p. 411.) ― -b10- And He (a man, Sgh) ascended a mountain. (Sgh, K.) -A2- See also 2, first sentence. -A3- xalafa , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. xuluwfN , (Lh, Msb, TA, and Ham p. 679,) [inf. n. xuluwfN ,] said of the taste of water, It was, or became, different from, or contrary to, what it was thought to be: and [hence,] it was, or became, altered [ for the worse ]: (Ham ubi suprà:) [and] said of milk, (S, K,) and of food, (Lh, S, Msb, K,) and the like, (Lh, TA,) and some say xalufa , (TA,) aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (Lh, TA,) of both verbs, (TA,) it was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] (Lh, S, Msb, K) in taste, or in odour; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Axlf : or, said of milk, the first signifies it became bad from being long kept; or, as in the A, (tropical:) what was good thereof became mixed ( xulifa , i. e. xuliTa ,) with other milk: and ↓ Axlf , said of milk, signifies also it was, or became, sour: (TA:) and the first, said of [the beverage called] nabiy* , it became bad. (K.) Also, inf. n. xuluwfN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and xuluwfapN (K) and xilofapN , (L, TA,) said of the mouth (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a person fasting, (S, Msb, K,) It was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] in odour; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Axlf . (S, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad. that the xuluwf of the mouth of one who is fasting is sweeter in the estimation of God than the odour of musk: or, accord. to some of the lawyers and of the relaters of traditions, xaluwf ; but [SM says,] I think this to be a mistake, as several affirm it to be, while others say that it is of a bad dial. : accord. to one reading, it is xilofap . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xalafa Eano xuluqi A^abiyhi , (K,) aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] from the natural disposition of his father. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And xalafa , (ISk, S, K,) inf. n. xalofN [or xuluwfN ]; or xalofa , aor. , inf. n. xalaAfapN and xuluwfN ; (TA;) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, bad, or corrupt. (ISk, S, K, TA.) ― -b4- And xalafa , (K) inf. n. xalaAfapN (IAth, K) and xuluwfN , (K,) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, stupid, or foolish; or one who had little, or no, intellect or understanding: (K, * TA:) or unprofitable: or a frequent promise-breaker: (IAth:) or xalafa and ↓ Axlf , said of a slave, he was, or became, idiotic, deficient in intellect, or bereft of his intellect. (JK.) -A4- xalafa , (K,) inf. n. xalofN ; (S, * K, * TA;) and ↓ Axlf , and ↓ Astxlf ; (S, K;) He drew water, (S, K, TA,) liA^aholihi for his family: [app. because he who does so leaves his family behind him: see 2, first sentence:] (K, TA:) [or] ↓ Astxlf , said of a man, signifies AisotaEo*aba AlmaA=' [app. as meaning he sought, or drew, or brought, sweet water: see art. E*b ]: and, accord. to IAar, you say, Alqawoma ↓ A^axolafotu , meaning properly I carried sweet water to the people, or party, when they were in the [ season, or herbage, called ] rabiyE and without sweet water, or when they were by salt water: A_ixolaAfN [as meaning the carrying, or drawing, of water ,] being [properly] only in the rbyE : in other cases, metaphorically applied. (TA.) El-Hoteíäh says, ↓ lizugobK kaA^awolaAdi AlqaTaA raAva xalofuhaA EalaY EaAjizaAti Aln~ahoDi HumorK HawaASiluho (assumed tropical:) [ To, or for, downy ones, like the young ones of the katà, whose procurer of water has been slow in coming to those lacking the power of spreading their wings for flight, red in their crops ]: he means ↓ mixolifuhaA [or xaAlifuhaA ], and has put in the place of this the inf. n.: and by HwASlh , accord. to Ks, he means HawaASilu maA *akoronaA [ the crops of what we have mentioned ]: but Fr says that the h relates to the zgb , exclusively of the EAjzAt , which [latter] has the sign of the pl. ; for every pl. that has the form of a sing. may be imagined to be a sing., as in the saying of the poet, mivolu AlfiraAxi nutifato HawaASiluho [meaning “ like the young birds of which the crops have been plucked ”]; for AlfrAx has not the sign of the pl., but has the form of a sing., like AlkitaAb and AlHijaAb : another says, [but this is very far-fetched,] that the h relates to AlnhD , which [sometimes] means a place in the shoulderblade of the camel; and that the poet has used it metaphorically as belonging to the qTA . (S.) -A5- xalafa Alv~awoba , (S,) or AlqamiySa , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xalofN (Kr, TA) and xulofapN , in some copies of the K xalofapN , [so in my MS. copy of the K, and so in the TK,] and [in some] xulafN also, but these require consideration, (TA,) He took out from the garment, or shirt, the part that was worn out, (S, Msb, K,) that is, the middle part, which was worn out, (S, Msb,) and then sewed the [ cut ] edges together. (S, Msb, K.) And Alv~awoba ↓ Axlf signifies the same as xalafahu , i. e. He repaired the garment [app. in any manner, or, as is implied in the S and TA, by substituting one piece for another ]. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- The saying, in a trad. of Hamneh, faA_i*aA xalafato *`lika falotagotasilo , meaning (assumed tropical:) And when she has discriminated that period of days and nights during which she has been HaAy^iD , [ she shall perform a complete ablution of herself, ] is from xalafa AlqamiyS signifying as explained above. (Msb.) -A6- xalafa signifies also He mixed [a thing with another thing; as, for instance, (see xulifa in a passage above,) milk with other milk]: and he mixed saffron, and medicine, with water. (TA.) -A7- xalafa bayotahu He put to, or made for, his tent, a pole, (K, TA,) termed a xaAlifap , (TA,) in the hinder part thereof. (K TA.) -A8- xalifa , aor. , (K,) inf. n. xalafN , (S, K,) He (a camel) inclined towards one side. (S, K.) ― -b2- xalafN is also an inf. n. (of xalifa , said of a man, TK) signifying The being A^axolaf as meaning contrarious, hard in disposition, as though going with a leaning towards one side: ― -b3- and the being left-handed: ― -b4- and the being A^aHowal [or squint-eyed ]. (K.) -A9- xalifato , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xalafN , (Msb, TA,) She (a camel) was, or became, pregnant. (Msb, K.)

And in like manner, rasuwli A@ll~`hi ↓ fariHa Almuxal~afuwna bimaqoEadihimo xilaAfa , in the Kur [ix. 82], means [ Those who were left behind rejoiced in their remaining ] behind the Apostle of God: (S, TA:) or the meaning here is, muxaAlafapa rswl All~`h [i. e. in disagreement with the Apostle of God ]: (JK, S:) thus says Lh; but IB disagrees with him; saying that xlAf here means baEoda ; and cites six exs. in which it has this meaning, from poets. (TA.) ― -b7- [Hence,] xalafa fulaAnN Eano kul~i xayorK (assumed tropical:) [ Such a one was, or became, kept back from all good; i. e., ] did not prosper, or was not successful. (TA. [It is there added, that it is explained in the A as tropical, and as meaning tagay~ara wafasada : but this is perhaps a mistake, occasioned by the accidental omission of waxalafa All~abanu or the like, of which this is a correct explanation: or the phrase thus explained in the TA, as from the A, may correctly mean He became altered for the worse, and corrupt; agreeably with other explanations of the verb below.]) ― -b8- xalafa , aor. , also signifies He (a man) retired, withdrew, or went away or apart. (JK.) And xalafato nafosahu Eani AlT~aEaAmi , aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (assumed tropical:) His soul turned away from, avoided, or shunned, the food, in consequence of disease. (JK, TA.) ― -b9- And He fled. (Ham p. 411.) ― -b10- And He (a man, Sgh) ascended a mountain. (Sgh, K.) -A2- See also 2, first sentence. -A3- xalafa , (S, Msb, K, &c.,) aor. xuluwfN , (Lh, Msb, TA, and Ham p. 679,) [inf. n. xuluwfN ,] said of the taste of water, It was, or became, different from, or contrary to, what it was thought to be: and [hence,] it was, or became, altered [ for the worse ]: (Ham ubi suprà:) [and] said of milk, (S, K,) and of food, (Lh, S, Msb, K,) and the like, (Lh, TA,) and some say xalufa , (TA,) aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (Lh, TA,) of both verbs, (TA,) it was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] (Lh, S, Msb, K) in taste, or in odour; (S, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Axlf : or, said of milk, the first signifies it became bad from being long kept; or, as in the A, (tropical:) what was good thereof became mixed ( xulifa , i. e. xuliTa ,) with other milk: and ↓ Axlf , said of milk, signifies also it was, or became, sour: (TA:) and the first, said of [the beverage called] nabiy* , it became bad. (K.) Also, inf. n. xuluwfN (S, Mgh, Msb, K) and xuluwfapN (K) and xilofapN , (L, TA,) said of the mouth (S, Mgh, Msb, K) of a person fasting, (S, Msb, K,) It was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] in odour; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) as also ↓ Axlf . (S, Msb, K.) It is said in a trad. that the xuluwf of the mouth of one who is fasting is sweeter in the estimation of God than the odour of musk: or, accord. to some of the lawyers and of the relaters of traditions, xaluwf ; but [SM says,] I think this to be a mistake, as several affirm it to be, while others say that it is of a bad dial. : accord. to one reading, it is xilofap . (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xalafa Eano xuluqi A^abiyhi , (K,) aor. , inf. n. xuluwfN , (TA,) (assumed tropical:) He was, or became, altered [ for the worse ] from the natural disposition of his father. (K, TA.) ― -b3- And xalafa , (ISk, S, K,) inf. n. xalofN [or xuluwfN ]; or xalofa , aor. , inf. n. xalaAfapN and xuluwfN ; (TA;) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, bad, or corrupt. (ISk, S, K, TA.) ― -b4- And xalafa , (K) inf. n. xalaAfapN (IAth, K) and xuluwfN , (K,) (assumed tropical:) He (a man) was, or became, stupid, or foolish; or one who had little, or no, intellect or understanding: (K, * TA:) or unprofitable: or a frequent promise-breaker: (IAth:) or xalafa and ↓ Axlf , said of a slave, he was, or became, idiotic, deficient in intellect, or bereft of his intellect. (JK.) -A4- xalafa , (K,) inf. n. xalofN ; (S, * K, * TA;) and ↓ Axlf , and ↓ Astxlf ; (S, K;) He drew water, (S, K, TA,) liA^aholihi for his family: [app. because he who does so leaves his family behind him: see 2, first sentence:] (K, TA:) [or] ↓ Astxlf , said of a man, signifies AisotaEo*aba AlmaA=' [app. as meaning he sought, or drew, or brought, sweet water: see art. E*b ]: and, accord. to IAar, you say, Alqawoma ↓ A^axolafotu , meaning properly I carried sweet water to the people, or party, when they were in the [ season, or herbage, called ] rabiyE and without sweet water, or when they were by salt water: A_ixolaAfN [as meaning the carrying, or drawing, of water ,] being [properly] only in the rbyE : in other cases, metaphorically applied. (TA.) El-Hoteíäh says, ↓ lizugobK kaA^awolaAdi AlqaTaA raAva xalofuhaA EalaY EaAjizaAti Aln~ahoDi HumorK HawaASiluho (assumed tropical:) [ To, or for, downy ones, like the young ones of the katà, whose procurer of water has been slow in coming to those lacking the power of spreading their wings for flight, red in their crops ]: he means ↓ mixolifuhaA [or xaAlifuhaA ], and has put in the place of this the inf. n.: and by HwASlh , accord. to Ks, he means HawaASilu maA *akoronaA [ the crops of what we have mentioned ]: but Fr says that the h relates to the zgb , exclusively of the EAjzAt , which [latter] has the sign of the pl. ; for every pl. that has the form of a sing. may be imagined to be a sing., as in the saying of the poet, mivolu AlfiraAxi nutifato HawaASiluho [meaning “ like the young birds of which the crops have been plucked ”]; for AlfrAx has not the sign of the pl., but has the form of a sing., like AlkitaAb and AlHijaAb : another says, [but this is very far-fetched,] that the h relates to AlnhD , which [sometimes] means a place in the shoulderblade of the camel; and that the poet has used it metaphorically as belonging to the qTA . (S.) -A5- xalafa Alv~awoba , (S,) or AlqamiySa , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xalofN (Kr, TA) and xulofapN , in some copies of the K xalofapN , [so in my MS. copy of the K, and so in the TK,] and [in some] xulafN also, but these require consideration, (TA,) He took out from the garment, or shirt, the part that was worn out, (S, Msb, K,) that is, the middle part, which was worn out, (S, Msb,) and then sewed the [ cut ] edges together. (S, Msb, K.) And Alv~awoba ↓ Axlf signifies the same as xalafahu , i. e. He repaired the garment [app. in any manner, or, as is implied in the S and TA, by substituting one piece for another ]. (S, K, TA.) ― -b2- The saying, in a trad. of Hamneh, faA_i*aA xalafato *`lika falotagotasilo , meaning (assumed tropical:) And when she has discriminated that period of days and nights during which she has been HaAy^iD , [ she shall perform a complete ablution of herself, ] is from xalafa AlqamiyS signifying as explained above. (Msb.) -A6- xalafa signifies also He mixed [a thing with another thing; as, for instance, (see xulifa in a passage above,) milk with other milk]: and he mixed saffron, and medicine, with water. (TA.) -A7- xalafa bayotahu He put to, or made for, his tent, a pole, (K, TA,) termed a xaAlifap , (TA,) in the hinder part thereof. (K TA.) -A8- xalifa , aor. , (K,) inf. n. xalafN , (S, K,) He (a camel) inclined towards one side. (S, K.) ― -b2- xalafN is also an inf. n. (of xalifa , said of a man, TK) signifying The being A^axolaf as meaning contrarious, hard in disposition, as though going with a leaning towards one side: ― -b3- and the being left-handed: ― -b4- and the being A^aHowal [or squint-eyed ]. (K.) -A9- xalifato , aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. xalafN , (Msb, TA,) She (a camel) was, or became, pregnant. (Msb, K.)

definition: , (Msb,) and xl~fhu waraA='ahu , (S, TA,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (Msb,) and xl~fhu waraA='ahu , (S, TA,) inf. n. taxoliyfN , (TA,) He left him behind him; (Msb;) namely, a man: (S, Msb, TA:) and ↓ xalafahu [signifies the same: or] he made him to be behind him; as also ↓ Axlfhu [q.v.], and ↓ Axtlfhu : (TA:) [whence the saying,] A^aloHaHotu EalaY fulaAnK ↓ fiY AlAitibaAEi Hat~aY A@xotalafotuhu i. e. [ I pressed upon such a one in following ] until I made him to be behind me. (ISk, TA.) You say also, xal~afahumo , inf. n. as above, meaning He was, or became, or went, before them; and left them behind him. (TA.) And xl~fwA A^avoqAlahum , inf. n. as above, They left their loads, or baggage &c., behind their backs; (O, K;) when they went away to draw water. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] xl~fhu He made him, or appointed him, his xaliyfap [i. e. successor, or vice-agent, &c.]; (K;) and so ↓ Astxlfhu . (S, Msb, K.) So in the Kur [xxiv. 54], ↓ layasotaxilafan~ahumo fiY A@loA^aroDi kamaA A@sotaxolafa A@l~a*iyna mino qabolihimo [ That He will assuredly make them to be successors in the earth, like as He made to be successors those who were before them ]. (TA.) -A2- xl~f binaAqatihi , (S, K,) inf. n. as above, (S,) He bound one of the teats of his she-camel with the thing termed SiraAr [in order that her young one might not suck it]: (S, K:) from Yaakoob. (S.)

definition: , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) inf.
sourceDefinition: , (Mgh, Msb, TA,) inf. n. xilaAfN (S, Mgh, Msb, K, TA) and muxaAlafapN , (S, Msb, K, TA,) He [or it ] disagreed with, or differed from, him [or it ]; or he dissented from him; (Mgh, Msb;) contr. of waAfaqahu ; fiY ka*aA [ in, or in respect of, such a thing ]: (Mgh:) and he, or it, was contrary, opposed, or repugnant, to him, or it: (TA:) [and he acted contrarily, contrariously, adversely, or in opposition, to him, or it; he, or it, contravened, or opposed, him, or it: ] and he [or it ] contradicted him [or it ]. (M in art. nqD .) It is said in a prov., A_in~amaA A^anota xilaAfa AlD~abuEi Alr~aAkiba , i. e. tuxaAlifu xilaAfa AlD~abuEi [ Verily thou art one who acts with the contrariousness of the hyena towards the rider ]: for the hyena [attacks a man on foot, but], when it sees the rider, flees from him. (IAar, TA.) You say also, xaAlafaniY Eano ka*aA He turned away from such a thing [ in opposition to me, or] when I betook myself to it: [see also the last sentence but one of the first paragraph of art. bht :] and xAlfnY A_ilaY ka*aA He betook himself to such a thing [ in opposition to me, or] when I turned away from it: (Mgh:) or xAlfhu A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i means he disobeyed him by betaking himself to the thing; or betook himself to the thing after he had forbidden him it. (TA.) And hence, (Mgh,) huwa yuxaAlifu A_ilaY A@moraA^api fulaAnK , (S, Mgh, *) or A_ilaY fulaAnapa , (O, L, TA,) in the K erroneously, hw yxAlf fulaAnapa , (TA,) He comes to the wife of such a one when he [the latter] is absent from her, (S,) or to such a woman when her husband is absent from her: (Mgh, * O, L, K, TA:) and xAlfhu A_ilaY A^aholihi [ he came to his (another's) wife in his (the husband's) absence]: see 1, in the former half of the paragraph. (Az, TA.) And xAlfhu A_ilayohimo He watched to see him, and, when he was absent from them, namely, his family, he went in to them: (Jm, O, TA:) and, accord. to AZ, fulaAnN SaAHibahu ↓ Axlf Such a one watched to see his companion, and, when he was absent, he came, and went in to him [or rather to his wife or to his family ]: (TA:) [or] SaAHibahu ↓ xAlf he watched to see his companion, and, when he was absent, went in to his wife: (K, and the like is said in the JK:) thus says IDrd, on the authority of AZ. (TA.) And xAlf A_ilaY qawomK He came to a party, or company of men, from behind them [or behind their backs ]: or he feigned to them the contrary of that which he conceived in his mind, and took them unawares. (TA.) Aboo-Dhu-eyb says, [describing a collector of wild honey,] A_i*aA lasaEatohu Aln~aHolu lamo yaroju lasoEahaA waxaAlafahaA fiY bayoti nuwbK EawaAsili (S in the present art., in which only the former hemistich is cited, and in art. rjw ,) i. e. [ When the bees sting him, ] he fears not nor minds [ their stinging ], (S in art. rjw ) [ but comes, during their absence, to the hiving-place of bees occupied in gathering honey: ] meaning, he comes to their honey, (S, TA, [in the latter of which, in the place of AlnHl , is put Ald~aboru “ the swarm of bees, ”]) and takes it, (TA,) while they are feeding; (S, TA;) or, as AA says, he comes behind them to the honey while they are absent: AO explains it by xaAlafahaA A_ilaY mawoDiEK A=xara which [he says] means he keeps with them [ to another place ]; syn. laAzamahaA ; [and thus this phrase (which is strangely misinterpreted in the TK and in Freytag's Lexicon) is explained in the K, but without any reference to the verse;] as also HaAlafahaA , with the unpointed H : (TA:) and some read the verse thus; but this reading is said to be a mistake. (TA in art. Hlf .) ― -b2- jaA='a xilaAfahu : see 1, near the beginning of the paragraph. And see also five other exs. in the middle portion of the same paragraph. ― -b3- xAlf bayona rijolayohi He put one of his legs forward and the other backward: and [hence,] AlmuxaAlafapu bayona Alr~ijolayoni [as signifying the alternate shifting of the legs to and fro ] is metonymically used as meaning the act of dancing. (Har p. 108.) [And xAlf bayona Al$~ayoy^ayoni He put, or placed, the two things contrariwise; or on contrary sides; or in contrary directions. Hence,] A^awo tuqaT~aEa A^ayodiyhimo waA^arojuluhumo mino xilaAfK , in the Kur v. 37, [ Or that their hands and their feet shall be cut off on contrary sides, ] means that their right hands and left feet shall be cut off. (Bd, Jel. [See also similar exs. in the Kur vii. 121 and xx. 74 and xxvi. 49.]) [Hence also,] farasN bihi $ikaAlN mino xilaAfK , (JK,) or *uw xadamataAni mino xilaAfK , (TA,) A horse having a whiteness in his right fore leg and his left hind leg [or the reverse ]: (JK, TA:) and some say, lahu xadamataAni mino xilaAfK when he has a whiteness [or rather a ring of white a little above the hoof ] in his fore leg [or right fore leg ] and another in his left fore leg [probably a mistake of a copyist for his left hind leg ]. (TA.)

definition: Also He put him, turned him, or made him to go back or stand back, behind him.
sourceDefinition: : see 2, first sentence. Also He put him, turned him, or made him to go back or stand back, behind him. (K, TA.) And Axlf yadahu He put his hand behind him. (Az, TA.) And also, (Fr, TA,) or Axlf biyadihi A_ilaY Als~ayofi , (JK,) or simply Axlf [used elliptically], (S, K,) He put [ back ] his hand to his sword, (Fr, S, K, TA,) in order to draw it, (JK, S, K, TA,) it being hung behind him. (Fr, * TA.) And Axlf Als~ayofa [ He hung the sword behind him; or kept it hung behind him ]: said, in a trad., of a man on the day of Bedr. (TA.) (tropical:) [ The stars broke their promise; meaning,] were attended with drought, not attended with rain: (S, K, TA:) a saying of the people in the Time of Ignorance: (S, TA:) and so Eano A^anowaAy^ihaA ↓ Aixotalafato : for they used to believe and say that they were rained upon by such and such a nawo' . definition: signifies The following reciprocally;
sourceDefinition: signifies The following reciprocally; or alternating. (Mgh.) So in the phrase in the Kur [ii. 159 and iii. 187 and xlv. 4], waA@xotilaAfi All~ayolu waAln~ahaAri And the alternating of the night and the day. (Mgh) [And in a verse of El-'Ajjáj cited voce A^abolaY , in art. blw .] And hence the phrase, AixotalafaA DarobapF Each of them beat, or struck the other in turn. (Mgh.) And the saying, in a trad. of 'Alee, faA@xotalafato bayona Eubayodapa boni AlH`rivi waAlwaliydi boni Euqobapa DarobataAni [ And two blows were interchanged between 'Obeydeh Ibn-El-Hárith and El-Weleed Ibn-'Okbeh]. (Mgh.) And the saying, in a trad. of Umm-Sabeeyeh, Aixotalafato yadiY waydu rasuwli A@ll~`hi fiY A_inaA='K waAHidK , meaning My hand and the hand of the Apostle of God were both put [ by turns ] into one vessel. (Mgh.) And AixotalafuwA signifies They followed, or succeeded, one another; whenever one went, another coming after him. (TA in art. Ewr .) ― -b2- Also The going, or moving, repeatedly, to and fro; so coming and going; or reciprocating; syn. tarad~udN [in this sense, as is shown in this art. in the K and TA, and in the S and K in art. rwd &c.: and also as mean ing the returning, or repairing, time after time, or repeatedly, or frequently, to a person or place; because it implies coming and going: and sometimes it means simply the returning; because this cannot be without a previous going]. (K.) You say, huwa yaxotalifu A_ilaY fulaAnK , i. e. yatarad~adu [ He returns, or repairs, time after time, repeatedly, or frequently, to such a one ]: and Aixotalafa A_ilayohi A@xotilaAfapF waAHidapF [ He returned to him once ]. (TA.) And huwa yaxotalifu A_ilaY majaAlisi AlEilomi He repairs frequently to, or frequents, the assemblies of science; syn. yatarad~adu . (A in art. rd .) And Aixotalafa A_ilaY AlmutawaD~aA^i [ He returned, or repaired, time after time, &c., to the privy ]. (S.) And Aixotalafa A_ilaY AlxalA='i [properly signifies the same: and hence, (assumed tropical:) He had a looseness of the bowels, or a diarrhœa ]. (K.) And [perhaps as implying coming and going,] Axtlf also signifies He supplied, or gave, or offered, water. (TA.) ― -b3- [Also The disagreeing, differing, or varying, in state or condition or quality &c.; being dissimilar, different, diverse, various, incongruous, discordant, or dissentient: ] Axtlf is the contr. of Ait~afaqa ; (K, TA;) and is said of anything that is dissimilar [in the parts or members &c. of which it is composed]; as also ↓ txAlf . (TA.) You say, AlA^amoraAni ↓ txAlf [and Axtlf AlAmrAn ], i. e. lamo yat~afiqaA [ The two things, or affairs, or cases, were, or became, dissimilar, &c.]. (TA.) And AxtlfwA and ↓ txAlfwA (Mgh, Msb) [ They disagreed, &c., fiY A^amorK in a thing or an affair or a case; ] every one of them took to, or held, a way, or an opinion, different from, or contrary to, that of another: (Msb:) both signify the same. (Mgh.) It is said in a trad., saw~uwA Sufuwfakumo walaA taxotalifuwA fataxotalifa quluwbukumo [ Make ye your ranks even when ye place yourselves to pray together, and be not dissimilar in your positions, for in that case your hearts would disagree ]; meaning, when one of you advances, or stands, before another in the ranks, your hearts will be affected, and disagreement in respect of friendship and amity will arise among you: or, as some say, it means, your hearts will be made to recoil: or the Suwrap [or specific character ] of your hearts will become changed into another Swrp . (TA.) [Hence,] Aixotalafato Eano A^anowaAy^ihaA , said of stars: see 4, near the middle of the paragraph. ― -b4- Also The being complicated, intricate, or confused. (KL.) [You say, Axtlf AlA^amoru bayonahumo The affair, or case, was, or became, complicated, intricate, or confused, so as to be a subject of disagreement, or difference, between them: a phrase of frequent occurrence.] -A2- Axtlfhu : see 1, in two places, in the former half of the paragraph. ― -b2- See also 2, in two places. ― -b3- Axtlf SaAHibahu : see 3, near the middle of the paragraph.

definition: [meaning The location, or quarter, that is behind;
sourceDefinition: [meaning The location, or quarter, that is behind; and the time past; ] (K; [so in my MS. copy, and thus it should be written as a simple noun; but in the CK xalofu ;]) or Alxalofu ; (Lth, K;) contr. of qud~aAmN [or Alqud~aAmu ]: (Lth, K:) [and] xalofa [ Behind; and after; ] contr. of qud~aAma : (S: [thus in my tow copies; and said in the margin of one of them to be thus in the copy of IB, and in that of El-Jawáleekee:]) a simple noun: and an adv. n.: of the fem. gender [as meaning the jihap ; but otherwise it seems to be masc.]. (TA.) You say, jaA='a xalofahu [and mino xalofihi , both meaning He came behind him, and after him ]. (Mgh.) And jalasotu xalofa fulaAnK I sat after, or behind, such a one; syn. baEodahu (S.) And labiva xalofahu He remained after him. (K.) Some read, in the Kur [xvii. 78], waA_i*FA laAyalobavuwna xalofaka : others read xilaAfaka [which means the same, as mentioned above: see the middle of the first paragraph of this art.]. (TA.) ― -b2- xalofN signifies also The back (K, TA) itself: so says IAar: and particularly, of a house; the side corresponding to, or over against, that in which is the door; and as a house may have two doors, [in two different sides,] it may be said to have two backs, each of which may be thus termed; and the dual of this word seems to be used as meaning two backs in a trad. [respecting the building of the Kaabeh]. (TA.) ― -b3- And One who comes after another; (S, TA;) as also ↓ xalafN , or, accord. to some, there is a difference between these two, as will be shown in what follows; (S;) and ↓ xaAlifN and ↓ xaAlifapN : it is originally an inf. n.: (TA:) and signifies one who remains after another, whether this other be dead or living: and one remaining after another who is dead; his follower, or successor; the follower, or successor, of one who has gone: used in praise and in dispraise: pl. xuluwfN : and the sing. also signifies [like the pl.] persons remaining after others; accord. to some: (IB, TA:) a remnant of people: (Lh, TA:) and a generation after a generation; (Lth, S, K;) as also ↓ xalafN : (Lth, TA:) but Lth says that the former is applied to the evil, and ↓ the latter to the good, (K, TA,) whether meaning a generation or a son: (TA:) the latter means a good son (K, TA) remaining after his father: (TA:) and the former, a bad son: (K, TA:) [therefore] one says, huwa xalofu sawo'K mino A^abiyhi [ He is a bad son ] who has taken the place of his father, and SidoqK mn Abyh ↓ xalafu [ a good son ] &c.: (S:) but sometimes each is used in the place of the other; so that one says, hw xalofu SidoqK mn Abyh : (K:) or both signify the same: (S, K:) so says Akh: some, he says, use the former; and some, the latter: but some say SidoqK ↓ xalafu and xalofu sawo'K , meaning thus to distinguish between them: (S:) accord. to IB, ↓ xalafN correctly signifies a man's successor who is a substitute for him, good and bad: and is originally an inf. n.: (TA:) and the pl. of this is A^axolaAfN : (AZ, IB, TA:) accord. to IAth, xalafu SidoqK means a good generation: and xalofu sawo'K , an evil generation: (TA:) and xalofN likewise signifies progeny [without restriction]. (K.) One says also, (S, K,) of a people following people more in number than they, (S,) h`w^ulaA='i xalofu sawo'K [ These are a bad generation. (S, K.) And baqiynaA fiY xalofi sawo'K We remained among an evil remnant. (Lh, TA.) And faxalafa mino baEodihimo xalofN , in the Kur [vii. 168 and xix. 60], is explained as meaning And there remained after them a remnant. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence,] (tropical:) One in whom is no good. (IB, K.) [And app. also Persons in whom is no good. .] ― -b5- And (tropical:) A thing in which is no good: (IB, TA:) [and particularly] (assumed tropical:) a bad saying; (ISk, S, Msb, K;) a wrong, bad saying, like the xalof of mankind. (A 'Obeyd, Msb.) See also xulofN . It is said in a prov., sakata A^alofFA wanaTaqa xalofFA (assumed tropical:) He held his tongue from a thousand words ( sakata Eano A^alofi kalimap ), and then uttered what was wrong. (ISk, S, Msb.) An Arab of the desert, who had been guilty of a breach of manners ( Habaqa HaboqapF ), pointed with his thumb towards his Aisot , and said, A_in~ahaA xalofN naTaqato xalofFA [which may be rendered, Verily it is a thing in which is no good: it uttered a thing in which was no good: but it obviously admits of being rendered otherwise]. (IAar, S.) ― -b6- Also People who have gone away from the tribe (T, K) to draw water, and have left their baggage &c. behind them: (T, TA:) and such as are present, [ remaining behind, ] of the tribe: thus bearing two contr. significations: pl. xuluwfN . (K.) You say HaY~N xuluwfN A tribe who are absent; none of them remaining behind: (S, TA:) or a tribe of which the men are absent and the women remaining: (TA:) and xuluwfN also signifies the contr., i. e. such as are present, (S, TA,) remaining behind. (S.) It is said of Mohammad, in a trad., lamo yatoruko A^aholahu xuluwfFA , i. e. He did not leave his family neglected, with no pastor nor protector. (TA.) See also a verse of El-Hoteíäh in the latter part of the first paragraph of this article. -A2- Old and worn out; applied to a waTob [or skin for milk, or for clarified butter and milk: as though it were a remnant thereof]. (Ibn-' Abbád, K.) -A3- A mirobad ; (S, K;) i. e. a place of confinement for camels: (TA:) or such as is behind the tent or house. (JK, S, * K.) -A4- A large faA^os [i. e. hoe or adze or axe ]: or such as has one head: and the edge of a fA^s : or the head thereof: (K:) you say faA^osN *aAtu xaloqayoni a two-headed fA^s : (S, TA:) or *aAtu xaloqayoni and ↓ *aAtu xiloqayoni are names of the fA^s (K, TA) when two-headed: (TA:) and the pl. is *awaAtu Alxaloqayoni : (K:) pl. xuluwfN . (JK.) ― -b2- And The head of a razor. (K.) ― -b3- And The [ pointed ] head of a minoqaAr , [ an iron instrument like the faA^os , (A and K in art. nqr ,) with which mill-stones &c. are pecked, or wrought into shape, (see minoqaArN ,) and ] with which wood is cut. (TA.) -A5- See also xilofN .

sourceDefinition: a subst. from A_ixolaAfN , (S, Msb, K,) relating to a promise, and restricted to future time; (Msb;) i. e. a subst. used in the place of A_ixolaAfN ; (Lh, TA;) meaning The breach, or non-fulfilment, of a promise; as also ↓ xulufN , which is said to be the original form of the word, and ↓ xuluwfN : (TA:) it is, in respect of the future, like ka*ibN in respect of the past: (S, K:) some say that it signifies a false, or wrong, saying; which is a meaning of ↓ xalofN , with fet-h, before mentioned: but perhaps these two words may be syn. dial. vars. (MF, TA.) ― -b2- Also, (Msb,) or ↓ xulofapN , and ↓ xilofapN , (K, TA,) Disagreement, difference, dissension, contrariety, contrariousness, or opposition, (Msb, K, * TA,) in opinions or the like, (Msb,) or in respect of friendship and amity, (TA in explanation of the second of these words,) or in natural disposition; (K;) as also ↓ xilafonapN (S, K) and ↓ xilafonaApN and ↓ xaAlifN and ↓ xaAlifapN . (K.) -A2- It is also pl. of xaliyfN , in its various senses.

You say, AijoEalo h`*aA xalofFA mino h`*aA Make thou this to be a substitute for this. (Msb.) And h`*aA xalafN mim~aA A^uxi*a laka This is a substitute for what has been taken to thee. (IB.) And fiY h`w^ulaA='i Alqawomi xalafN mim~ano maDaY In these people are such as supply the place of those who have gone. (TA.) And fiY fulaAnK xalafN mino fulaAnK [ In such a one is a substitute for such a one ]. (TA.) And huwa mino A^abiyhi xalafN He is a substitute for his father. (IB.) See also xalofN , in six places, in the former half of the paragraph.

sourceDefinition: a subst. signifying A mode, or manner, of coming after [or behind ]; like qiEodapN signifying “ a mode, or manner, of sitting. ” (Msb.) ― -b2- See also xulofN . ― -b3- It signifies also Difference [ of any kind ]: (K, * TA:) or the coming and going of the night and the day; (S, K, * TA;) and likewise of wild animals. (K.) Hence the saying in the Kur [xxv. 63], wahuwa A@l~a*iY jaEala A@ll~ayola waA@ln~ahaAra xilofapF , (S, K, *) meaning *awaY xilofapK , (Bd,) i. e. [ And He it is who hath made the night and the day ] so that each replaces the other: or each follows the other: (K, * TA:) or so that he who is unable to accomplish a thing in the night may do it in the day, and the reverse. (Fr, L, K.) Zuheyr says, of wild animals, yamo$iyna xilofapF , meaning They go to and fro. (S, TA. [See Em p. 109.]) And one says, A^axa*atohu xilofapN , meaning He was taken with [ an affection causing ] a frequent going to and from the privy. (S, K.) [And hence,] xilofapN signifies also, A discharging of the bowels; or a purging and vomiting together; (K;) or a disordered state of the stomach arising from [ unwholesome ] food; (TA;) a looseness, or diarrhœa. (JK, TA.) ― -b4- See also xilofN . ― -b5- Also The bringing of camels to the watering-place in the evening, after the people have gone away. (L, K.) ― -b6- And A man's watching to see another, ( A^ano yunaAZira in some copies of the K, and An yunaASira in other copies, being put for An yubaASiru , which is the right reading, agreeably with an explanation of Aixotalafa SaAHibahu , [for which see 3, near the middle of the paragraph,] TA,) and when he is absent from his family, going in to them, (K, TA,) or [rather], when he is absent from his wife, going in to her. (TA, after the explanation of the phrase above mentioned.) -A2- A thing that is suspended behind the rider; (JK, K;) such as is suspended behind the [ kind of vehicle called ] maHomil . (TA.) ― -b2- Remains of water in a trough or tank. (TA.) ― -b3- What remains, of food, between the teeth. (Lh, K.) ― -b4- A plant, or herbage, that comes forth after another plant, or other herbage, (S, Msb, K,) which has become dry, and broken in pieces: (S, TA:) or that comes forth not from rain, but by reason of the cold of the latter part of the night. (Aboo-Ziyád El-Kilábee, K. [See also rabolN .]) ― -b5- What the trees disclose in the beginning of the cold, (K, TA,) by reason of the [ rain called ] Safariy~ap [q. v.]: (TA:) or fruit that comes forth after other fruit: (K:) or fruit that comes forth after abundant fruit; (S, Mgh, TA;) this being termed the xilofap of trees: (S, Mgh:) or a growth of leaves after the falling away of other leaves: (K, * TA: duwna in the K is a mistake for baEoda : TA:) or leaves that come forth after the first leaves, in the [ season called ] Sayof . (Nh, TA.) ― -b6- What grows in the Sayof [or summer ]; so says A 'Obeyd: (S, K:) or, (JK, Mgh, K,) as also ↓ xilofN , (K,) the herbage produced by the Syf , (JK, K,) or in the Syf , (Mgh,) after the springherbage has dried up. (JK, Mgh.) ― -b7- A produce of grape-vines after the grapes have turned black; the grapes being gathered while it is fresh and green, it then ripens: and so other fruits: or a new produce, by the vine, of fresh sour grapes. (K.) ― -b8- Grain that is sown (JK, * Mgh, K *) after the former has come to maturity: (Mgh, TA:) because taken as a substitute for wheat and barley: (K:) pl. xilafN . (Mgh.) ― -b9- A piece with which a garment is patched (K) when it is old and worn out. (TA.) ― -b10- A time after a time. (IAar, K.) -A3- Differing [ one from another or others ]; as also ↓ xilofN : (K:) it is applied in this sense to a people, or company of men: (AZ, S, K:) and to beasts, or horses or the like, as meaning differing (K, TA) in their colours and appearances: (TA:) and xilofataAni is applied to any two things that are different; (Ks, TA;) as also ↓ xilofaAni : (Ks, Msb, TA:) and xilofapN , (K,) or xilofataAni , (Ks, TA,) to any two colours that are combined [because different ]. (Ks, K, TA.) AZ cites, as an ex., the saying [of a rájiz], saAqiyaAhumaA ↓ dalowaAYo xilofaAni [ My two buckets are different, and their two suppliers with water ]; (S, TA;) meaning that one of them [i. e. of the buckets] is ascending and full, and the other is descending and empty; or that one of them is new, and the other is old and worn out. (TA, in two places.) And one says of two children, or two male slaves; or two female slaves, that they are xilofataAni , (Ks, K,) and ↓ xilofaAni , (K,) applying to the male and the female, (TA,) meaning One tall and the other short: or one white and the other black. (Ks, K.) One says also, banuw fulaAnK xilofapN , meaning The children of such a one are half males and half females. (S.) And nitaAju fulaAnK xilofapN The offspring of the beasts of such a one are one year male and another year female. (JK, TA.) And ↓ waladato xilofayoni , said of ewe or goat, (K,) or of a camel, (L,) She brought forth one year a male and another year a female. (L, K.) The pl. [of ↓ xilofN ] (K, TA) in all its senses (TA) is A^axolaAfN and xilafapN ; (K, * TA;) the latter, [in the CK xilofapN ,] like qiradapN as pl. of qirodN . (TA.)

sourceDefinition: an inf. n. of 3 [q. v. passim]. (S, &c.) ― -b2- Also The contrary, or opposite, of a thing; syn. Did~N . (Msb in art. Dd . [Very often used in this sense.]) You say, AlAixotilaAfu xilaAfu AlAit~ifaAqi [i. e. AlAxtlAf is the contrary of AlAt~fAq ] (TA.) -A2- Also, (S, Msb, K,) by the vulgar (O, Msb, TA) incorrectly pronounced with teshdeed (O, Msb, K, TA) and fet-h [to the x , i. e. xal~aAfN ], (TA,) A well-known kind of tree; (S;) the [ kind of tree called ] SafoSaAf : (Msb:) or a species of the SfSAf , but not the SfSAf itself: (K:) [the salix Aegyptia of Linnæus; called by this name in the present day; and by some, improperly, baAnN , q. v.:] it abounds in the land of the Arabs; and is [ also ] called sawojarN [or sawoHarN ]; and there are many varieties thereof; all of them soft and weak; (TA;) but it is seldom, or never, found in the desert: (Msb:) they assert that it is thus called because the torrent brings it from one locality to another, so that it grows in a place different from that of its origin; (AHn, Msb, K, * TA;) but this is not a valid assertion: (TA:) [it is a coll. gen. n.:] n. un. with p . (Msb, TA.) suw~iyna mino xilaAfi , in the saying of the rájiz cited voce xuf~N , means Made of different trees: it does not mean of the tree called xilaAf ; because this is seldom, or never, found in the desert. (S, TA.) ― -b2- Also The sleeve of a shirt. (IAar, K.)

definition: A successor: and a vice-agent, vice- gerent, lieutenant, substitute, proxy, or deputy: (KL:) one who has been made, or appointed, to take the place of him who has been before him: (JK:) an act.
sourceDefinition: A successor: and a vice-agent, vice- gerent, lieutenant, substitute, proxy, or deputy: (KL:) one who has been made, or appointed, to take the place of him who has been before him: (JK:) an act. part. n. of xalafahu , inf. n. xalafN and xilaAfapN ; as also ↓ xaliyfN : (TA:) or it may have the meaning of an act. part. n. or that of a pass. part. n.: and so in the sense next following: (Msb:) the supreme, or greatest, ruler or sovereign, (S, Msb, K, TA,) who supplies the place of him who has been before him; (TA;) [particularly the successor of the Prophet; whence “ Caliph, ” commonly used by English writers for “ Khaleefeh; ”] as also ↓ xaliyfN , (K,) which is the original form, (Msb,) without p ; (Msb, TA;) disapproved by some, but mentioned by AHát and Ibn-' Abbád and IB, and occurring in a verse of Ows Ibn-Hajar cited by IB: (TA:) the p in the former is to denote intensiveness of signification, (Nh, Msb, TA,) as in Eal~aAmapN and nas~aAbapN : (Msb:) or, as some say, liln~aqoli [i. e. for the transference of the word from the category of epithets to that of substs.]: (TA:) it is also said that the word may be an epithet of which the subst. qualified thereby is suppressed, for nafosN xaliyfapN ; but this requires consideration: (MF, TA:) it is an epithet applied to a man peculiarly: (Msb:) some make it fem.; (Fr, S, Msb, K;) saying h`*aA xaliyfapN A^uxoraY [ This is another Khaleefeh ]; though the proper way is to make it masc.: (Msb:) a poet says, A^abuwka xaliyfapN waladatohu A^uxoraY waA^anota xaliyfapN *aAka AlkamaAlu [ Thy father was a Khaleefeh, whom another Khaleefeh begat; and thou art a Khaleefeh: that is perfection ]: (Fr, S:) the pl. is xalaAy^ifu [generally applied to any people that have succeeded others, and supplied their places, as in the Kur x. 15], (S, K,) like as karaAy^imu is pl. of kariymapN ; (S;) and xulafaA='u [generally applied to successors of the Prophet], (S, K,) because, as it applies only to the male, and has p added, the p is dropped in forming the pl., which is thus like ZurafaA='u as pl. of ZariyfN : (S:) thus says ISk, and the like is said in the O: but what AHát and Ibn-'Abbád say requires not this straining: (TA:) [i. e.] xalaAy^ifu is pl. of xaliyfapN ; and xulafaA='u , of ↓ xaliyfN : (JK:) or some, having regard to the original, make the pl. to be xulafaA='u , like as $urafaA='u is pl. of $ariyfN ; (Msb;) and this pl. is masc. only, so that you say valaAvapN xulafaA='a : (ISk, Msb, TA:) and some, having regard to the word itself [in its altered and used state], make the pl. to be xalaAy^ifu ; (Msb;) and this pl. may have prefixed to it either a masc. or a fem. n. of number, so that you say valaAvapN xalaAy^ifa and valaAvu xalaAy^ifa ; (ISk, Msb, TA;) both of which are chaste. (Msb.) You say, kaAna A@ll~`hu xaliyfapa waAlidika Ealayoka [ May God be to thee a supplier of the place of thy father ]: (S, Msb: *) and in like manner you say, to a person, of any one whom he has lost by death, (S, Msb,) and who cannot be replaced; as the paternal uncle; (Msb;) or the mother. (K.) Some say that the application of the title xaliyfapu A@ll~`hi [ The Vicegerent of God ] is not allowable, except to Adam and David because there is express authority in these instances [in the Kur ii. 28 and xxxviii. 25]; but others allow it in other cases, like suloTaAnu A@ll~`hi and junuwdu A@ll~`hi and Hizobu A@ll~`hi and xayolu A@ll~`hi ; all of which have been heard: (Msb:) and Zj says that it is allowable to say of the Imáms that they are xulafaA='u A@ll~`hi fiY A^aroDihi [ The Vicegerents of God in his earth ]. (TA.)
