sourceDefinition: : see xalofN , in the former half of the paragraph. ― -b2- Also One who remains behind, or after, another, (Yz, K, TA,) or others, in the case of a war, or a warring and plundering expedition, and in other cases: (TA:) pl. xaAlifuwna (Yz, K, TA) and xawaAlifu , which latter is extr. [in this case], but is also said to be a [reg.] pl. of ↓ xaAlifapN , and as such to signify persons who do not go forth on a warring, or warring and plundering, expedition: and AlgaAziY ↓ xaAlifapu signifies he who remains behind, or after, him who goes forth on such an expedition, being of his family. (TA.) faA@qoEuduwA maEa AlxaAlifiyna , in the Kur [ix. 84], means Then stay ye with those who remain behind. (Yz, K. *) xawaAlifu is also pl. of ↓ xaAlifapN [as fem. of xaAlifN ], (TA,) and signifies Women (K, TA) remaining behind in the houses or tents: but some assign to it the first of the meanings explained above: and some say that it means the children remaining behind. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [ix. 88 and 94], ↓ raDuwA biA^ano yakuwnuwA maEa AlxawaAlifi , i. e. [ They chose to be ] with the women: (S, K: *) thus it is explained by Ibn-'Arafeh: but some say that the meaning is, with the bad, or corrupt, persons; and that xwAlf is here a pl. [of xaAlifN ,] like fawaArisu . (TA.) For ― -b3- xaAlifN is applied to a man [as meaning Bad, or corrupt ]; and ↓ xaAlifapN to a woman as meaning bad, or corrupt, and remaining behind in her abode: and the former to a slave as meaning bad, or corrupt: and also contrarious: and in this last sense it is likewise applied to a companion: and some of the grammarians say that there is no word of the measure faAEilN having its pl. of the measure fawaAEilu , except xaAlifN and haAlikN and faArisN : but see this last: (TA:) and ↓ xil~iyfapN , also, has this last signification; (JK, TA;) or [rather] signifies very contrarious; (K;) as also ↓ xaAlifapN ; (JK;) and so ↓ xilafonapN , and ↓ xilafonaApN , (Lh, JK, K,) in each of which the n is augmentative, and each of which is applied to a man and to a woman and to a pl. number; (Lh, K;) but xilafonayaAtN has been mentioned as pl. [of xlfnAp ], and as applied to males and females: (TA:) and xaAlifuwna is likewise used in this sense applied to a number of men. (JK.) ― -b4- Also, applied to a slave, [and app. to any man, but in this latter case I find it written xlf , which I believe to be a mistranscription,] One who has withdrawn from the people of his house: so says Lh. (TA.) ― -b5- Also Stupid; foolish; or having little, or no, intellect or understanding; as also ↓ xaAlifapN , (K, TA,) but in an intensive sense, and also applied to a woman; (TA;) and ↓ A^axolafu , (JK, K,) of which the fem. is xalofaA='u ; (JK, TA;) and ↓ xulofufN , (K,) or ↓ xulofafN , (L,) or both, (JK,) likewise applied to a woman, as also ↓ xulofufapN , (K,) or ↓ xulofafapN : (JK:) or, as some say, xaAlifN signifies one in whom is no good: and, as also ↓ xaAlifapN , one who has not what suffices: or who often breaks his promises: (TA:) or both of these mean one who has not what suffices, and in whom is no good: or very contrarious. (JM.) One says that a man is A^aholi bayotihi ↓ xaAlifapu and xaAlifu , Ahl byth , meaning The one in whom is no good, of the people of his house: (S, K:) and the ungenerous: (K:) or the stupid, or foolish: or the bad, or corrupt, and the evil: and it is [said to be] tropical. (TA.) And ↓ qawomN xawaAlifN Persons in whom is no good. (JK.) ― -b6- And, [app. because he leaves his family behind him,] A drawer of water; (S, TA;) as also ↓ musotaxolifN [q. v.]: both mentioned in the K; but Als~aq~aA='u is there erroneously put for AlmusotaqiY . definition: A camel that has exceeded in age the baAzil ;
sourceDefinition: A camel that has exceeded in age the baAzil ; [which latter is generally one that has entered the ninth year; ] (S, M, K;) beyond which there is no age [having an epithet to denote it]; therefore, (TA,) one says muxolifu EaAmK and muxolifu EaAmayoni [ that has exceeded in age the bAzl by a year and by two years ]; (S, TA; [see 4;]) applied alike to the male and the female; (S, K;) and the female is also termed muxolafapN : (K:) or this latter signifies (tropical:) a she-camel that appears, (S, K,) or is thought, (A,) to be pregnant, and is not pregnant: (S, A, K:) and the pl. is maxaAliyfu . (TA.) ― -b2- See also mixolaAfN . ― -b3- Also A man whose cattle have not obtained the [ herbage termed ] rabiyE . (JK.) ― -b4- rajulN muxolifN mutolifN , or ↓ mixolafN mitolafN , and mitolaAfN ↓ mixolaAfN : see art. tlf . ― -b5- nawomapu AlD~uHaY muxolifapN lilofami , (K, TA,) also written ↓ maxolafapN , and in some copies nawomu AlD~uHaY , [which requires the reading maxolafapN ,] (TA,) i. e. (JK.) ― -b7- See also the explanation of the verse of El- Hoteiäh cited in the last quarter of the first paragraph. The qaTaA are termed muxolifaAtN because they draw water for their young ones. (JK.)

definition: A man who often breaks his promises;
sourceDefinition: A man who often breaks his promises; (S, K;) as also ↓ muxolifN : (TA:) [whence the latter (which properly signifies simply breaking a promise ) is applied to a star, or an asterism, as meaning (tropical:) Unattended with rain: (see 4:) and in the same sense to clouds ( saHaAb ): or, accord. to Freytag's Lex., in this or in the contr. sense.] ― -b2- See also muxolifN . ― -b3- And see maxolafaAn . -A2- Also A kuwrap [i. e. province, district, or region ] (S, Mgh, Msb) pertaining to the people of El-Yemen, (S,) or in the dial. of El-Yemen; (Mgh, Msb;) pl. maxaAliyfu ; (S, Msb;) every mxlAf thereof having a [distinctive] name whereby it is known; (S;) the mxAlyf of the people of El-Yemen being like the A^ajonad of the people of Syria and the kuwar of the people of El-'Irák and the rasaAtiyq of the people of El-Jibál and the TasaAsiyj of the people of El-Ahwáz: (IB:) or mixolaAfN signifies a kuwrap (JK, M, K) to which a man comes; (M;) [ in any country; ] and hence the mxAlyf of ElYemen, (K,) i. e. its kuwar : (TA:) some say that there is a mxlAf in every country; (Msb;) so says Khálid Ibn-Jembeh; (TA;) i. e. a naAHiyap [as meaning a district &c.]; (Msb;) and thus one says the mxlAf of El-Medeeneh, and of ElYemámeh, (Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, TA,) and the mxAlyf of Et-Táïf: (AA, Msb, TA:) but properly it is peculiar to the dial. of El-Yemen. (TA.) ― -b2- Also i. q. bnkrd [a foreign word, and perhaps mistranscribed], i. e. The poor-rate of any particular people or party, which is given by them to [the poor of] their own community: so says Aboo-Mo'ádh: (L:) and ↓ maxaAlifu [is its pl., as also, app., maxaAliyfu , agreeably with rule, and] signifies the poor-rates of the Arabs; (JK, TA;) [as in the saying,] AusotuEomila fulaAnN EalaY maxaAlifi baniY fulaAnK [ Such a one was employed as collector of the poor-rates of the sons of such a one ]. (JK.)

sourceDefinition: , (T, S, M, K, &c.,) aor. , (M, Msb,) inf. n. duvuwrN , (T, S, M, K, &c.,) said of a trace, or mark, of a house; or of what remains, cleaving to the ground, marking the place of a house; (S, Msb, K, TA;) or of a place of abode, (T, A,) &c.; (T;) or of a thing; (M;) It became covered with sand and dust blown over it by the wind: this is the primary signification: (TA:) or it became effaced, or obliterated, (T, S, M, A, K, TA,) by the blowing of the winds over it; (TA;) as also ↓ tdAvr , (S,) or ↓ Andvr : (M, K:) and it became old; (M, K;) as also ↓ Andvr , (M,) or ↓ tdAvr . (K.) By one of the poets it is metaphorically said of a man's reputation, meaning (tropical:) It became worn out of regard or notice; became effaced, or obliterated. (M, TA.) ― -b2- And, said of a man, (assumed tropical:) He became overcome by old age and emaciation. (T, TA.) ― -b3- Also, said of a garment, (T, K,) inf. n. as above, (T,) It became dirty. (T, K.) ― -b4- And, said of a sword, (T, A, K,) inf. n. as above, (A,) (tropical:) It became sullied from remaining long unfurbished; (A;) it became rusty. (T, K.) Hence the trad. of El-Hasan, HaAdivuwA h`*ihi Alquluwba bi*ikori A@ll~`hu faA_in~ahaA sariyEapu Ald~uvuwri [explained in art. Hdv ]. (Sh, T, A, TA.) duvuwrN attributed to the heart is (assumed tropical:) The having the remembrance of God effaced from it: and attributed to the mind, (assumed tropical:) The being quick to forget. (Sh, T, K.) -A2- davara Al$~ajaru , (K,) inf. n. as above; (TA; [in which, by a strange mistake, Alrjl is put for Al$jr ;]) or ↓ dv~r ; (so in the M, accord. to the TT;) The trees put forth their leaves (M, K, TA) and their branches. (M, TA.)

definition: (tropical:) Much property or wealth;
sourceDefinition: (tropical:) Much property or wealth; or many camels or the like: (T, S, M, K:) or much, or many, of any thing or things: (M:) [the sing. and dual and pl. are alike; as in the case of its syn. diborN or daborN :] you say, [using it as an epithet,] maAlN daborN , (T, S, K,) and maAlaAni davorN , and A^amowaAli davorN : (S, K:) [but sometimes duvuwrN is used as its pl.; for] you say A^aholu davorK and A^aholu duvuwrK : (A 'Obeyd, T:) you also say ↓ maAlN divorN : (T:) and the expression ↓ EasokarN davarN , meaning a numerous army, occurs thus written: (S:) an instance is found in a verse of Imra-el-Keys, where it is thus for the sake of the metre. sourceDefinition: , (S Msb, K, &c.,) inf. n. A_idoraAkN (S, Msb) and mudorakN , (Msb,) He, or it, attained, reached, overtook, or came up with, him, or it: (S, K, TA:) or sought, or pursued, and attained, reached, &c., him, or it: (Msb:) [ dArkhu , also, signifies the same, as shown above:] and ↓ tdArkhu , likewise, [of which Aid~arAakahu is a variation,] is syn. with Adrkhu ; (Jel in lxviii. 49, and KL, * and TA; *) and so is ↓ Aid~arakahu . (TA.) You say, A^adorakotu Alr~ajula and ↓ Aid~arakotuhu [ I attained, reached, overtook, or came up with, the man ]. (IJ, TA.) And ma$ayotu Hat~aY A^adorakotuhu I walked, or went on foot, until I overtook him, or came up with him. (S, TA.) And Ei$otu Hat~aY A^adorakotu zamaAnahu I lived until I attained, or reached, his time. (S, TA.) And A^adorakotu AlfaAy^ita [ I attained, &c., that which was passing away ]. (Mgh.) And Adrkhu bimakoruwhK [ He overtook him, or visited him, with some displeasing, or abominable, or evil, action ]. (M and K in art. wtr . See also 6, in the latter half of the paragraph, in two places: and see 10, first sentence.) And A^adorakaniY Aljahodu [ Difficulty, or distress, &c., overtook me, ensued to me, or came upon me ]; a phrase similar to balaganiY Alkibaru in the Kur [iii. 35]: and so A^adorakotu Aljahoda [ I came to experience difficulty, &c.]; like balagotu mina Alkibari EutiyFA in the Kur [xix. 9]. (Er-Rághib, TA in art. blg .) ― -b2- [Hence, He attained, obtained, or acquired, it; and so ↓ tdArkhu , as is shown in the KL; so too Adrk bihi , for one says,] Adrk bidamihi [ He obtained revenge, or retaliation, for his blood ]. (S in art. wtr .) ― -b3- [Hence also, He perceived it; attained a knowledge of it by any of the senses. ] You say, A^adorakotuhu bibaSariY [ I perceived it by my sight; ] I saw it. (S, TA.) laA tudorikuhu AlA^aboSaAru , in the Kur [vi. 103], means, accord. to some, The eyes [ perceive him not ]: accord. to others, the mental perception comprehendeth not [or attaineth not the knowledge of ] the real nature of his hallowed essence. (TA.) You say also, Adrk EilomiY , meaning My knowledge comprehended that such a thing was a fact. (TA.) ― -b4- [Hence likewise, as an intrans. v., or a trans. v. of which the objective complement is understood,] Adrk also signifies [ He attained a knowledge of the uttermost of a thing; or] his knowledge attained the uttermost of a thing. (TA.) See also 6, in the former half of the paragraph, in two places. ― -b5- Also It (a thing) attained its proper time: (Msb, K:) it attained its final time or state, or its utmost point or degree. (K.) [ He (a boy, and a beast,) attained his perfect, ripe, or mature, state; and in like manner Adrkt is said of a girl: or it is like Adrk as meaning] he (a boy) attained to puberty, (S, Msb,) or to the utmost term of youth. (TA.) It (fruit) attained to ripeness, or maturity; became ripe, or mature; (S Msb;) attained its time, and its utmost degree of ripeness or maturity. (T, TA.) And Adrkt Alqidoru The cooking-pot attained its proper time [ for the cooking of its contents ]. (TA.) And Adrkt Alxamoru [ The wine became mature ]. (Msb and K in art. xmr .) And Adrk maA='u Alr~akiy~api The water of the well reached its darak , i. e. its bottom (Aboo-' Adnán, TA.) ― -b6- Also It passed away and came to an end; came to nought; became exhausted; or failed entirely: (S, K:) said in this sense of flour, or meal: (S:) and thus it has been explained as used in the Kur [xxvii. 68], where it is said, [accord. to one reading,] balo A^adoraka Eilomuhumo fiY AlA=xirapi [ Nay, their knowledge hath entirely failed respecting the world to come ]. (TA. [See also 6.]) Sh mentions this signification as heard by him on no other authority than that of Lth; and Az asserts it to be incorrect: but it has been authorized by more than one of the leading lexicologists, and the language of the Arabs does not forbid it; for it is said of flour, or meal, and in this case can only mean it came to its end, and entirely failed, or became exhausted; and fruits, when they are ripe ( A_i*aA A^adorakoto ) are exposed to coming to nought, and so is everything that has attained to its extreme term; so that the signification of “ coming to nought ” is one of the necessary adjuncts of the meaning of A_idoraAkN . (TA.) [In like manner,] ↓ Aid~araka signifies It (a thing) continued uninterruptedly and then come to nought: (IJ, TA:) and agreeably with this signification is explained the saying in the Kur [xxvi. 61], A_in~aA lamud~arikuwna [ Verily we are coming to nought, by those who read thus instead of lamudorakuwna being overtaken ]. (TA.) ― -b7- You say also, Adrk Alv~amanu Almu$otariYa , meaning [The payment of] the price was, or became, obligatory on the purchaser: this is an ideal reaching, or overtaking. (Msb.)

[See also 6.]) Sh mentions this signification as heard by him on no other authority than that of Lth; and Az asserts it to be incorrect: but it has been authorized by more than one of the leading lexicologists, and the language of the Arabs does not forbid it; for it is said of flour, or meal, and in this case can only mean it came to its end, and entirely failed, or became exhausted; and fruits, when they are ripe ( A_i*aA A^adorakoto ) are exposed to coming to nought, and so is everything that has attained to its extreme term; so that the signification of “ coming to nought ” is one of the necessary adjuncts of the meaning of A_idoraAkN . [In like manner,] ↓ Aid~araka signifies It (a thing) continued uninterruptedly and then come to nought: (IJ, TA:) and agreeably with this signification is explained the saying in the Kur [xxvi. 61], A_in~aA lamud~arikuwna [ Verily we are coming to nought, by those who read thus instead of lamudorakuwna being overtaken ]. (TA.) ― -b7- You say also, Adrk Alv~amanu Almu$otariYa , meaning [The payment of] the price was, or became, obligatory on the purchaser: this is an ideal reaching, or overtaking. (Msb.)

sourceDefinition: i. q. tlAHqwA (S) [i. e.] They attained, reached, overtook, or came up with, one another; as also Aid~aArakuwA , and ↓ Aid~arakuwA ; (Sh, TA;) [or] the last of them attained, reached, overtook, or came up with, the first of them. (S Msb, K, TA.) Hence, in the Kur [vii. 36], (S,) Hat~aY A_i*aA A@d~aArakuwA fiyhaA jamiyEFA [ Until, when they have overtaken one another, or have successively arrived, therein, all together ]: originally tadaArakuwA . (S, K. *) And tdArk Alv~ariyaAna [ The two moistures reached each other; (like AilotaqaY Alv~arayaAni ;) meaning] the moisture of the rain reached the moisture of the earth. (S.) ― -b2- And [hence] tdArk signifies [ It continued, or was carried on, uninterruptedly; it was closely consecutive in its parts, or portions; ] one part, or portion, of it, followed, or was made to follow, another uninterruptedly; said of anything. (TA.) You say, tdArk Als~ayoru [ The course, or pace, or journeying, continued uninterruptedly ]. (S and TA in art. Hfd , &c.) And tdArkt AlA^axobaAru The tidings followed one another closely. (TA.) ― -b3- [Hence, when said of knowledge, meaning, accord. to Fr, It continued unbroken in its sequence or concatenation. ] bali A@d~araAka Eilomuhumo fiY AlA=xirapi (K, TA,) in the Kur [xxvii. 68], (TA,) [virtually] means Nay, they have no knowledge respecting the world to come: (K, TA:) or, as IJ says, their knowledge is hasty, and slight, and not on a sure footing, &c.: Az says that AA read balo A^adoraka [of which an explanation has been given above (see 4)]: that I'Ab is related to have read ↓ balaYA=A^adoraka [&c., i. e. Yea, hath their knowledge reached its end &c.?], as interrogatory, and without tesh-deed: and that, accord. to the reading bl Ad~rAk Fr says that the proper meaning is, [ Nay, ] hath their knowledge continued unbroken so as to extend to the knowledge of the world to come, whether it will be or not be? wherefore is added, balo humo fiY $ak~K minohaA balo humo minohaA Eamuwna : he says also that Ubeí read, A^amo tadaAraka ; and that the Arabs substitute balo for A^amo , and A^amo for balo , when a passage begins with an interrogation: but this explanation of Fr is not clear; the meaning is [said to be] their knowledge shall be unbroken and concurrent [ respecting the world to come ] when the resurrection shall have become a manifest event, and they shall have found themselves to be losers; and the truth of that wherewith they have been threatened shall appear to them when their knowledge thereof will not profit them: accord. to Aboo-Mo'ádh the Grammarian, the readings ↓ balo A^adoraka &c. and bali A@d~aAraka &c. mean the same; i. e. they shall know in the world to come; like the saying in the Kur [xix. 39], A^asomiEo bihimo waA^aboSiro , &c.: and Es-Suddee says of both these readings that the meaning is, their knowledge shall agree, or be in unison, in the world to come; i. e. they shall know in the world to come that that wherewith they have been threatened is true: or, accord. to Mujáhid, the meaning of bali A@d~aAraka Eilomuhumo &c. is said to be, is their knowledge concurrent respecting the world to come? bl being here used in the sense of A^am : (TA:) or it may mean their knowledge hath gone on uninterruptedly until it hath become cut short; from the phrase tdArk banuw fulaAnK meaning The sons of such a one went on uninterruptedly into destruction. (Bd.) -A2- tdArkhu : see 4, in two places. It is used in the [primary] sense of A^adorakahu in the saying in the Kur [lxviii. 49], lawo laA A^ano tadArakahu niEomapN mino rab~ihi lanubi*a biA@loEaraA='i [ Had not favour ( meaning mercy, Jel) from his Lord reached him, or overtaken him, he had certainly been cast upon the bare land ]. (Jel.) ― -b2- [Hence, elliptically, He overtook him, or visited him, with good, or with evil. ] El-Mutanebbee says, A^ana fiY A^um~apK tadaArakahaA A@ll~` hu gariybN kaSaAliHK fiY vamuwdi [ I am among a people ( may God visit them with favour and save them from their meanness, or visit them with destruction so that I may be safe from them,) a stranger, like Sálih among Thamood ]: tdArkhA All~`h is a prayer for the people, meaning All~`h wnj~Ahm mn lwmhm ↓ AdrkhA [i. e. luw^omihimo ]: or it may be an imprecation against them, i. e. All~`h bAlAhlAk liA^anojuwa mnhm ↓ Adrkhm : [each meaning as explained above:] and IJ says that because of this verse the poet was named Almtnb~Y . (W p. 35. [The verse there commences with A^anaA ; but A^ana is required by the metre, and is more approved in every case except the case of a pause.]) It is mostly used in relation to aid, or relief, and benefaction: [so that it signifies He aided, or relieved, him; he benefited him; he repaired his, or its, condition; he repaired, amended, corrected, or rectified, it: ] whence the saying of a poet, tadaArakaniY mino Eavorapi Ald~ahori qaAsimN bimaA $aA='a mino maEoruwfihi AlmutadAriki [ Kásim relieved me, or has relieved me, from the slip of fortune with what he pleased of his relieving, or continuous, beneficence ]. (TA.) [See also, in the first paragraph of art. dq , another example, in a verse of Zuheyr, which is cited in that art. and the present in the TA: and see the syn. talaAfaAhu . Hence,] tadaArakotu maA faAta i. q. Astdrkthu , q. v. (S, Msb, TA.)

definition: [properly] signifies bihi ↓ HaAwala A_idoraAkahu [i.
sourceDefinition: [properly] signifies bihi ↓ HaAwala A_idoraAkahu [i. e. He sought, or endeavoured, to follow up the thing with the thing ]: (K:) as, for instance, AlxaTaA^a biAlS~awaAbi [ the mistake with what was right ]. (TK.) [Hence,] you say, Aisotadorakotu maAfaAta [ I repaired, amended, corrected, or rectified, what had passed neglected by me, or by another; and I supplied what had so passed, or what had escaped me, or another, through inadvertence ]; and ↓ tadaArakotuhu signifies the same [in relation to language and to other things; whereas the former verb is generally restricted to relation to language or to a writer or speaker]. (S, Msb.) You say also, Astdrk Ealayohi qawolahu He corrected, or rectified, what was wrong, or erroneous, in his saying: [but more commonly, he supplied what he had omitted in his saying; generally meaning, what he had omitted through inadvertence: and Aisotadorakotuhu Ealayoh I subjoined it, or appended it, to what he had written, or said, by way of emendation; or, more commonly, as a supplement, i. e., to supply what had escaped him, or what he had neglected: ] and hence, EalaY AlbuxaAriY~i ↓ Almusotadoraku [ The Supplement to ElBukháree; a work supplying omissions of ElBukháree;] by El-Hákim. (TA.) [Thus] AisotidoraAkN signifies The annulling a presumption, or surmise, originating from what has been before said, [ by correcting an error, or errors, or by supplying a defect, or defects, ] in a manner resembling the making an exception. (Kull.) [Hence Harofu A@sotidoraAkK , meaning A particle of emendation, applied to balo , and to l`kin~a or l`kino .]

definition: The act of attaining, reaching, or overtaking;
sourceDefinition: The act of attaining, reaching, or overtaking; syn. laHaAqN ; (K, TA; [in the CK, All~iHAqu is erroneously put for All~aHaAqu ;]) [properly an inf. n. of the unused verb daraka (q. v.), but, having no used verb, said to be] a noun from AlA_idoraAku [with which it is syn.], (TA,) or a noun from A^adorakotu Al$~aYo'a ; as also ↓ darokN : and hence DamaAnN Ald~araki [which see in what follows]. (Msb.) [Hence,] laA taxaAfu darakFA , in the Kur [xx. 80.], means Thou shalt not fear Pharaoh's overtaking thee. (TA.) One says also AlT~arydapi ↓ farasN daroku , meaning A horse that overtakes what is hunted; like as they said farasN qayodu AlA^awaAbidi . (TA.) ― -b2- ― -b3- Also The attainment, or acquisition, of an object of want: and the seeking the attainment or acquisition thereof: as in the saying, bak~iro fafiyhi darakN [ Be thou early; for therein is attainment, &c.]: and ↓ darokN signifies the same. (Lth, TA.) [Hence, perhaps,] yawomu Ald~arika : this was [a day of contest] between El-Ows and El-Khazraj: (K:) thought to be so by IDrd. (TA.) ― -b4- And i. q. tabiEapN [i. e. A consequence; generally meaning an evil consequence: and perhaps it also means here a claim which one seeks to obtain for an injury ]: as also ↓ darokN . (S, K.) One says, maA laHiqaka mino darakK faEalaY~i xalaASuhu (S, TA) and ↓ mn darokK [i. e. Whatever evil consequence ensue to thee, on me be the compensation thereof ]: in the A, mA A^adorakahu mn darakK fElY~ xlASh i. e. maA yaloHaquhu mino tabiEapK [ Whatever evil consequence ensue to it, &c.; relating to a thing sold]. (TA.) And hence DamaAnu Ald~araki in the case of a claim for indemnification for a fault of a defect or an imperfection in a thing sold [meaning either Responsibility, or indemnification, (see DamaAnN ,) for evil consequence ]: (TA in the present art:) or this means [ indemnification for evil consequence in a sale; i. e., virtually,] the returning of the price to the purchaser on the occasion of requirement by the thing sold: the vulgar say incorrectly [ DamaAn darak , and still more incorrectly] DumaAn darak [generally meaning thereby I sell this, or I purchase this, on the condition of responsibility, or indemnification, for any fault or defect or imperfection that may be found in it]: (TA in art. Dmn :) [and in this manner DamaAnu Ald~araki may be correctly rendered; for] darakN also signifies a fault or a defect or an imperfection [in a thing sold]; for instance, in a slave that is sold. (TA in art. Ehd .) [In the KT, Ald~araku is also explained as signifying The purchaser's taking from the seller a pledge for the price that he has given him, in fear that the thing sold may require it: but this seems to be an explanation of the case in which the word is used; not of the word itself.] -A2- Also A rope, (M, K,) or a piece of rope, (S,) that is tied upon the [ lower ] extremity of the main rope (S, M, K) of a well, to the cross pieces of wood of the bucket, (S,) so as to be that which is next the water, (S, M, K,) in order that the main rope may not rot (S, M) in the drawing of water: (M:) or a doubled rope that is tied to the cross pieces of wood of the bucket, and then to the main wellrope: (Az, TA:) and ↓ darokN signifies the same. (K. [But only darakN is authorized by the TA in this sense.]) [See also karabN .] ― -b2- Also, and ↓ darokN , The bottom, or lowest depth, (Sh, T, S, M, K,) of a thing, (T, M, K,) as of the sea and the like, (T,) or of anything deep, as a well and the like: (Sh:) pl. A^adoraAkN , (K,) a pl. of both, of a form frequent and analogous with respect to the former, but extr. with respect to the latter; and darakaAtN also. (TA.) And A stage of Hell: (IAar:) a stage downwards: (MA:) or stages downwards; like darakaAtN : (B:) opposed to darajN (MA, B) and darajaAtN , (B,) which are upwards: wherefore, (MA, B,) the abodes of Hell, or the stages thereof, are termed darakaAtN ; (AO, S, MA, K, B;) [Golius and Freytag give darakapN as its sing.; the former as from the S, and the latter as from the K, in neither of which it is found;] and those of Paradise, darajaAtN . (S, MA, B.) It is said in the Kur [iv. 144], A_in~a A@lomunaAfiqiyna fiYA@ld~araki A@loA^asofali mina A@ln~aAri [ Verily the hypocrites shall be in the lowest stage of the fire of Hell]: here the Koofees, except two, read ↓ fY Ald~aroki . (TA.) ― -b3- [Golius gives another signification, “ Pars terræ, ” as on the authority of the S and K, in neither of which it is found.]

definition: an epithet from A^adoraka , (S, Kudot;
sourceDefinition: an epithet from A^adoraka , (S, Kudot;,) applied to a man, (K,) and signifying kaviyru AlA_idoraAki [i. e. One who attains, reaches, or overtakes, &c., much, or often: and also having much, or great, or strong, perception: as will be seen from what follows]: (S, TA:) and so ↓ mudorikN [expressly said in the TA to signify kvyr AlAdrAk , though why it should have this signification as well as that (which it certainly has) of simply attaining &c., I cannot see,] and ↓ mudorikapN : (K, TA:) the last explained by Lh as signifying sariyEu AlA_idoraAki [i. e. quick in attaining, &c.]. (TA.) Keys Ibn-Rifá'ah says, ↓ waSaAHibu Alwitori layosa Ald~ahora mudorikahu EinodiY waA_in~iY ladar~aAkN biA^awotaAri [ And he who has a claim for blood-revenge is not ever an attainer of it with (meaning from ) me; but verily I am one who often attains bloodrevenges ]. (IB.) Seldom does faE~aAlN come from A^afoEala ; but they sometimes said Has~aAsN dar~aAkN [i. e. Having much, or great, or strong, perception ]; it being [in this instance] a dialectal syn. [of Hs~As ], or thus for conformity: (S:) it is said to be the only instance of faE~aAlN from A^afoEala except jab~aArN and saA^~=rN ; [and some other instances might be added; but all of them require consideration:] accord. to IB, dr~Ak is from the unused verb daraka . (TA.)

definition: [ A certain kind of palm-trees;
sourceDefinition: [ A certain kind of palm-trees; ] i. q. xiSaAbN [not as meaning “ palm-trees having much fruit, ” but as an appellation applied by the people of El-Bahreyn to the palm-trees which others call daqalN : see art. xSb ]: (S, O, TA:) in the K, AlxiDaAbu is erroneously put for AlxiSaAbu : (TA:) n. un. with p : (S:) Az says that daqalN signifies species ( A^alowaAnN , of which the sing. is lawonN , [but here meaning varieties, ]) of palm-trees; and the dates thereof are bad, though the daqalap may be abundant in fruit; and some have red dates, and some have black; the body of the dates being small, and the stones being large: (TA:) accord. to AHn, the term daqalN is applied to any palmtrees [ of which the varieties are ] unknown: the n. un. daqalapN is syn. with xaSobapN , of which the pl. is xiSaAbN : and what are termed A^adoqaAlN [pl. of daqalN ] are the worst of palm-trees, and their dates are the worst of dates. (O, TA.) ― -b2- Also [The fruit of the trees thus called; described above;] the worst of dates: (JK, S, Msb, K:) or a bad kind of dates: (Mgh:) or dates of which the kinds are unknown: (M, K:) accord. to EsSarakustee, the fruit of the dawom : n. un. with p . definition: It buzzed, or made a buzzing sound;
sourceDefinition: It buzzed, or made a buzzing sound; syn. Saw~ata , and Tan~a , (K,) and TanoTana ; (Sh, T, TA;) as also ↓ dan~a , and ↓ dn~n ; said of the fly, (K,) [and of the bee, and of the hornet, and the like; for] danodanapN [inf. n. of danodana ] (Lth, T, M, K) and daniynN [inf. n. of ↓ dan~a ] (Lth, T, M) and ↓ dinodinN [a simple subst.] (M) signify the buzzing ( Sawot , Lth, T, M, K) of the fly, (M, K,) or the bee, (Lth, T,) and the hornet, (Lth, T, M, K,) and the like. (M.) ― -b2- And [hence,] He (a man) spoke in a low, gentle, or soft, tone, so that his speech was not understood; (A'Obeyd, K, TA;) [as also ↓ dan~a ; for] danodanapN [inf. n. of the former] (A'Obeyd, T, S, M, K) and daniynN [inf. n. of ↓ dan~a ] and ↓ dinodinN (M, K) signify the speaking in a low, gentle, or soft, tone, (A'Obeyd, T, S,) or in the manner termed hayonamapN , (M, K,) so that the speech is not understood : (A'Obeyd, T, S, M:) or danodanapN signifies [merely] the speaking in a low, or faint, tone : (M:) accord. to IAth, it is a little above what is termed hayonamapN . (TA.) A poet says, nudanodinu mavola danodanapi Al*~ubaAbi [ We buzz in our speech like the buzzing of the fly ]. (Sh, T.) And it is said in a trad., HawolahaA nudanodinu , (S,) or HawolahumaA , (M, JM, TA,) which is thus explained: the Prophet asked an Arab of the desert, “ What dost thou say in the ta$ah~ud ? ” [see this word, which means the repetition of a form of words at the close of the ordinary prayers:] and he answered, “ I ask of God Paradise, and seek protection of Him from the fire [of Hell]: but as to thy danodanap and the danodanap of Mo'ádh, I do not approve it: ” and the Prophet said, HawolahumaA nudanodinu ; (M, JM; *) i. e. [ We speak with a low, or faint, voice ] about those two things, namely, the seeking Paradise and the praying for protection from the fire [of Hell]; and on account of them: (JM:) accord. to some, it is from danodana Hawola AlmaA='i He went round about the water: [hence it may mean we utter our prayer respecting them with a low, or faint, sound, as though we were buzzing round about them like flies; seeking to enter the one, and to keep outside the other:] As says that it may be from the signification of the sound [of buzzing], or from that of going round about: (TA:) or, accord. to one relation, the Prophet said, EanohumaA nudanodinu [ From a consideration of them we utter our prayer with a low, or faint, voice; ] i. e. our danodanapu arises from them; and is because of them: and hence, (JM,) danodana means also He (a man, JM) went to and fro in one place. (JM, TA.)

definition: is said by Aboo-'Alee to be originally *aYo ;
sourceDefinition: is said by Aboo-'Alee to be originally *aYo ; the Y , though quiescent, being changed into A : (M:) or it is originally *ayaY or *awaY ; the final radical letter being elided: some say that the original medial radical letter is Y because it has been heard to be pronounced with imáleh [and so it is now pronounced in Egypt]; but others say that it is w , and this is the more agreeable with analogy. (Msb.) It is a noun of indication, [properly meaning This, but sometimes, when repeated, better rendered that, ] relating to an object of the masc. gender, (S, M, K,) such as is near: (I'Ak p. 36:) or it relates to what is distant [accord. to some, and therefore should always be rendered that ]; and h`*aA , [which see in what follows,] to what is near: (K in art. haA : [but the former is generally held to relate to what is near, like the latter:]) or it is a noun denoting anything indicated that is seen by the speaker and the person addressed: the noun in it is *a , or * alone: and it is a noun of which the signification is vague and unknown until it is explained by what follows it, as when you say *aA Alr~ajulu [ This man ], and *aA Alfarasa [ This horse ]: and the nom. and accus. and gen. are all alike: (T:) the fem. is *iY (T, S, M, K, but omitted in the CK) and *iho , (S, M, K, but omitted in the CK,) the latter used in the case of a pause, (S,) with a quiescent h , which is a substitute for the Y , not a sign of the fem. gender, (S, M,) as it is in TaloHaho and Hamozaho , in which it is changed into p when followed by a conjunctive alif, for in this case the h in *ih remains unchanged [but is meksoorah, as it is also in other cases of connexion with a following word]; and one says also *hiY ; (M;) and taA and tiho : (S and K &c. in art. tA :) for the dual you say *aAni and taAni ; (M;) *aAni is the dual form of *aA (T, S) [and taAni is that of taA used in the place of *iY ]; i. e., you indicate the masc. dual by *aAni in the nom. case, and *ayoni in the accus. and gen.; and the fem. dual you indicate by taAni in the nom. case, and tayoni in the accus. and gen.: (I'Ak p. 36:) the pl. is A^ulaA='i [or A^ulaA='i ] (T, S, and I'Ak ib.) in the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, (I'Ak,) and A^uwlaY [or A^ulaY ] (T, I'Ak) in the dial. of Temeem; each both masc. and fem. (I'Ak ib. [See art. AlY .]) You say, *aA A^axuwka [ This is thy brother ]: and *iYA^uxotuka [ This is thy sister ]: (T:) and laAA=tiyka fiY *iY Als~anapi [ I will not come to thee in this year ]; like as you say fY h`*ihi Als~anapi and fY h`*iY Als~anapi ; not fY *aA Als~anapi , because *A is always masc. (As, T.) And you say, *aAni A^axawaAka [ These two are thy two brothers ]: and taAni A^uxotaAka [ These two are thy two sisters ]. (T.) And A^uwlaA='i A_ixowatuka [ These are thy brothers ]: and A^uwlaA='i A^axawaAtuka [ These are thy sisters ]: thus making no difference between the masc. and the fem. in the pl. (T.) ― -b2- The haA that is used to give notice, to a person addressed, of something about to be said to him, is prefixed to *aA [and to *iY &c.], (T, S, M, K,) and is a particle without any meaning but inception: (T:) thus you say h`*aA , (T, S, M,) and some say h`*aAA , adding another A ; (Ks, T;) fem. h`*iY , (T, S, M,) and [more commonly] h`*iho in the case of a pause, (M,) and h`*ihi in other cases, (T, S,) and haAtaA , and some say h`*aAti , but this is unusual and disapproved: (T:) dual h`*aAni for the masc., and haAtaAni for the fem.; (T;) said by IJ to be not properly duals, but nouns formed to denote duals; (M;) and many of the Arabs say h`*aAn~i ; (T;) some, also, make h`*aAni indecl., like the sing. *aA , reading [in the Kur xx. 66] A_in~a h`*aAni lasaAHiraAni [ Verily these two are enchanters ], and it has been said that this is of the dial. of Belhárith [or Benu-l-Hárith] Ibn-Kaab; but others make it decl., reading A_in~a h`*aAyoni lasaAHiraAni : (S, TA: [see, however, what has been said respecting this phrase voce A_in~a :]) the pl. is h`w^ulaA in the dial. of Temeem, with a quiescent A ; and h`w^ulaA='i in the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, with medd and hemz and khafd; and h`w^ulaA='K in the dial. of Benoo- 'Okeyl, with medd and hemz and tenween. (AZ, T.) The Arabs also say, laA haA A@ll~`hi *aA , introducing the name of God between haA and *aA ; meaning No, by God; this is [my oath, or] that by which I swear. (T.) In the following verse, of Jemeel, waA^ataY SawaAHibuhaA faqulona h`*aA A@l~a*iY manaHa Almawad~apa gayoranaA wajafaAnaA [it is said that] ha*aA is for A^a*aA , (M,) i. e., h is here substituted for the interrogative hemzeh (S * and K in art. hA ) [so that the meaning is, And her female companions came, and said, Is this he who gave love to other than us, and treated us unkindly? ]: or, as some assert, ha*aA is here used for h`*aA , the A being suppressed for the sake of the measure. (El-Bedr El-Karáfee, TA in art. hA .) ― -b3- One says also *aAka , (T, S, M, K,) affixing to *aA the k of allocution, [q. v., meaning That, ] relating to an object that is distant, (T, *, S, and I'Ak p. 36,) or, accord. to general opinion, to that which occupies a middle place between the near and the distant, (I'Ak pp. 36 and 37,) and this k has no place in desinential syntax; (S, and I'Ak p. 36;) it does not occupy the place of a gen. nor of an accus., but is only affixed to *A to denote the distance of *A from the person addressed: (T:) for the fem. you say tiyka (T, S) and taAka ; (S and K in art. tA , q. v.;) but not *iyka , for this is wrong, (T, S,) and is used only by the vulgar: (T:) for the dual you say *aAnika (T, S) and *ayonika , as in the phrases jaA='aniY *aAnika Alr~ajulaAni [ Those two men came to me ] and raA^ayotu *ayonuka Alr~ajulayoni , [ I saw those two men ]; (S;) and some say *aAn~ika , with teshdeed, (T, S,) [accord. to J] for the purpose of corroboration, and to add to the letters of the noun, (S,) but [accord. to others] this is dual of *`lika , [which see in what follows,] the second n being a substitute for the l ; (T on the authority of Zj and others;) and some say taAn~ika also, with tesh-deed, (T, S,) as well as taAnika : (T in this art., and S and K in art. tA , but there omitted in some copies of the S:) the pl. is [ A^uwlaAka and] A^uwl`y^ika . (T, S.) haA is also prefixed to *aAka ; so that you say, h`*aAka zayodN [ That is Zeyd ]: (S, TA:) and in like manner, for the fem., you say haAtiyka and haAtaAka : (S and K in art. tA :) but it is not prefixed [to the dual nor] to A^uwl`y^ika . (S.) ― -b4- You also add l in *aAka , (T, S, M, K,) as a corroborative; (TA;) so that you say *`lika , [meaning That, ] (T, S, M, K,) relating to an object that is distant, by common consent; (I'Ak pp. 36 and 37;) or hemzeh, saying *aAy^ika , (K,) but some say that this is a mispronunciation: (TA in art. *wY :) for the fem. you say tiloka and taAlika : the dual of *`lika is *aAn~ika , mentioned above; and that of the fem. is vaAn~ika : (T: [and in the K in art. tA , taAlika is also mentioned as a dual, as well as a sing.:]) and the pl. is A^uwlaAlika . (S and M and K voce A^uwlaY or A^ulaY or A^ulaA . [See art. AlY .]) haA is not prefixed to *`lika (S) nor to tiloka [nor to A^uwlaAlika ] because, as IB says, the l denotes the remoteness of that which is indicated and the hA denotes its nearness, so that the two are incompatible. (TA in art. tA .) ― -b5- In the saying in the Kur [ii. 256, the Verse of the Throne], mano *aA Al~a*iY ya$ofaEu Einodahu A_il~aA biA_i*onihi , (T, TA,) accord. to Th and Mbr, (TA,) h`*aA is syn. with *A [so that the meaning is, Who is this that shall intercede with Him but by his permission? ]: (T, TA:) or it may be here redundant [so that the meaning is, Who is he that &c.? ]. (Kull.) ― -b6- It is sometimes syn. with Aal~a*iY . (T, S, M.) So in the saying, maA *aA raA^ayota [ What is it that thou sawest? ]; to which one may answer, mataAEN HasanN [A goodly commodity]. (Sb, S.) And so in the Kur [ii. 216], wa yasoA^aluwnaka maA maA *aA yunofiquwna [ And they ask thee what amount of their property is it that they shall expend in alms]; (T, M, TA;) accord. to those who make the reply to be in the nom. case; for this shows that mA is [virtually] in the nom. case as an inchoative, and *A is its enunciative, and ynfqwn is the complement of *A ; and that mA and *A are not to be regarded as one word: [or] this is the preferable way of explanation in the opinion of Sb, though he allowed the other way, [that of regarding mA and *A as one word, together constituting an inchoative, and ynfqwn as its enunciative, (see Ham p. 521,)] with [the reply in] the nom. case: (M:) and h`*aA , also, is used in the same sense: (TA:) so too *A in maA *aA huwa and mano *aA huwa may be considered as syn. with Al*Y ; but it is preferable to regard it as redundant. (Kull.) ― -b7- It is [said to be] redundant also in other instances: for ex., in the trad. of Jereer, as related by Aboo-'Amr Ez-Záhid, who says that it is so in this instance: yaToluEu Ealayokumo rajulN mino *iY yamanK EalaY wajohihi masoHapN mino *iY mulokK [ There will come to you a man from El-Yemen, having upon his face an indication of dominion ]. (TA. [But this evidently belongs to art. *uw ; in which see a similar ex. ( A^atayonaA *aA yamanK ). See also other exs. there.]) ― -b8- [ ka*aA lit. means Like this: and hence, thus: as also h`ka*aA . ― -b9- It is also often used as one word, and, as such, is made the complement of a prefixed noun; as in sanapa ka*aA and fiY sanapi ka*aA In such a year. See also art. ka*aA : and see the letter k .] ― -b10- h`*aA is sometimes used to express contempt, and mean estimation; as in the saying of 'Áïsheh respecting 'Abd-Allah Ibn- 'Amr Ibn-'Abbás, yaA EajabFA liA@boni EamorKw h`*aA [ O wonder (meaning how I wonder ) at Ibn-'Amr, this fellow!]. (Kitáb el-Miftáh, cited in De Sacy's “ Gram. Ar., ” 2nd ed., i. 442.) [ yaA h`*aA often occurs as addressed to one who is held in mean estimation: it is like the Greek ὦ οὗτος , and virtually like the vulgar Arabic expression yaA A^anota , and the Latin heus tu; agreeably with which it may be rendered O thou; meaning O thou fellow; an appellation denoting mean estimation being understood: in the contrary case, one says yaA fataY . See also, in what follows, a usage of *aAka and *`lika . ― -b11- h`*aA in a letter and the like is introduced when the writer breaks off, turning to a new subject; and means “ This is all that I had to say on the subject to which, it relates: ” what follows it is commenced with the conjunction wa .] ― -b12- One says, layosa bi*aAka [and layosa bi*`lika ], meaning It is not approved: for, [like as a person held in mean estimation is indicated by h`*aA , which denotes a thing that is near, so,] on account of its high degree of estimation, a thing that is approved is indicated by that whereby one indicates a thing that is remote. (Kull voce lys .) [See also what next follows.] ― -b13- *`lika AlkitaAbu in the Kur ii. 1 is said by Zj to mean h`*aA AlkitaAbu [ This book ]: but others say that *lk is here used because the book is remote [from others] in respect of highness and greatness of rank. (TA.) ― -b14- ka*`lika [lit. Like that, often means so, or in like manner: and ― -b15- ] Let that suffice [thee or] you. (TA in art. *Er , from a trad.) ― -b16- The dim. of *aA is *ay~aA : (T, S, M:) you form no dim. of the fem. *iY , using in its stead that of taA , (S,) which is tay~aA : (T:) the dim. of the dual [ *aAni ] is *ay~aAni : (S:) and that of [the pl.] A^uwlaA='i [and A^uwlaY ] is A^uwlay~aA='i [and A^uwlay~aA ]: (T:) ― -b17- that of h`*aA is *ay~aA , like that of *aA ; [and you may say h`*ay~aA also; for] that of h`w^ulaA='i is h`w^ulay~aA='i : (T:) ― -b18- that of *aAka is *ay~aAka : (S, K: *) and that of taAka is tay~aAka : (K in art. tA :) ― -b19- that of *`lika is *ay~aAlika : (S, K: *) and that of tiloka is tay~aAlika . (S.) A rájiz says, A^awo taHolifiY birab~ika AlEaliY~i A_in~iY A^abuw *ay~aAliki AlS~abiY~i [ Or thou shalt swear by thy Lord, the High, that I am the father of that little child ]: (S, TA:) he was an Arab who came from a journey, and found that his wife had given birth to a boy whom he disacknowledged. (TA.) -A2- *aA is also the accus. case of *uw , q. v.

rawSourceText: is said by Aboo-'Alee to be originally *aYo ; the Y , though quiescent, being changed into A : (M:) or it is originally *ayaY or *awaY ; the final radical letter being elided: some say that the original medial radical letter is Y because it has been heard to be pronounced with imáleh [and so it is now pronounced in Egypt]; but others say that it is w , and this is the more agreeable with analogy. (Msb.) It is a noun of indication, [properly meaning This, but sometimes, when repeated, better rendered that, ] relating to an object of the masc. gender, (S, M, K,) such as is near: (I'Ak p. 36:) or it relates to what is distant [accord. to some, and therefore should always be rendered that ]; and h`*aA , [which see in what follows,] to what is near: (K in art. haA : [but the former is generally held to relate to what is near, like the latter:]) or it is a noun denoting anything indicated that is seen by the speaker and the person addressed: the noun in it is *a , or * alone: and it is a noun of which the signification is vague and unknown until it is explained by what follows it, as when you say *aA Alr~ajulu [ This man ], and *aA Alfarasa [ This horse ]: and the nom. and accus. and gen. are all alike: (T:) the fem. is *iY (T, S, M, K, but omitted in the CK) and *iho , (S, M, K, but omitted in the CK,) the latter used in the case of a pause, (S,) with a quiescent h , which is a substitute for the Y , not a sign of the fem. gender, (S, M,) as it is in TaloHaho and Hamozaho , in which it is changed into p when followed by a conjunctive alif, for in this case the h in *ih remains unchanged [but is meksoorah, as it is also in other cases of connexion with a following word]; and one says also *hiY ; (M;) and taA and tiho : (S and K &c. in art. tA :) for the dual you say *aAni and taAni ; (M;) *aAni is the dual form of *aA (T, S) [and taAni is that of taA used in the place of *iY ]; i. e., you indicate the masc. dual by *aAni in the nom. case, and *ayoni in the accus. and gen.; and the fem. dual you indicate by taAni in the nom. case, and tayoni in the accus. and gen.: (I'Ak p. 36:) the pl. is A^ulaA='i [or A^ulaA='i ] (T, S, and I'Ak ib.) in the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, (I'Ak,) and A^uwlaY [or A^ulaY ] (T, I'Ak) in the dial. of Temeem; each both masc. and fem. (I'Ak ib. [See art. AlY .]) You say, *aA A^axuwka [ This is thy brother ]: and *iYA^uxotuka [ This is thy sister ]: (T:) and laAA=tiyka fiY *iY Als~anapi [ I will not come to thee in this year ]; like as you say fY h`*ihi Als~anapi and fY h`*iY Als~anapi ; not fY *aA Als~anapi , because *A is always masc. (As, T.) And you say, *aAni A^axawaAka [ These two are thy two brothers ]: and taAni A^uxotaAka [ These two are thy two sisters ]. (T.) And A^uwlaA='i A_ixowatuka [ These are thy brothers ]: and A^uwlaA='i A^axawaAtuka [ These are thy sisters ]: thus making no difference between the masc. and the fem. in the pl. (T.) ― -b2- The haA that is used to give notice, to a person addressed, of something about to be said to him, is prefixed to *aA [and to *iY &c.], (T, S, M, K,) and is a particle without any meaning but inception: (T:) thus you say h`*aA , (T, S, M,) and some say h`*aAA , adding another A ; (Ks, T;) fem. h`*iY , (T, S, M,) and [more commonly] h`*iho in the case of a pause, (M,) and h`*ihi in other cases, (T, S,) and haAtaA , and some say h`*aAti , but this is unusual and disapproved: (T:) dual h`*aAni for the masc., and haAtaAni for the fem.; (T;) said by IJ to be not properly duals, but nouns formed to denote duals; (M;) and many of the Arabs say h`*aAn~i ; (T;) some, also, make h`*aAni indecl., like the sing. *aA , reading [in the Kur xx. 66] A_in~a h`*aAni lasaAHiraAni [ Verily these two are enchanters ], and it has been said that this is of the dial. of Belhárith [or Benu-l-Hárith] Ibn-Kaab; but others make it decl., reading A_in~a h`*aAyoni lasaAHiraAni : (S, TA: [see, however, what has been said respecting this phrase voce A_in~a :]) the pl. is h`w^ulaA in the dial. of Temeem, with a quiescent A ; and h`w^ulaA='i in the dial. of the people of El-Hijáz, with medd and hemz and khafd; and h`w^ulaA='K in the dial. of Benoo- 'Okeyl, with medd and hemz and tenween. (AZ, T.) The Arabs also say, laA haA A@ll~`hi *aA , introducing the name of God between haA and *aA ; meaning No, by God; this is [my oath, or] that by which I swear. (T.) In the following verse, of Jemeel, waA^ataY SawaAHibuhaA faqulona h`*aA A@l~a*iY manaHa Almawad~apa gayoranaA wajafaAnaA [it is said that] ha*aA is for A^a*aA , (M,) i. e., h is here substituted for the interrogative hemzeh (S * and K in art. hA ) [so that the meaning is, And her female companions came, and said, Is this he who gave love to other than us, and treated us unkindly? ]: or, as some assert, ha*aA is here used for h`*aA , the A being suppressed for the sake of the measure. (El-Bedr El-Karáfee, TA in art. hA .) ― -b3- One says also *aAka , (T, S, M, K,) affixing to *aA the k of allocution, [q. v., meaning That, ] relating to an object that is distant, (T, *, S, and I'Ak p. 36,) or, accord. to general opinion, to that which occupies a middle place between the near and the distant, (I'Ak pp. 36 and 37,) and this k has no place in desinential syntax; (S, and I'Ak p. 36;) it does not occupy the place of a gen. nor of an accus., but is only affixed to *A to denote the distance of *A from the person addressed: (T:) for the fem. you say tiyka (T, S) and taAka ; (S and K in art. tA , q. v.;) but not *iyka , for this is wrong, (T, S,) and is used only by the vulgar: (T:) for the dual you say *aAnika (T, S) and *ayonika , as in the phrases jaA='aniY *aAnika Alr~ajulaAni [ Those two men came to me ] and raA^ayotu *ayonuka Alr~ajulayoni , [ I saw those two men ]; (S;) and some say *aAn~ika , with teshdeed, (T, S,) [accord. to J] for the purpose of corroboration, and to add to the letters of the noun, (S,) but [accord. to others] this is dual of *`lika , [which see in what follows,] the second n being a substitute for the l ; (T on the authority of Zj and others;) and some say taAn~ika also, with tesh-deed, (T, S,) as well as taAnika : (T in this art., and S and K in art. tA , but there omitted in some copies of the S:) the pl. is [ A^uwlaAka and] A^uwl`y^ika . (T, S.) haA is also prefixed to *aAka ; so that you say, h`*aAka zayodN [ That is Zeyd ]: (S, TA:) and in like manner, for the fem., you say haAtiyka and haAtaAka : (S and K in art. tA :) but it is not prefixed [to the dual nor] to A^uwl`y^ika . (S.) ― -b4- You also add l in *aAka , (T, S, M, K,) as a corroborative; (TA;) so that you say *`lika , [meaning That, ] (T, S, M, K,) relating to an object that is distant, by common consent; (I'Ak pp. 36 and 37;) or hemzeh, saying *aAy^ika , (K,) but some say that this is a mispronunciation: (TA in art. *wY :) for the fem. you say tiloka and taAlika : the dual of *`lika is *aAn~ika , mentioned above; and that of the fem. is vaAn~ika : (T: [and in the K in art. tA , taAlika is also mentioned as a dual, as well as a sing.:]) and the pl. is A^uwlaAlika . (S and M and K voce A^uwlaY or A^ulaY or A^ulaA . [See art. AlY .]) haA is not prefixed to *`lika (S) nor to tiloka [nor to A^uwlaAlika ] because, as IB says, the l denotes the remoteness of that which is indicated and the hA denotes its nearness, so that the two are incompatible. (TA in art. tA .) ― -b5- In the saying in the Kur [ii. 256, the Verse of the Throne], mano *aA Al~a*iY ya$ofaEu Einodahu A_il~aA biA_i*onihi , (T, TA,) accord. to Th and Mbr, (TA,) h`*aA is syn. with *A [so that the meaning is, Who is this that shall intercede with Him but by his permission? ]: (T, TA:) or it may be here redundant [so that the meaning is, Who is he that &c.? ]. (Kull.) ― -b6- It is sometimes syn. with Aal~a*iY . (T, S, M.) So in the saying, maA *aA raA^ayota [ What is it that thou sawest? ]; to which one may answer, mataAEN HasanN [A goodly commodity]. (Sb, S.) And so in the Kur [ii. 216], wa yasoA^aluwnaka maA maA *aA yunofiquwna [ And they ask thee what amount of their property is it that they shall expend in alms]; (T, M, TA;) accord. to those who make the reply to be in the nom. case; for this shows that mA is [virtually] in the nom. case as an inchoative, and *A is its enunciative, and ynfqwn is the complement of *A ; and that mA and *A are not to be regarded as one word: [or] this is the preferable way of explanation in the opinion of Sb, though he allowed the other way, [that of regarding mA and *A as one word, together constituting an inchoative, and ynfqwn as its enunciative, (see Ham p. 521,)] with [the reply in] the nom. case: (M:) and h`*aA , also, is used in the same sense: (TA:) so too *A in maA *aA huwa and mano *aA huwa may be considered as syn. with Al*Y ; but it is preferable to regard it as redundant. (Kull.) ― -b7- It is [said to be] redundant also in other instances: for ex., in the trad. of Jereer, as related by Aboo-'Amr Ez-Záhid, who says that it is so in this instance: yaToluEu Ealayokumo rajulN mino *iY yamanK EalaY wajohihi masoHapN mino *iY mulokK [ There will come to you a man from El-Yemen, having upon his face an indication of dominion ]. (TA. [But this evidently belongs to art. *uw ; in which see a similar ex. ( A^atayonaA *aA yamanK ). See also other exs. there.]) ― -b8- [ ka*aA lit. means Like this: and hence, thus: as also h`ka*aA . ― -b9- It is also often used as one word, and, as such, is made the complement of a prefixed noun; as in sanapa ka*aA and fiY sanapi ka*aA In such a year. See also art. ka*aA : and see the letter k .] ― -b10- h`*aA is sometimes used to express contempt, and mean estimation; as in the saying of 'Áïsheh respecting 'Abd-Allah Ibn- 'Amr Ibn-'Abbás, yaA EajabFA liA@boni EamorKw h`*aA [ O wonder (meaning how I wonder ) at Ibn-'Amr, this fellow!]. (Kitáb el-Miftáh, cited in De Sacy's “ Gram. Ar., ” 2nd ed., i. 442.) [ yaA h`*aA often occurs as addressed to one who is held in mean estimation: it is like the Greek ὦ οὗτος , and virtually like the vulgar Arabic expression yaA A^anota , and the Latin heus tu; agreeably with which it may be rendered O thou; meaning O thou fellow; an appellation denoting mean estimation being understood: in the contrary case, one says yaA fataY . See also, in what follows, a usage of *aAka and *`lika . ― -b11- h`*aA in a letter and the like is introduced when the writer breaks off, turning to a new subject; and means “ This is all that I had to say on the subject to which, it relates: ” what follows it is commenced with the conjunction wa .] ― -b12- One says, layosa bi*aAka [and layosa bi*`lika ], meaning It is not approved: for, [like as a person held in mean estimation is indicated by h`*aA , which denotes a thing that is near, so,] on account of its high degree of estimation, a thing that is approved is indicated by that whereby one indicates a thing that is remote. (Kull voce lys .) [See also what next follows.] ― -b13- *`lika AlkitaAbu in the Kur ii. 1 is said by Zj to mean h`*aA AlkitaAbu [ This book ]: but others say that *lk is here used because the book is remote [from others] in respect of highness and greatness of rank. (TA.) ― -b14- ka*`lika [lit. Like that, often means so, or in like manner: and ― -b15- ] Let that suffice [thee or] you. (TA in art. *Er , from a trad.) ― -b16- The dim. of *aA is *ay~aA : (T, S, M:) you form no dim. of the fem. *iY , using in its stead that of taA , (S,) which is tay~aA : (T:) the dim. of the dual [ *aAni ] is *ay~aAni : (S:) and that of [the pl.] A^uwlaA='i [and A^uwlaY ] is A^uwlay~aA='i [and A^uwlay~aA ]: (T:) ― -b17- that of h`*aA is *ay~aA , like that of *aA ; [and you may say h`*ay~aA also; for] that of h`w^ulaA='i is h`w^ulay~aA='i : (T:) ― -b18- that of *aAka is *ay~aAka : (S, K: *) and that of taAka is tay~aAka : (K in art. tA :) ― -b19- that of *`lika is *ay~aAlika : (S, K: *) and that of tiloka is tay~aAlika . (S.) A rájiz says, A^awo taHolifiY birab~ika AlEaliY~i A_in~iY A^abuw *ay~aAliki AlS~abiY~i [ Or thou shalt swear by thy Lord, the High, that I am the father of that little child ]: (S, TA:) he was an Arab who came from a journey, and found that his wife had given birth to a boy whom he disacknowledged. (TA.) -A2- *aA is also the accus. case of *uw , q. v.

sourceDefinition: and ↓ *ur~uwHN , (S, A, K,) the latter (respecting which see below) anomalous in form, (TA,) and ↓ *ar~uwHN , (K,) agreeably with analogy, (TA,) and ↓ *ir~ayHN (K) and ↓ *ar~aAHN (Fr) and ↓ *aruwHN and ↓ *uraAHN (K) and ↓ *uraHN (IO) and ↓ *ur~aHN (K) and ↓ *ur~uwHapN and ↓ *ir~ayHapN (ISd) and ↓ *ariyHapN and ↓ *uronuwHN (K) and ↓ *aronuwHN , accord. to some, (TA,) and ↓ *uronuwHapN (ISd) and ↓ *uraHoraHN and ↓ *uruHoruHN , and ↓ the second letter [in the latter of these two forms, or in both,] is sometimes doubled by teshdeed, (K,) and sometimes the second r is meksoorah, and the termination p is also added thereto, (ISd,) and ↓ A^abuw *rHrHK and ↓ Abw *aroyaAHK and ↓ Abw *uraAHK , and ↓ Abw *rHrHpa imperfectly decl., (Kr,) [The cantharis, or Spanish fly; ] a kind of insect of a red colour, (S, A, K,) spotted, or speckled, with black, which flies, (S, K,) and is of a poisonous nature; (S, K;) a kind of insect larger than the common fly, variegated with red and black and yellow, having a pair of wings with which it flies, and of a deadly poisonous nature: when they desire to allay the heat of its poison, they mix it with lentils, and so mixed it becomes a remedy for him who has been bitten by a mad dog: (IO:) Ibn-Ed-Dahhán the Lexicologist says that the *r~wH is a kind of fly variegated with yellow and white; and what is called faroxapu Ald~ayolami : by certain of the acute physicians it is described as HayawaAnN duwdiY~N , app. meaning a worm-like animal, of the size of the finger, and of a conical shape, the head of which is at the thickest part of it: and IDrst says that it is a flying insect, resembling the zunobuwr [or hornet ], and of a deadly poisonous nature. (TA.) It is observed in the S, with reference to *ur~uwHN , that, in the opinion of Sb, layosa fiY AlkalaAmi fuE~awolN biwaAHidapN ; meaning, there is not in the language a subst. (as distinguished from an epithet) of the measure fuE~awolN ; (marg. note in a copy of the S;) or his meaning is, [there is not a word of this measure] with damm alone; (MF;) or with a single dammeh, that is, to the f ; but with dammeh to the f and to the E : (IB:) and it is added in the S, that he (Sb) used to say sab~uwHN and qad~uwsN : Sb, however, also mentions the forms sub~uwHN and qud~uwsN . (MF.) The pl. is *araAyiHu : (S, K:) in the L, *ur~aAHN is also said to be a pl.: and Kr mentions *araAriHu ; but AHát says that this last is only used in poetry. (TA.) Sb says that the sing. of *araAriyHu is *uraHoraHN , (or, in other words, that one of the [insects called] *rAryH is [called] *rHrH ,) which is of the measure fuEaloEalN , and of which the dim. is ↓ *urayoriHN , formed by throwing out the first *uryoriHN ; [not H , as it would be by rule, making it of the measure *urayoHirN , and its curtailed original fuEayoliEN ;] for there is not in the language a word of the measure fElE , except fElE , (S,) which is the proper name of a man. (MF.) AHát cites a verse in which HadoradN occurs as pl. of *araAniHu ; but the correct reading is *rnwH . (MF.)

definition: meaning SaAHib [i.
sourceDefinition: meaning SaAHib [i. e. A possessor, an owner, a lord, or a master, but often better rendered having, possessing, possessed of, or endowed with ], (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K, but omitted in the CK,) used as a prefixed noun, (S, Mgh, Msb, &c.,) is originally *awFA , like EaSFA , the A being changed from w ; (S;) or it is originally *aw~aY ; and if one used it as a proper name, he would say, h`*aA *aw~aYqado jaA='a [ This is Dhawà, he has come ]; (M;) [not *awFA , as in copies of the S; i. e.,] its third radical letter is Y , not, as J says, w ; this Y being afterwards suppressed; (IB;) [so that the word becomes *awN , and then, by reason of its being prefixed to another noun, *uw , like as A^abawN , the original form of A^abN , becomes A^abuw :] it is declined [like A^abuw ] with w and | and Yi ; (Msb;) [i. e.,] the nom. case is *uw , accus. *aA , and gen. *iY : (Mgh:) the fem. is *aAtu ; (T, S, M, Mgh, Msb, K; in a copy of the M, *Ap , and the CK, *aApN [as though it were not a prefixed noun];) and in the case of a pause, some say *aAto , and others say *aAho : (Lth, T: the latter usage, only, is mentioned in the S:) dual. masc., *awaA , (S, * M,) [accus and gen. *awaYo ;] fem. *awaAtaA , (T, M, Mgh, Msb, K,) for which *aAtaA is allowable in poetry, but *awaAtaA is better, (T,) [accus, and gen. *awaAtaYo :] pl., masc., *awuw , (T, *, S, * M, Msb, K, but omitted in the CK,) [accus, and gen. *awiY ;] fem. *awaAtu , (T, S, * M, Mgh, Msb, K,) accus. and gen. *awaAti ; (S;) and A^uwluw and A^uwlaAt are like *awuw and *awaAt [in signification]. (T. [See art. Alw .]) In this sense it is not used otherwise than as a prefixed noun: when used to characterize an indeterminate noun, prefixed to an indeterminate noun; and when used to characterize a determinate noun, prefixed to [a noun rendered determinate by] the article Al . (S.) [Thus you say rajulN *uw maAlK A man a possessor of wealth; and Alr~ajulu *uw AlmaAli The man the possessor of wealth .] In the phrase gayora *aAti Al$awokapi [ Not those possessed of weapons, &c.], in the Kur [viii. 7], the fem. form is used as meaning the TaAy^ifap [or party]. (T.) SaAra *aA *anobK [ He became one having a sin, or crime, &c., attributable to him, i. e. he had a sin, &c., attributable to him, ] means taHam~ala *anobFA [ he became chargeable with a sin, &c.]. (Msb in art. *nb .) ― -b2- Accord. to the S, it is not prefixed to a pronoun ( muDomar ); nor to a proper name, such as zayod and Eamorw and the like: but there are several instances of its being prefixed, in its pl. form, to a pronoun; among which is the saying of a poet, A_in~amaA yaSoTaniEu AlmaEoruwfu fiY Aln~aAsi *awuwhu [ Only they who are possessors thereof do that which is good among men ]: (TA:) [this usage, however, is perhaps only allowable by poetic license: see another ex. (also here cited in the TA) in the Ham p. 442, and the remarks there appended to it:] and it is also prefixed to proper names, as is shown by the phrase, (TA,) h`*aA *uw zayodK (M, K, TA,) mentioned, as heard from the Arabs, by Ahmad Ibn-Ibráheem, the preceptor of Th, meaning This is Zeyd, (M, TA,) i. e., this is the owner of the name Zeyd; (M, K, TA;) and [perhaps] by the name *uw AlxalaSapi , for AlxlSp is [said by some to be] the name of a certain idol, and *w is a metonymical appellation of its bayot ; and by the proper names *uw ruEayonK and *uw yazana and [accord. to some] *uw jadonK [and the like, of which several are mentioned in the S, as well as in the M &c.]. (IB, TA.) [But see a later portion of this paragraph, where, prefixed to a proper name, it is said to be redundant.] ― -b3- *awuw AlA^aroHaAm , [or, as in the Kur viii. last verse, and xxxiii. 6, A^uwluw AlA^aroHaAmi , pls. of *uw Alr~aHimi ,] in the classical language, means [ The possessors of relationship; i. e.] any relations: and in law, any relations that have no portion [ of the inheritances termed faraAy^iD ] and are not [ such heirs as are designated by the appellation ] EaSabap [q. v.: they are so called because they are relations by the women's side: see raHimN ]. (KT, TA.) ― -b4- If you form a pl. from *uwmaAlK , you say, h`w^ulaA='i *awuwna [ These are possessors of wealth]; because in this case the pl. is not a prefixed noun. (S.) Accord. to Lth, Al*~awuwna signifies The former, or first, [ of persons, ] and the more, or most, distinguished. (T, TA. *) Also, (S, M,) and AlA^a*owaA='u , [which is another pl. of *uw ,] (S,) The kings (S, M) of El-Yemen, of the tribe of Kudá'ah, (S,) whose surnames commenced with *uw , (M,) [i. e.] who were named [or rather surnamed ] (S) *uw yazana (S, M) and *uw jadanK and *uw nuwaAsK (S) and the like. (S, M.) qura$iY~N layosa mino *iY walaA *uw , occurring in a trad., means A Kurashee in respect of lineage, not of the A^a*owaA=' [above mentioned]. (TA.) ― -b5- [ *uw and *aAt and *aA and *iY are also used as prefixed nouns in various expressions here following, in several thereof as meaning Something in possession, or the like; not a possessor: or, in these instances, as is said in explanation of the first of the following phrases, and also of the phrase *aAtu Alyadi (mentioned below) in Har p. 93, that which is contained is made to be as though it were the possessor ( SaAHib ) of that which contains.] ― -b6- maw~ata *aAbaTonihaA [ He killed what was in her belly ]. (Har ubi suprá.) And waDaEati AlmaroA^apu *aA baTonihaA , (T,) or *aAta baTonihaA , (TA,) The woman brought forth [ her child ]. (T, TA.) And navarato *aA baTonihaA She brought forth many children. (T in art. nvr ; and Mgh there and in the present art., in the latter of which it is added that the usual phrase is navarato baTonahaA .) And A^aloqati Ald~ajaAjapu *aA baTonihaA The hen laid her egg, or eggs: or muted. (Mgh.) And A^aloqaY Alr~ajulu *aA baTonihi The man ejected his excrement, or ordure. (T.) And Al*~iy^obu magobuwTN bi*iY baTonihi The wolf is envied [ for what is in his belly, or] for his distention of the belly [ with food ]. (TA.) ― -b7- [In like manner,] *aAtu Alyadi means (tropical:) Wealth; as though it were the possessor of that which contains it: (Har ubi suprá:) [or what is in the possession of the hand: ] or what one possesses, of wealth; because gained by the hand and disposed of by the hand. (Har p. 66.) You say, qal~ato *aAtu yadihi (assumed tropical:) What his hand possessed became little in quantity; (Lth, T;) or the possessions accompanying his hand; (Mgh;) app. meaning his riches. (Lth, T.) ― -b8- *aAtu Alr~iy^api and *aAtu Aljanobi are Two well-known diseases. (TA. [See arts. rA^Y and jnb .]) ― -b9- EaliymN bi*aAti AlS~uduwri , in the Kur iii. 115, means [ Acquainted, or well acquainted, ] with what is in the minds: (Ksh, Bd, Jel: [and the like is indicated in the Mgh:]) or with the true, or real, nature of the notions that are concealed in the minds: (IAmb, T:) or with the hidden things of the minds: or with the minds themselves. (Msb. [If the last meaning be correct, the phrase should be mentioned with others later in this paragraph.]) [And similar to this is the saying,] Earafahu mino *aAti nafosihi He knew it from what he conceived in his mind [without his being informed thereof; i. e. he knew it of himself ]. (Lth, T.) And jaA='a mino *iYnafosihi and mino *aAti nafosihi (M, K) He came [ from a motive in his own mind; of himself; ] of his own accord; or willingly; syn. Tay~iEFA : (M, TA:) in the copies of the K, TaboEFA ; but the former is the right explanation. (TA.) And maA kal~amotu fulaAnFA *aAta $afapK and *aAta famK I spoke not to such a one a word. (AZ, T.) ― -b10- *aAta Alyamiyni and *aAta Al$~imaAli [are adverbial expressions, and] mean In the direction of the right hand and of the left: properly in the direction that has the name of the right hand [and that has the name of the left hand ]. (Bd in xviii. 16.) And A^atayonaA *aA yamiynK means We came on the right hand. (TA.) ― -b11- *aAta mar~apK and *aA SabaAHK [also, and the like,] are adverbial expressions, which may not be used otherwise than as such: (S:) you say, laqiytuhu *aAta mar~apK [ I met him once, or once upon a time ], (S,) and *aAta AlmiraAri many times, (M and K in art. mr ,) or sometimes, (S in that art.,) and *aAta yawomK (Fr, T, S) i. e. mar~apF fiY yawomK [ once upon a day, or one day ], therefore you use the fem. form, (T,) and *aAta layolapK [ one night ], (Fr, T, S,) and *aAta gadaApK [ one morning, or one morning between daybreak and sunrise ], and *aAta AlEi$aA='i [ once in the evening at nightfall ], (S,) meaning, accord. to Th, in the hour, or time, in which is nightfall, (T,) and *aAta Alz~umayoni (Fr, T, S) [ some time ago, or ] three [ or more, to ten, ] seasons ago, ( mu*o valaAvapu A^azomaAnK , T, [by AzmAn being app. meant periods of two, or three, or six, months,]) and *aAta AlEuwayomi (Fr, T, S) [ some years ago, or] three years ago (T,) or three years ago or more, to ten; (Az on the authority of AZ, TA in art. Ewm ;) and *aA SabaAHK [ one morning ], and *aA masaA='K [ one evening ], (T, S,) and *aA SabuwHK [lit, at a time of drinking the morning-draught ], and *aA gabuwqK [lit. at a time of drinking the evening-draught ]; in these four instances without p : and this mode of expression has been heard only in the cases of the times here mentioned: they did not say *aAta $ahorK nor *aAta sanapK : (S:) or one may also well say *aAta SabaAHK , like *aAta yawomK ; for *A and *At both mean the time: and accord. to IAar, one says, A^atayotuhu *aAta AlS~abuwHi and *aAta Algabuwqi , as meaning I came to him in the morning, or in the morning between daybreak and sunrise, and in the evening, or in the evening between sunset and nightfall. (T.) ― -b12- You say also, laqiytuhu *aAta yadayoni , (TA,) or laqiytuhu A^aw~ala *iY yadayoni (M) and *aAti yadayoni , (AZ, M, Msb, [whence it seems to be not improbable that the phrase in the TA is imperfectly transcribed,]) meaning I met him the first thing, (M,) or first of everything. (AZ, Msb, TA.) And A^afoEaluhu A^aw~ala *iY yadayoni and *aAti yadayoni [ I will do it the first thing, or first of everything ]. (M.) And A^am~aA A^aw~ala *aAti yadayoni faA_in~aniY A^aHomadu A@ll~`ha , (AZ, M, Msb,) i. e. [ Whatever be the case, the first thing, or] first of everything, I praise God. (AZ, Msb.) ― -b13- [Respecting the phrase *aAtu Albayoni , which has two contr. meanings, see art. byn . It is inadequately explained in this art. in the T and M and K, as follows.] waA^aSoliHuwA *aAta bayonikumo , (T, M, K, *) in the Kur [viii. 1], accord. to Ahmad Ibn-Yahyà, means [ And do ye rightly dispose, or arrange, or order, ] the case that is between you: (T:) or, accord. to Zj, (M,) that wherein consists your union; ( Haqiyqapa waSolikumo , M, K;) i. e. be ye of one accord, or in unison, respecting that which God and his Apostle have commanded: (M:) or *aAtu Albayoni means the state of circumstances whereby the Muslims become of one accord, or in unison: (K:) this is the meaning in the saying, Aall~`hum~a A^aSoliHo *aAta Albayoni [ O God, do Thou rightly dispose &c.]. (M.) ― -b14- *aAtN is sometimes used as a noun independent in its meaning, (Mgh, Msb,) so as to denote material [or real] things; (Msb;) and is described by the epithets mutamay~izapN [or “ distinct ”] (Mgh, Msb) and qadiymapN [as meaning “ that has existed from eternity ”] (Mgh) and muHodavapN [as meaning “ that has been brought into existence ”]. (Mgh, Msb.) Thus used, (Msb,) it signifies The essence of a thing, meaning that by being which a thing is what it is, or that in being which a thing consists; or the ultimate and radical constituent of a thing: and the essence as meaning the peculiar nature of a thing: syn. HaqiyqapN , (T, IB, Msb, TA,) and maAhiy~apN , (Msb,) and xaAS~apN : (T, IB, TA:) it is also used as meaning a thing's self: (Mgh, * Msb:) [a man's self, or person: (see $axoSN :)] and a thing; a being; anything, whatever it be; every $aYo' being a *aAt , and every *At being a $Y' : (Aboo-Sa'eed, Mgh, Msb:) and particularly a substance, or thing that subsists by itself: [hence Aisomu *aAtK meaning a real substantive; also termed Aisomu EayonK : opposed to Aisomu maEonFY , i. e. an ideal substantive:] and [hence] it signifies also a word that is independent in its meaning; [i. e. *aAtN (alone), though oftener used in the sense assigned above to Aisomu *aAtK , signifies also, absolutely, a substantive; ] opposed to SifapN as signifying a word that is not independent in its meaning. (Kull p. 187.) Its application to God, in the sense of HaqiyqapN and xaAS~apN , is forbidden by most persons: (TA:) [for] *aAtu A@ll~`hi [as meaning The essence of God ], used by the scholastic theologians, is said to be an ignorant expression, because the names of God do not admit the fem. affix p ; so that one does not apply to Him the epithet Eal~aAmapN , though He is the all-surpassing in knowledge. (Msb.) The phrase fiY *aAti A@ll~`hi is like fiY janobi A@ll~`hi [ In, or in respect of, that which is the right, or due, of God; or in, or in respect of, obedience to God, or the means of obtaining nearness to God, or the way of God ]: and like liwajohi A@ll~`hi [ for the sake of God; or to obtain the countenance, or favour, or approbation, or recompense, of God ]: (Msb:) or it means in obedience to God; and in the way of God or his religion: (TA:) [or it may be rendered for the sake of God Himself; and so liwajohi A@ll~`hi : it is said to have been used by the Arabs [of the classical age], as well as by Aboo-Temmám, [who was a Muwelled;] (Mgh, Msb, *) but some deny that it occurs in the old language. (Msb. [See, however, an ex. from a trad. voce A^uxayo$inu .]) [It is said that] the phrase majal~atuhumo *aAtu AlA_il`hi , used by En-Nábighah, (Msb,) i. e. EdhDhubyánee, (TA in art. jl ,) means Their book is the service of God Himself: (Msb:) [but it seems more reasonable to render this phrase agreeably with the primary signification of *At as meaning their book is that of God, in a sense like that in which a house of worship is said to be a house of God; for,] as some relate it, the phrase used by En-Nábighah is maHal~atuhumo *aAtu AlA_il`hi , with HA' , [i. e. their abode is in a peculiar manner that of God, ] meaning, their abode is one of pilgrimage and of sacred sites. (S and TA in art. jl .) ― -b15- *uw is sometimes redundant [in respect of meaning, though governing as a prefixed n.]; and so is its pl. (T, * TA.) Az says, (TA,) I have heard more than one of the Arabs say, kun~aA bimawoDiEi ka*aA maEa *iY EamorKw , i. e. We were in such a place with Amr: (T, TA:) and kaAna maEanaA *uw EamorKw , i. e. 'Amr was with us: and A^atayonaA *aA yamanK , meaning A^atayonaA Alyamana [ We came to El-Yemen ]. (T.) [See an ex. similar to this last, and evidently belonging to the present art., in the latter half of art. *A . And see laA *aA jarama and laA A^ano *aA jarama and laA Eano *aA jarama and laA *aA jara (in which *A is in like manner redundant, as are also A^ano and Eano , the latter of which is a dial. var. of the former of them,) in art. jrm : perhaps belonging to the present art., like A^atayonaA *aAyamanK ; or perhaps to art. *A . See also what is said respecting *uw prefixed to a proper name in an early portion of this paragraph.] ― -b16- It is also used in the sense of Aal~a*iY , (T, S, M, K,) in the dial. of Teiyi, (T, S, TA,) for the purpose of qualifying a determinate noun (S, M, K) by means of a proposition which it connects with that noun: (M, K:) and when thus used, it [generally] retains the same form when it denotes a dual and a pl. (S, M, K) and a fem., (S,) and exhibits no sign of case: (M, K:) you say, A^anaA *uw Earafotu [ I who knew ], and *uw samiEotu [ who heard ]; and h`*ihi AlmaroA^apu *uw qaAlato ka*aA [ This is the woman who said such a thing: (S:) and A^ataAniY *uw qaAla *`lika [ He who said that came to me ]; and A^ataAniY *uw qaAlaA *`lika [ They two who said that came to me ]; and A^ataAni *uw qaAluwA *`lika [ They who said that came to me ]. (M.) But Fr says, I heard an Arab of the desert say, biAlfaDoli *uw faD~alakumo A@ll~`hu bihi waAlkaraAmapi *aAtu A^akoramakumu A@ll~`hu bihaA [ By the excellence wherewith God hath made you to excel, and the honour wherewith God hath honoured you ]; thus they use *aAtu in the place of Aal~atiY , and they make it to be with refa in every case: and they confuse [numbers and genders] in speaking of a dual number and a pl. number [and a fem.]; they sometimes say, [for ex.,] in the case of the dual, h`*aAni *uw taEorifu and haAtaAni *uw taEorifu [ These two whom, or which, thou knowest ]; and a poet says, [namely, Sinán Ibn-El-Fahl, of the tribe of Teiyi, (Ham p. 292,)] faA_in~a AlmaA='a A^abiY wajad~iY wabiy^oriY *uw Hafarotu wa*uw Tawayotu [ For verily the water is the water of my father and my grandfather, and my well which I dug and which I cased; making *w to relate to a fem. noun]: and some, he adds, use the dual and pl. and fem. forms; thus they say, h`*aAna *awaA qaAlaA *aAka [ These two who said that ], and h`w^ulaA='i *awuwA qaAluwA [ These who said ], and h`*ihi *aAtu qaAlato [ This female who said ]; and he cites the saying of a poet, jamaEotuhaA mino A^ayonuqK sawaAbiqo *awaAtu yanohaDona bigayori saAy^iqo [ I collected them from outstripping she-camels, that rise and hasten in their pace without a driver ]; and the prov., A^ataY Ealayohi *uw A^ataY EalaY Aln~aAsi , meaning Al~a*iY A^ataY [i. e. What has come upon men in general has come, or came, upon him ]. (T.) Accord. to the usage most in repute, *uw in this sense is indecl., and has no variation of gender or number; but some decline it, like *w in the sense of SaAHib , except that they make *aAt and *awaAt indecl., with damm for the termination, saying *aAtu and *awaAtu in every case, if they adopt the chaste mode; otherwise, in the accus. and gen. cases, saying *aAti , and in like manner *awaAti (I' Ak pp. 40 and 41.) ― -b17- They said also, laAA^afoEalu *`lika bi*iY tasolamu (M, K) and b*Y tasolamiyna , (M,) and b*Y tasolamaAni , (M, K,) and b*Y tasolamuwna and b*Ytasolamona , (M,) meaning I will not do that by thy, and by your, safety: (M, K:) or by God who, (M,) or by Him who, (K,) maketh thee, and you, to be in safety. (M, K.) [See also art. slm .]
