definition: Wine: (K:) so, accord.
sourceDefinition: Wine: (K:) so, accord. to Fr and others in the Kur [xvi. 69], tat~axi*uwna minohu sakarFA warizoqFA HasanFA , meaning, ye obtain therefrom wine, and raisins and dried dates and the like; this being said before wine was prohibited: (TA:) and the [ beverage called ] nabiy* (S, A) prepared from dried dates: (S:) so in the Kur, ubi suprà: (S:) or the expressed juice of fresh ripe dates when it has become strong; (Mgh, Msb;) originally an inf. n.: (Mgh:) or an infusion of dried dates, untouched by fire: (A 'Obeyd:) a beverage, (A,) or nabiy* , (K,) made from dried dates and from ka$uwv [ a species of cuscuta, or dodder ] (A, K) and myrtle, A=s , (A,) which is the most bitter beverage in the world, (A,) and forbidden like wine; (TA;) or made from dried dates and k$wv , disposed layer upon layer, upon which water is poured; and some assert that sometimes myrtle ( A=s ) is mixed with it, and this increases its strength: (AHn:) also anything that intoxicates: (K:) and what is forbidden [ that is obtained ] from fruit (I'Ab, T, K) [ of the palm-tree and grape vine ], meaning wine, before its being forbidden; and Alr~izoqu AlHasanu is what is lawful [that is obtained] from grapes and dates: (I 'Ab, T, TA:) and vinegar; (K;) accord. to some of the expositors of the Kur, ubi suprà; but this is a meaning unknown to the leading lexicologists: (B, TA:) and food: (K:) so accord. to AO alone; as in the following saying of a poet; jaEalota A^aEoraADa AlkiraAmi sakaraA [ Thou hast made the reputations of the generous to be food: or] thou hast made the vituperation of the generous to be food to thee: but the leading lexicologists disallow this; and Zj says that the more probable meaning here is wine. (TA.)

definition: [ Sugar; ] a certain sweet substance, (TA,) well known: (Msb, TA:) a Pers. word, (S,) arabicized, (S, K,) from $akaro : (K:) n. un. with p [signifying a piece of sugar ]: (S, K:) it is hot and moist,...
sourceDefinition: [ Sugar; ] a certain sweet substance, (TA,) well known: (Msb, TA:) a Pers. word, (S,) arabicized, (S, K,) from $akaro : (K:) n. un. with p [signifying a piece of sugar ]: (S, K:) it is hot and moist, accord. to the most correct opinion; but some say, cold: and the best sort of it is the transparent, called Tabaroza*N ; and the old is more delicate than the new: it is injurious to the stomach, engendering yellow bile; but the juice of the layomuwn and naAranoj counteract its noxiousness: it is said to be a word recently introduced; but some say that it occurs in one trad. (TA.) ― -b2- Also Like suk~ar [or sugar ] in sweetness: so used by Aboo-Ziyád El-Kilábee. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A certain kind of sweet fresh ripe dates; (K;) a sort of fresh ripe dates, likened to sugar in sweetness: (Mgh:) or a kind of very sweet dates; (AHát, T, Msb;) known to the people of ElBahreyn, (T,) and in Sijilmáseh and Dar'ah, and, as some say, in El-Medeeneh, where, how- ever, they require to be dried artificially. (MF.) ― -b4- A kind of grapes, which, being affected by what is termed maraq , fall off, (K,) for the most part: their bunches are of middling size; and they are white, juicy, and very sweet, (TA,) of the best kinds of grapes; (K;) and are made into raisins. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: A certain plant, always green, the grain whereof is eaten: (K: [but this description seems to be an incorrect abstract of what here follows:]) Ed-Deenawaree [i. e. Arab., p. lxiii.,) hyoscyamus datora. See also $ayokuraAnN .]

sourceDefinition: , (S, M, &c.,) aor. , (M, L,) inf. n. sumuwdN , He (a man, IAar) was, or became, high, or elevated. (IAar, S, M, L, K. [ EalA'F in the CK is a mistake for EalA .]) ― -b2- He raised his head; (L; [and the same is implied in the S; see saAmidN ;]) and so samida : (M, L:) [and] he raised his head in pride. (S, L, K.) And in the former sense it is said of a camel, in his going along. (Bd in liii. 61.) ― -b3- Also He (a man) stood, raising his head, and with his breast erect; like as the stallion [camel] does when excited by lust: (A:) [for] it is said of a stallion [camel] when thus excited. (L.) ― -b4- And hence, (A,) (tropical:) He sang: (M, A, L:) because the singer raises his head and erects his breast: (A:) but Th says that this is rare: (M:) accord. to I'Ab, sumuwdN signifies the act of singing in the dial. of Himyer. (L.) ― -b5- Also, (M, K,) aor. as above, (TA,) and so the inf. n., (S, M,) (assumed tropical:) He diverted himself, sported, or played. (S, M, K, TA. [For lahiYa in the CK, I read lahaA , as in the M, and in MS. copies of the K, and in the TA; and agreeably with the S, in which the inf. n. is expl. as syn. with lahowN .]) ― -b6- He was, or became, negligent, inattentive, inadvertent, inconsiderate, or heedless; and went away from, or relinquished, or left, a thing. (L.) ― -b7- He was, or became, confounded, perplexed, or amazed, and unable to see his right course; or affected with wonder; or cut short, or silent, being confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; syn. buhita : inf. n. as above: (M:) [or] he stood confounded, or perplexed, and unable to see his right course; syn. qaAma mutaHay~irFA . (K. [After this explanation and lahaA immediately following it, it is said in the K, wAls~umuwdu yakuwnu HuzonFA wasurwrFA : meaning that it is by reason of grieving, or mourning, as signifying the “ standing confounded ” &c.; and by reason of rejoicing, or being happy, as signifying the “ diverting oneself ” &c. See as an ex. of its usage in a case of grief the verses which I have cited at the close of the first paragraph of art. rd , and which are cited in the present art. in the L and TA.]) ― -b8- Also He kept constantly, or continually, (M, L,) to an affair, (M,) or upon the ground, or in the land. (L.) ― -b9- He strove laboured, or exerted himself, or he wearied himself, in work, (K, TA,) and in journeying. (TA.) And samadati AlA_ibilu (S, M, K) fiY sayorihaA , (S,) aor. and inf. n. as above, (M,) The camels strove, laboured, or exerted themselves, in their journeying: (S, K:) or knew not fatigue, or weariness. (M.) [See also samodN , (which is likewise, perhaps, an inf. n. of the same verb,) below.] -A2- samadahu , inf. n. samodN , i. q. qaSadahu [ He tended, repaired, betook himself, or directed himself or his course or aim, to, or towards, him, or it; or endeavoured to reach, or attain, or obtain, him, or it; &c.]; like Samadahu . (M.) -A3- And samada AlA^aroDa , inf. n. samodN , He made the land, or ground, plain, or smooth, or soft. (M.)

definition: Any [man or animal] raising his head [in pride or otherwise].
sourceDefinition: Any [man or animal] raising his head [in pride or otherwise]. (S, M, L.) ― -b2- A man standing: (IAar; and so in a copy of the S:) or standing, raising his head, and with his breast erect; (A, IAth;) as the stallion [camel] does when excited by lust. (A.) ― -b3- [And hence, as is indicated in the A, (see 1,)] (assumed tropical:) A singer; or singing. (M, L; and so in two copies of the S.) And the latter is said to be the meaning of the pl. in the Kur liii. 61. (M, L.) ― -b4- [Hence also,] Behaving proudly. (I 'Ab in explanation of the pl. in the Kur liii. 61; and IAar.) ― -b5- Diverting himself; playing; or sporting. (IAar, S, M; and Bd in liii. 61,) ― -b6- Negligent, inattentive, inadvertent, inconsiderate, or heedless. (Lth, IAar A.) Thus the pl. is said by Lth to mean in the Kur liii. 61. definition: They descended to the sahol [i.
sourceDefinition: They descended to the sahol [i. e. smooth or soft, or plain or level, or smooth and soft, tract ]: (JK, Msb:) or they betook themselves to the sahol : (S:) or they became in the sahol : (K:) and they alighted and abode in the sahol , after they had been alighting and abiding in the Hazon [i. e. rugged, or rugged and hard, or rugged and high, ground ]. (TA.) Hence, in a trad. respecting the throwing of the pebbles [at Minè], yusohilu occurs as meaning He betakes himself to the interior of the valley. (TA.) ― -b2- Also They used smoothness, or easiness, ( suhuwlap ,) with men: opposed to A^aHozanuwA . (TA.) [See also 3.] -A2- Ashl is also trans., signifying He found [a thing, a place, &c.,] to be smooth or soft, plain or level, or smooth and soft. (Ham p. 675.) ― -b2- Ashl AlT~abiyEapa (S) or AlbaTona , (Msb, K,) said of medicine, (S, Msb, K,) It relaxed, or loosened, the bowels; syn. A^alaAna , (K,) or A^aTolaqa . (Msb.) And A^usohila Alr~ajulu [ The man was relaxed in his bowels]: and A^usohila baTonuhu [ His bowels were relaxed ]. (K.) [Hence the inf. n. A_isohaAlN signifies A diarrhœa. And Ashl , likewise said of medicine, signifies also It attenuated a humour of the body.] ― -b3- Ashlt bihi She brought it forth (i. e. her fœtus, or offspring,) prematurely; i. q. A^amolaSato bihi [q. v.] &c. (Abu-l-'Abbás [i. e. Th], TA in art. mlS .)

definition: Smooth or soft, plain or level, or smooth and soft: (Msb:) or anything inclining to smoothness or softness, plainness or levelness, or smoothness and softness;
sourceDefinition: Smooth or soft, plain or level, or smooth and soft: (Msb:) or anything inclining to smoothness or softness, plainness or levelness, or smoothness and softness; (JK, M, K;) inclining to have little roughness, or ruggedness and hardness; (JK, M, TA;) and ↓ sahilN signifies the same. (K.) You say A^aroDN saholapN , [meaning the same as saholN used as a subst., expl. in what follows,] (S, Msb,) contr. of HazonapN . (TA.) (TA.) rajulN saholu Alwajohi , (K, TA,) a phrase mentioned, but not explained, by Lh, (TA,) means A man having little flesh in the face, (K, TA,) in the opinion of ISd: and [it is said that] saholu Alxad~ayoni , in a description of the approved characteristics of the Prophet, means having expanded cheeks, not elevated in the balls thereof. (K.)

definition: A certain star [ well known;
sourceDefinition: A certain star [ well known; namely, Canopus ]; (T, S, K;) not seen in Khurásán, but seen in El-'Irák; (T, TA;) as Ibn-Kunáseh says, seen in El-Hijáz and in all the land of the Arabs, but not seen in the land of Armenia; and between the sight thereof by the people of ElHijáz and the sight thereof by the people of El- 'Irák are twenty days: (TA:) it is said that shyl was a tyrannical collector of the tithes on the road to El-Yemen, and God transformed him into a star: (Lth, TA:) [ it rose aurorally, in Central Arabia, about the commencement of the ear of the Flight, on the 4th of August, O. S.: the place where it rises, in that latitude, is S. 29 degrees E.; and the place where it sets, in the same latitude, S. 29 degrees W.: (see 10 in art. Hb : and see januwbN :)] at the time of its [ auroral ] rising, the fruits ripen, and the qayoZ [q. v., here meaning the greatest heat, ] ends. (K.) [ baAla suhayolN , which is a prov., and the saying of a poet, baAla suhayolN fiY AlfaDiyxi fafasado have been expl. in art. bwl .] 'Omar Ibn-'AbdAllah Ibn-Abee-Rabeea says respecting Suheyl Ibn-'Abd-Er-Rahmán Ibn-'Owf, and his taking in marriage Eth-Thureiyà El-'Ableeyeh of the Benoo-Umeiyeh, deeming their coming together to be a strange thing by likening them to the stars named Eth-Thureiyà and Suheyl, A^ay~uhaA AlmunokiHu Alv~uray~aA suhayolFA Eamoraka A@ll~`ha kayofa yalotaqiyaAni hiYa $aAmiy~apN A_i*aA maA A@sotaqal~ato wasuhayolN A_i*aA A@sotaqal~a yamaAniY [ O thou marrier of Eth-Thureiyà to Suheyl, by thine acknowledgment of the everlasting existence of God, (or, as it sometimes means, I ask God to prolong thy life, ) tell me, how can they meet together? She is of the northern region when she rises, and Suheyl, when he rises, is of the southern region ]. (Har p. 276. [But I have substituted A@ll~`ha for All~`hu , and yamaAniY for yamaAnK . See also the notice of the poet above named in the work of Ibn-Khillikán: (I have the express authority of the TA for thus writing this name:) and De Sacy's Anthol. Gramm. Arabe, p. 139.]) [Freytag states that qadamaA suhayolK is the name of Two stars which are behind Canopus; on the authority of Meyd: and also mentions the name of shyl Al$Am , and shyl Alfrd , as given to Certain stars in the constellation Anguis; adding that Canopus is distinguished from shyl Al$Am by the name of shyl Alymn .] The name of A^uxotaAsuhayolK [ The two sisters of Canopus ] is applied to Al$~iEoraY AlEabuwru [or Sirius ] and Al$~iEoraY AlgumayoSaA='u [or Procyon ], together. (S and K in art. $Er .) [See also HaDaAri and Alwazonu .]

sourceDefinition: , aor. yasiyru , inf. n. sayorN and masiyrN , (S, M, A, Mgh, Msb, K,) which latter is extr., for by rule it should be of the measure mafoEalN , with fet-h [to the E ], (S,) and masiyrapN (M, K) and sayoruwrapN (M, Mgh, K) like qayoluwlapN , but [Mtr says] we have not heard it, (Mgh,) and tasoyaArN , (S, M, K,) which last denotes repetition or frequency of the action, (M,) He, or it, went [ in any manner, or any pace ]; went, or passed, along; marched, journeyed, or proceeded; went away, passed away, or departed; (M, * K, * TA;) by night and by day. (Msb, TA.) You say, saArati Ald~aAb~apu [ The beast went, went along, &c.]. (S.) [And sAr sayorFA $adiydFA He (a camel or other beast, and a man,) went a vehement pace, or vehemently. And sAr AlEanaqa He (a camel, or a horse,) went the pace, or in the manner, termed AlEanaq : and the like.] And saAruwA mino baladK libaladK [ They went, or journeyed, from town to town, or from country to country ]: (A:) or sAr mino baladK A_ilaY baladK [ he went, &c.]. (Mgh.) And baAraka A@ll~`hu fiY masiyrika i. e. sayorika [ May God bless thy journeying ]. (S.) And siro Eanoka Go thou from thy place; pass thou from it: (L in art. nf* :) or (assumed tropical:) feign thou heedlessness, and bear, or endure, or be forbearing; an elliptical phrase; as though it were originally siro wadaEo Eanoka AlmiraA='a waAl$~ak~a [ go thou, and leave wrangling and doubt ]. (S.) ― -b2- [Hence, sArt Als~afiynapu (tropical:) The ship went, or sailed: for] sayoru Als~afiynapi is a tropical phrase. (Mgh.) ― -b3- And sAr siyrapF HasanapF (tropical:) [ He pursued a good way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like ], (S, A, Msb,) and siyrapF qabiyHapF [ a bad way, &c.]. (Msb.) ― -b4- And sAr fiY Aln~aAsi (assumed tropical:) It became current, or commonly known, among the people; [as also ↓ tasay~ara , alone; (see Har p. 318;)] i. e. a proverb, and a saying. (M.) ― -b5- And sArt sun~apN (assumed tropical:) [ A way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like, obtained, or was usual, among people ]. (M.) -A2- sAr is also trans., syn. with say~ara . (S, M, Msb, K.) See the latter, in five places. ― -b2- [Hence,] sAr sun~apF (assumed tropical:) He made, or caused, a way, course, mode, or manner, of acting, or conduct, or the like, to obtain, or became usual, among people. (S, M, * TA.) The Hudhalee (Khálid Ibn-Zuheyr, M) says, falaA tajozaEano mino sun~apK A^anota sirotahaA faA^aw~alu raADK sun~apF mano yasiyruhaA [ Then by no means be thou impatient of a way of acting which thou hast made usual; for the first who should be content with a way of acting is he who makes it usual ]. (S, M, L, TA: but in the M and TA, in the place of tjzEn , we find tagoDabano .)

sourceDefinition: A man having his colour, or complexion, altered [ for the worse, wan, or haggard ], (TA,) or so $aAHibu All~awoni , (A,) in consequence of disease, or travel, or the like: (TA: [see 1:]) and emaciated, or lean; (TA, KL;) as also ↓ $aHibN . (Msb.) You say, $a*~a Eanohu It was, or became, apart, &c., from it. (S, L.) And $a*~a Eani AljamaAEapi He was, or became, apart from the collective body [or generality ] of people. (Mgh.) definition: A thing that is, or becomes, apart, (S, L, Msb,) and that falls, or goes, or comes, out, or forth, from the generality of things, general assemblage, main body, bulk, or common mass, (S, L,) to which...
sourceDefinition: A thing that is, or becomes, apart, (S, L, Msb,) and that falls, or goes, or comes, out, or forth, from the generality of things, general assemblage, main body, bulk, or common mass, (S, L,) to which it pertains: (L:) anything apart, or alone: and a man apart from his companions, or alone: (Lth, L:) and [app. a beast] taking fright, and running away: (Msb:) $u*~aAnN is a pl. thereof, like as $ub~aAnN is of $aAb~N ; [and so is $u*~aA*N , agreeably with analogy;] and ↓ $a*~aAn is used in a similar sense, but is an epithet of the measure fiEolaAn , not a pl. of $aA*~N . (L.) maA yadaEu fulaAnN $aA*~FA walaA naAd~FA A_il~aA qatalahu [ Such a one does not leave any one apart from his companions, nor any one taking fright and running away, but he slays him, ] is said of a courageous man whom no one encounters without his slaying him. (IAar, L.) And one says $u*~aAnu qawomK Those, of a people, who have become apart, or separate, from their companions. (L, from a trad.) And $u*~aA*u Aln~aAsi Those who are among a people but do not belong to their tribes (S, L) nor to their places of abode: (L:) and those who are scattered, or dispersed, of people; (A, L;) as also Aln~aAsi ↓ $a*~aAnu , (S, L,) and $u*~aAnuhumo . (L.) And qawomN $u*~aA*N A people not among their own tribe nor in their own places of abode: (L, K: *) or a people among another people, not among their own tribes nor in their own places of abode. (M, TA.) And $u*~aA*u AlA=faAqi The strangers. (Har p. 352.) And jaAw^uwA $u*~aA*FA They came few in number. (L, K. *) And AlA_ibili ↓ $a*~aAnu and $u*~aAnuhaA Those that are scattered, or dispersed, of the camels. (L.) And $u*~aAnu AlHaSaY (M, L) and AlHaSaY ↓ $a*~aAnu (S, IJ, M, L, K) What are scatterred, or dispersed, of pebbles; (S, L, K;) what have flown about, and become scattered or dispersed, thereof: (M, L:) and in like manner one says of other things, (L, K,) or of similar things. (M, L.) ― -b2- Applied to a word, form or measure, construction, or government, it signifies (tropical:) Deviating from the common, or constant, course of speech in respect of analogy, or rule; deviating from common, or constant, analogy or rule; extraordinary, or exceptional, as to rule; or anomalous, abnormal, or irregular: such a word, &c., though itself admitted if agreeable with common usage, is not taken as an example to be imitated: also, applied to the same, deviating from the common, or constant, course of speech in respect of usage; deviating from common, or constant, usage; extraordinary, or exceptional, as to usage; unusual: [used absolutely to express each of these significations; the context in general showing clearly which signification is meant: the former is that which is most frequently intended:] a word, &c., may be $A*~ in respect of usage but agreeable with common analogy or rule; as the pret. of ya*aru and yadaEu ; and the regular phrase makaAnN muboqilN , the epithet more commonly heard being baAqilN : and $A*~ in respect of analogy, or rule, but agreeable with common usage; as A^axowaSa Alr~imovu , and AisotaSowabotu AlA^amora : and $A*~ in respect of analogy, or rule, and of usage, together; as vawobN maSowuwnN , and misokN madowuwfN : (Mz, 12th nwE : [and the like is said, but less fully, in the Msb:]) the pl. masc. is $u*~aA*N ; and pl. fem. $awaA*~u . (Mz, ib.) See 4, last sentence. [See also the contr. muT~aridN : and see $a*~a , latter part.] ― -b3- Applied to a tradition, (assumed tropical:) Having a single ascription, attested by a [ single ] sheykh, whether he be trustworthy or not: in the latter case, not accepted: in the former case, one hesitates respecting it, and does not adduce it as an argument, or evidence. (KT.)

sourceDefinition: , inf. n. ta$oriyfN , He (God) rendered him high, elevated, exalted, or eminent, [ in rank, condition, or estimation; or ennobled him: ] (S, KL, * PS: *) and he held him, or esteemed him, to be so. (MA, PS.) ISd thinks that the verb may also mean He regarded with more, or exceeding, honour. (TA.) [And Golius explains it as meaning He decked with a royal garment; on the authority of the KL; in my copy of which I find no other meaning assigned to it than the first mentioned above.] One says, $ar~afa A@ll~`hu AlkaEobapa , (O, K, TA,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) [ God rendered, or may God render, the Kaabeh an object of honour, or glorious, ] from Al$~arafu , (O, K, TA,) i. e. Almajodu . (TA.) [ ta$oriyfN is also used as a subst. properly so called; and as such is expl. by itself in this art.] ― -b2- Also He put to it $uraf [pl. of $urofapN , q. v.]; (O, K;) namely, his house, (K,) or a [palace, or pavilion, or other building such as is called] qaSor , &c.; inf. n. as above. (O.) [See also $arafa AlHaAy^iTa .] ― -b3- $r~f AlmarobaA^a , expl. in the K as syn. with A$rfhu and $Arfhu , is a mistake for t$r~fhu [q. v.]. definition: It rose; or it was, or became, high or elevated; [ so as to overtop, or overlook, what was around it or adjacent to it: overtopped, surmounted, overpeered, overlooked, overhung; was, or became,...
sourceDefinition: It rose; or it was, or became, high or elevated; [ so as to overtop, or overlook, what was around it or adjacent to it: overtopped, surmounted, overpeered, overlooked, overhung; was, or became, protuberant, prominent, or projecting: and rose into view, came within sight or view, or became within a commanding, or near, view: ] said of a place [&c.]. (Msb.) One says of a piece of ground, A^a$orafa EalaY maA Hawolahu [ It rose above, or overtopped, what was around it ]. (Sh, TA.) And A^a$orafa liY $arafN famaA zilotu A^arokuDu Hat~aY Ealawotuhu [ An eminence rose into view to me, and I ceased not to urge on my beast until I ascended, or mounted, upon it ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Hence,] A^a$orafotu Ealayohi I looked upon it, or viewed it, (S, O, Msb, K, *) from above; (S, O, K;) [ I overlooked it, or looked down upon it: and I came in sight of it: got a view of it: and got knowledge of it; became acquainted with it; or knew it: all of which meanings may be intended to be conveyed by the explanation in the Msb, which is AiT~alaEotu Ealayohi :] and Al$~aYo'a ↓ $aArafotu signifies the same as A^a$orafotu Ealayohi [app. in the first of the senses expl. in this sentence, as well as in another sense expl. in what follows]: (S, O:) and ↓ $aArafuwhumo signifies the same as A^a$orafuwA Ealayohimo . (TA.) ― -b3- And A$rf EalaY Almawoti He (a sick man) was, or became, on the brink, or verge, or at the point, of death. (O, K.) And A$rf bihi EalaY Almawoti [ He made him to be on the brink, or verge, or at the point, of death ]. (T and K in art. *rf .) ― -b4- And A^a$orafato nafosuhu EalaY $aYo'K His soul was vehemently eager for a thing. (Mgh. [See also 10.]) A_i$oraAfN signifies The being eager, and the being vehemently eager: and hence the saying, in a trad., mano A^axa*a Ald~unoyaA biA_i$oraAfi nafosK lamo yubaArako lahu fiyhaA [ Whoso takes the enjoyments of the present world with eagerness, or vehement eagerness, of soul, he will not be blessed therein ]. (TA.) ― -b5- And A$rf Ealayohi He regarded him with solicitous affection or pity or compassion. (O, * K.) ― -b6- [And A$rf liY He, or it, came within sight, or view, to me; or came within a commanding, or near, view of me: see an ex. voce A^ajohada ; and another voce rabaA^a .] ― -b7- And [hence,] A$rf laka Al$~aYo'u The thing became, or has become, within thy power or reach; or possible, practicable, or easy, to thee. (TA.) -A2- See also 5, in two places.

(S, O, K.) A poet says, taTaAlalotu waA@sota$orafotuhu faraA^ayotuhu faqulotu lahu A=A^anota zayodu AlA^araAmili [ I stretched up myself, and raised my eyes towards him, expanding my hand over my eyebrow like him who is shading his eyes from the sun; and I said to him, Art thou Zeyd-el-Arámil? ]. (TA.) ― -b3- And yasota$orifu maEaAliYa AlA^umuwri (tropical:) He desires, or seeks, [or raises his eye to, ] the means of attaining eminence. (Msb in art. $wf .) ― -b4- Ast$rf A_ibilahumo means He (a man) smote their camels with the [ evil ] eye; syn. taEay~anahaA : (S, TA:) or he looked at them ( tEy~nhA ) to smite them with the [ evil ] eye. (TA.) ― -b5- Ast$rfhu Haq~ahu He defrauded him of his right, or due. (O, K.) -A2- See also 5: -A3- and 8.

sourceDefinition: Highness, elevation, exaltation, or eminence, [ in rank, condition, or estimation, in respect of religion or of worldly things: (see the first sentence of this art.:)] (S, O, Msb, K:) [generally meaning high birth: ] glory, honour, dignity, or nobility; syn. majodN : or not unless [ transmitted ] by ancestors: (K:) [for] accord. to ISk, $arafN and majodN may not be unless [transmitted] by ancestors; but HasabN and karamN may be in a man though he have not ancestors [endowed therewith]: (O:) or, (K,) accord. to IDrd, (O,) it signifies highness of Hasab [which means grounds of pretension to respect or honour, consisting in any qualities ( either of oneself or of one's ancestors ) which are enumerated, or recounted, as causes of glorying ]: (O, K:) and ↓ $urofapN signifies the same as $arafN ; (TA;) or the same as faDolN and $arafN [meaning a favour and a glory or an honour ]; as in the saying, A^aEud~u A_itoyaAnakumN $urofapF [ I reckon your coming a favour, and a glory or an honour ]; (O, K;) and A^araY *`lika $urofapF [ I regard that as a favour, and a glory or an honour ]: (O:) the pl. of $arafN is A^a$oraAfN , like as that of sababN is A^asobaAbN . (TA.) nuhobapN *aAtu $arafK means Spoil, or booty, of high value, at which men raise their eyes, and look, or which they smite with the [ evil ] eye: [see Aisota$orafa A_ibilahumo :] but the phrase is also related with s . (TA. See sarafN .) ― -b2- See also $ariyfN , with which, or with the pls. of which, it is said to be syn. ― -b3- Also An elevated place; an eminence: (S, Mgh, O, K:) accord. to Sh, any piece of ground that overtops what is around it, whether extended or not, only about ten cubits, or five, in length, of little or much breadth in its upper surface: (TA:) pl. A^a$oraAfN : (TA voce waTo'N :) and ma$aArifu AlA^aroDi signifies the high, or elevated, places, or parts, of the earth or ground: (S, Msb, K:) sing. ↓ ma$orafN , with fet-h to the m and r . (Msb. (O, TA: * in the former of which, the Pers. word here mentioned is written without the points to the P ; and in the latter, AldAbrnyAn .)

sourceDefinition: High, elevated, exalted, or eminent, (S, O, * Msb, K, TA,) [ in rank, condition, or estimation, ] in respect of religion or of worldly things: (TA:) [generally meaning high-born, or noble: ] possessing glory, honour, dignity, or nobility: or such, and having also [ such ] ancestry: (TA:) [using it as not implying highness, or nobility, of ancestry,] you say, huwa $ariyfN Alyawoma [ He is high, or noble, to-day ], and Eano qaliylK ↓ $aArifN as meaning one who will be $ariyf [ after a little while ]: (Fr, S, K:) the pl. [of pauc.] is A^a$oraAfN and [of mult.] $urafaA='u (S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ $arafN , so in the K, app. denoting that this last is one of the pls. of $ryf , and it is said in the O that $arafN is syn. with $urafaA='u ; but in the L it is said that it is syn. with $ariyfN ; and hence the saying huwa $arafu qawomihi meaning He is the $ariyf of his people, and karamuhumo meaning the kariym of them; and thus it has been expl. as used in a trad.: (TA:) [but both these assertions are probably correct; for it seems to be, agreeably with analogy, an inf. n. used as an epithet, and therefore applicable to a single person and to a pl. number, and also to two persons, and likewise to a female as well as to a male.] ― -b2- [By the modern Arabs, and the Turks and Persians, it is also applied, as a title of honour, to Any descendant of the Prophet; like say~id . And, with the article Al , particularly to the descendant of the Prophet who is The governor of Mekkeh; now always a vassal of the Turkish Sultán.]

definition: The ruw^aAn [now applied to darnel-grass (but see this latter word zw^An )] that is [ often found ] in wheat;
sourceDefinition: The ruw^aAn [now applied to darnel-grass (but see this latter word zw^An )] that is [ often found ] in wheat; also called ↓ $aAlamN (Msb, K) and ↓ $awolamN ; (K;) of Pers., or foreign, origin; ( A^aSoluhu A^aEojamiY~N ;) and it is said that one of its two extremities is sharp and the other thick: (Msb:) of the dial. of the Sawád: accord. to IAar, i. q. ziywaAn [sic.] and saEiyE : AHn says that it is a small, oblong, red, erect grain, resembling in form the suws [or grub ] of wheat; and it does not intoxicate, but renders the wheat very bitter: and in one place he says, the plant of the $ylm spreads upon the ground, and its leaves are like those of the xilaAf [or salix Aegyptia ] that is termed baloxiY~ , very green, and juicy, or tender; people eat its leaves when they are fresh, and they are pleasant [ to the taste ], without bitterness; but its grain is more intensely, or nauseously, bitter ( A^aEoqaY ) than aloes. (TA.) [Forskål, in his Flora Aegypt. Arab. p. 199, after describing the zw^An , says, “ $ylm etiam agri vitium; a priore tamen diversa species: decocto plantæ obtunduntur sensus hominis qui operationem chirurgicam subire debet; Avicenna sic referente. ” See also sakarapN .] -A2- [Golius says, on the authority of a gloss in a copy of the KL, that it signifies also A short, or little, avaricious, man; “ vir curtus, avarus: ” a meaning, if correct, app. tropical.]

definition: The fourteenth letter of the alphabet;
sourceDefinition: The fourteenth letter of the alphabet; called SaAdN . It is one of the letters termed mahomuwsap [or nonvocal, i. e. pronounced with the breath only, without the voice]; and of the letters termed A^asaliy~ap , as also z and s , because proceeding from the tip of the tongue; (TA;) and is one of the letters termed musotaEoliyap , which are obstacles to A_imaAlap : (M in art. Swd :) it is not conjoined with s , nor with z , [nor, as some say, with j , (see A_ij~aASN ,)] in any Arabic word. (TA. [See also art. Swd .]) It is a radical, and a substitute; not an augmentative. (M in art. Swd .) It is sometimes substituted for s ; and, as MF observes, what Ibn-Umm-Kásim says appears to mean that this substitution is allowable unrestrictedly; but Ibn-Málik, in the Tes-heel, makes it subject to conditions, saying that it is allowable accord. to a certain dial. when the s is followed by g or x or q or T , even when separated therefrom by a letter or by two letters: MF says that the dial. above mentioned is that of Benu-l-'Ambar, accord. to Sb and others; who give as exs. Sagiba for sagiba , and Saxira for saxira , and SaqabN for saqabN , and SaTaEa for saTaEa . (TA.) -A2- [As a numeral, S denotes Ninety. ]

Say^iY~N (S, M, K) and Siy^iY~N (Ks, M, K, TA) and Suy^iY~N , (Ks, K, TA,) said of a young bird and the like, (S, K,) of a bird and of a young bird (M) and of a rat or mouse (S, M) and of a jerboa (S) and of a cat and of a dog (M) and of a pig and of an elephant, (S, M,) It uttered a cry, or sound; (S, M, K;) as also ↓ taSaA='aY : (M, K:) and accord. to Fr, one says also of the scorpion, taSiYo'u and taSoy^iY . (S.) It is said in a prov., talodagu AlEaqorabu wataSoy^iY or wataSiYo'u , (As, S, Meyd,) this latter verb being formed by transposition, (Meyd,) i. e. The scorpion stings while uttering a cry; (S, Meyd;) the w being a denotative of state: (As, S:) applied to him who does wrong in the guise of him who complains of wrongdoing. (Meyd.) And one says also, jaA='a bimaA SaA^aY waSamata , (S, K,) and bimaA SaA='a waSamata (IAar, S, TA,) SaA='a being formed by tranposition from SaA^aY , (S,) He brought what was vocal and what was mute; (S, K;) such as slaves and beasts, and clothes and silver; (As, TA;) or sheep or goats, and camels, and gold and silver; (IAar, TA;) meaning he brought much property: and this is likewise a prov. (S.)

SiH~apN (S, * A, * MA, Msb, * MF, TA) and SuH~N , (S, * K, * MF, TA,) two forms of the inf. n. of which there are some other exs., as qil~apN and qul~N , and *il~apN and *ul~N , (MF, TA,) and SaHaAHN also, (K, * TA, * TK,) [like salaAmN &c.,] He was, or became, healthy, or sound; (MA;) or restored to health, or soundness, mino Eil~atihi [ from his disease ]; (S, A;) as also ↓ AstSH~ : (S:) or his disease departed. (K, TK.) And (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, [or proved, ] sound, valid, (MA,) [ substantial, real, sure, certain, ] true, right, (MA, Msb,) correct, just or proper, whole or entire, (MA,) or [ unmarred, or unimpaired, ] free from every imperfection or defect or fault or blemish, (L, K, TA,) and from everything that would occasion doubt or suspicion or evil opinion: (L, TA:) and (tropical:) it was, or became, suitable to the case, or event. (Msb.) You say, SaH~ato $ahaAdatuhu (tropical:) [ His testimony was sound, valid, &c.]. (A, TA.) And SaH~a qawoluhu (tropical:) [ His saying was, or proved, true ]. (A, TA.) And SaH~a Einoda AlqaADiY Haq~uhu (tropical:) [ His right, or due, or just claim, was, or became, established, substantiated, made good, or verified, in the estimation of the judge; like vabata ]. (A, TA.) And SaH~a lahu Ealayohi ka*aA (tropical:) [ Such a thing became established, or verified, as due to him from him; like vabata ]. (A, TA.) And SaH~a AlEaqodu (tropical:) The contract became established by its execution. (Msb,) And SaH~ati AlS~alaApu , as used by the lawyers, (tropical:) The prayer [ was suitable to the ordinance thereof, so that it ] annulled the obligation of performing it after the appointed time. (Msb, * and Dict. of Techn. Terms of the Mussalmans pp. 815-816. [This meaning is expressed in the former by the phrase A^asoqaTati AlqaDaA='a ; which is fully expl. in the latter work, with other conventional meanings of SiH~apN , all reducible to explanations given above.] -A2- SaH~a Al$~aYo'a [if not a mistranscription for A^aSaH~a or SaH~aHa ] signifies (assumed tropical:) He made the thing SaHiyH [i. e. sound, valid, &c.]. (L, TA. [In the latter app. taken from the former.])

definition: A man having his family and his cattle in a healthy, or sound, state;
sourceDefinition: A man having his family and his cattle in a healthy, or sound, state; whether he himself be in health or sick: (L:) or having his cattle in a healthy, or sound, state, after their having been affected by a plague, or murrain, or distemper: pl. muSiH~uwna . (S, L.) It is said in a trad., laA yuwridan~a *uw EaAhapK EalaY muSiH~K (S, L) i. e. One whose camels are affected by a murrain, or distemper, shall by no means bring them to water immediately after one whose camels are in a healthy, or sound, state, so as to water the former beasts with the latter: a prohibition apparently given for fear that the latter beasts should become diseased like the former, and it should be supposed that the disease had passed by contagion, which ought not to be imagined. (L. [See also mumoriDN .])

sourceDefinition: , (K,) inf. n. muSaAdaApN , (S,) He imitated him, or it; syn. EaAraDahu : (S, * K:) and he, or it, corresponded, and was equal, to him, or it. (TA.) In the Kur xxxviii. 1, some read SaAdi , with kesr, as an imperative from AlmuSaAdaApu (Bd, TA) as meaning AlmuEaAraDapu ; and hence AlS~adaY [i. e. the echo], because it imitates ( yuEaAriDu ) the first sound: so that the meaning is, Imitate thou ( EaAriD ) the Kur-án by thy works. (Bd.) ― -b2- [And] i. q. dab~arahu [i. e. He considered, or forecast, its issues, or results; did, performed, or executed, it with thought, or consideration; or managed, conducted, ordered, or regulated, it ]; relating to an affair: (M:) [or] AlmuSaAdaApu signifies the turning about, or revolving, the opinion, or idea, [ that one forms ] respecting the management ( tadobiyr ) of a thing, and the doing of it: (Ham p. 35:) [or,] accord. to As, the minding a thing attentively, carefully, or solicitously: a man who had assisted his she-camel in her bringing forth said, bit~u A^uSaAdiyhaA Tuwla layoliY [ I passed all my night minding her attentively, carefully, or solicitously ]; because he disliked binding her fore shank to her arm, as it would distress her; or leaving her, as she might go away at random and the wolf might devour her young one: and in like manner one says of the pastor, yuSaAdiY A_ibilahu [ He minds attentively, &c., his camels ]; when they thirst before the completion of their usual period of being kept from drinking, he restricts them to journeying by night so as to arrive at water on the morrow. (TA.) ― -b3- And He soothed, coaxed, wheedled, or cajoled, him; or deceived, deluded, beguiled, circumvented, or outwitted, him; or strove, endeavoured, or desired, to do so: syn. daAraAhu , (S, M, K, TA,) and daAjaAhu , and saAtarahu , (S, K, TA,) all of which have one meaning, (TA,) [though the last implies concealing enmity, ] and laAyanahu . (M.) mano SaAdaAka faqado SaAdaka [ He who soothes thee, or coaxes thee, surely ensnares thee ] is a saying mentioned in the A. (TA.)

definition: [sometimes written SadFA ] An echo;
sourceDefinition: [sometimes written SadFA ] An echo; i. e. AlS~adaY signifies what the mountain returns to him who utters a sound, or voice, or cry, therein; (K;) or the sound of the mountain and the like that responds to one; (M;) or what responds to one with the like of his voice, or cry, in the mountains &c. (S.) One says, Sam~a SadaAhu (tropical:) [ His echo became dumb, or may his echo become dumb ]; (S, TA;) meaning he perished, or may he perish: (S and K and TA in art. Sm :) and A^aSam~a A@ll~`hu SadaAhu (tropical:) [ May God make his echo to return no sound ]; (S, K, TA;) meaning may God destroy him: (S, K, and TA in art. Sm :) for when a man dies, the SdY hears not from him anything, that it should respond to him. (S. [See also another explanation of this saying in what follows.]) ― -b2- And A sound, voice, or cry, (M, TA,) in an absolute sense. (TA.) ― -b3- Also The part of the head, (M,) or the part of the brain, (TA,) which is the place [or seat ] of hearing. (M, TA.) And therefore one says, A^aSam~a A@ll~`hu SadaAhu [ May God render deaf the part of his brain which is the seat of hearing ]. (TA.) ― -b4- And The brain, (M, K, TA,) itself. (TA.) And The [ entire ] contents (lit. the stuffing, Ha$ow ,) of the head; (M, K, TA;) also called the haAmap . (TA.) One says, SadaEa A@ll~`hu SadaAhu [ May God crack his brain, or the contents of his head ]. (M.) ― -b5- And A bird that cries in the haAmap [or head ] of the slain when his blood has not been avenged by retaliation: (M:) or a bird that comes forth (M, K) from his head, ( mino raA^osihi , M,) or from the head of the slain, (K,) when he, or it, has become consumed, or decayed, (M, K,) also called the haAmap ; (M;) accord. to the assertion of the people of the Time of Ignorance; (M, K;) mentioned by A 'Obeyd; and some of them used to say that the bones of the dead became a haAmap , which flew: pl. A^aSodaA='N : (TA:) and [this may be meant by the saying that it signifies] the male of the buwm (S, M, K, TA) and haAm : pl. A^aSodaA='N : (M:) they used to say that when a man was slain and his blood was not avenged by retaliation, there came forth from his head a bird like the buwmap , i. e. the haAmap , the male being called the SdY ; and it cried upon his grave, AisoquwniY AisoquwniY [ Give ye me to drink, give ye me to drink, meaning, of the blood of the slayer]; and if the slayer was slain, it abstained from its crying: (TA:) and [it is said that] it signifies also the body [itself] of a human being after his death; (M, K;) or the remains of the dead in his grave, i. e. his juv~ap [or corpse ]. (Jm, TA.) ― -b6- And, (K,) accord. to El- 'Adebbes, (S,) [ A cricket; ] a certain flying thing, that creaks by night, and hops, (S, K,) and flies, thought by the [ common ] people to be the junodab , but it is only the SdY , the jndb being smaller than the SdY . (S. [See also AlS~ar~aAru .]) ― -b7- And A certain fish, black, long, (K, TA,) and bulky: n. un. SadaApN . (TA.) ― -b8- And [A man] small, or slender, in person; (AA, M, K, TA;) and so SadaA^o , with ' , as mentioned by Az. (TA. [See also SadoEN and SadaEN .]) ― -b9- And Knowing in respect of what is conducive to the good of cattle: (K:) or SadaY maAlK means thus: (M:) or gentle in the management of cattle; like A_izaA='u maAlK : so in the Jm: (TA:) or, as some particularly say, of camels: (M, TA:) [i. e.] you say, A_in~ahu laSadaY A_ibilK , meaning Verily he is knowing in respect of camels, and of what is conducive to their good. (S.) -A2- Also Thirst: (S, M, K:) or vehement thirst: (M:) [see the first paragraph, in which it is mentioned as an inf. n.:] it is said that thirst does not become vehement but the brain dries, and therefore the skin of the forehead of him who dies of thirst cracks. (TA.) ― -b2- See also the next paragraph. -A3- And The act of the mutaSad~iY , (M, K, TA,) i. e., [as is indicated in the M,] of him who raises his head and breast, looking towards, or regarding, a thing; and so ↓ SadaApN . (TA.)

definition: The vehemence of the midday-heat in summer: (K:) or the most vehement heat of midday in summer: (S:) and it is prefixed to EumaY~ : (K:) one says, laqiyutuh Sak~apa EumaY~K , (S, O,) a prov.
sourceDefinition: The vehemence of the midday-heat in summer: (K:) or the most vehement heat of midday in summer: (S:) and it is prefixed to EumaY~ : (K:) one says, laqiyutuh Sak~apa EumaY~K , (S, O,) a prov., meaning I met him in the most vehement heat of midday in summer when the heat almost blinded by its vehemence: (Lh, O, TA:) for EumaY~ is said to be an abbreviated dim. of A^aEomaY : (S, O, TA:) and by it is said to be meant the gazelle, because he is dazzled and confounded in the midday-heats of summer, and knocks against the thing that is before him: some say, Sak~apa HumaY~K , from Hamiyati Al$~amosu : and some assert that EumaY~ means the heat, itself: (O, TA:) or it is the name of a certain man [as will be found expl. in art. EmY , with variations of this saying]. (S, O, K, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. yaSuwru , (S, M, K,) inf. n. SaworN , (M, K,) He made it (a thing, M, K, or, as some say, specially the neck, M) to incline, or lean; (S, M, K;) as also SArhu , aor. yaSiyru ; (S;) and ↓ ASArhu : (S, M, Msb, K:) or he demolished it threw it down, or pulled it down to the ground; as also ↓ ASArhu . (K.) One says, of a man, yaSuwro Eunuqahu A_ilaY Al$~aYo'i He inclines his neck to the thing. (Lth.) And Surotu A_ilaY~a Al$~aYo'a , and ↓ A^aSarotuhu , I inclined, or bent, the thing to, or towards, me. (El-Ahmar.) And Surotu AlguSona liA^ajotaniYa Alv~amara [ I inclined, or bent, the branch, that I might pluck, or gather, the fruit ]. (A.) And quluwbN laA taSuwruhaA AlA^aroHaAmu (assumed tropical:) [ Hearts which the ties of relationship do not incline ]. (TA, from a trad.) faSurohun~a A_ilayoka , in the Kur [ii. 262], means And turn them towards thee; and so faSirohun~a : (Akh, S, M:) but the former is the more common reading: this is the meaning commonly known, of each reading: though Lh says that the former means as above, and the latter means cut them, and divide them, in pieces; (M;) and some thus explain the former, making a transposition in the verse, as though the words were thus, faxu*o A_ilayoka A^arobaEapF mina A@lT~~ayori faSurohun~a . (S.) One says also, Suro A_ilaY~a , and Suro wajohaka A_ilaY~a , Turn thou thy face towards me. (Akh, S.) And SaAra wajohahu , aor. yaSuwru , (M, K,) and yaSiyru , (K,) He turned his face towards a person or thing. (M, K.) And huwa yaSuwra maEoruwfahu A_ilaY Aln~aAsi (tropical:) [ He turns his beneficence towards men ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [Agreeably with a statement cited above, it is said that] SaArahu , aor. as above, (S, K,) and so the inf. n., (TA,) signifies also He dissected it; or cut it, or divided it, in pieces. (S, K, TA.) ― -b3- And hence, (TA,) SaAra AlHukoma (assumed tropical:) He (the judge, A, TA) decided the judgment. (S, * A, TA.) ― -b4- [Freytag states, on the authority of the Kitáb el-Addád, that SAr , aor. as above, has two contr. significations: He separated, or dispersed: ― -b5- and He collected. ] ― -b6- See also 2. -A2- SaAra also signifies He (a man, M) uttered a cry, or sound. (M, K.) -A3- Sawira , (M, A, K,) [aor. yaSowaru ,] inf. n. SawarN , (S, M, A,) He, (Lth,) or it, (a thing, M, Msb, K, or a man's neck, M, A, *) inclined, or leaned; (Lth, S, * M, A, K;) as also ↓ AnSAr : (S, M, Msb, K: *) it bent; or was, or became, crooked. (A.) One says, fiY Eunuqihi SawarN In his neck is an inclining; and a bending, or crookedness. (A.) ― -b2- And SawarN as an attribute of a man signifies also (tropical:) An inclining, or inclination; (S;) a desiring, or desire. (S, Msb.)

definition: Form, fashion, figure, shape, or semblance;
sourceDefinition: Form, fashion, figure, shape, or semblance; syn. $akolN , (M, K,) and mivaAlN ; (Msb;) the external state of a thing; (IAth;) that whereby a thing is sensibly distinguished by men in general, and even by many other animate beings, from other things; as the Swrp of a man, and of a horse, and of an ass. (B.) ― -b2- And An effigy; an image, or a statue; a picture; anything that is formed, fashioned, figured, or shaped, after the likeness of any of God's creatures, animate or inanimate: it is said that the maker of an effigy, or image, will be punished on the day of resurrection, and will be commanded to put life into it; and that the angels will not enter a house in which is a Swrp . (Mgh.) [See also taSaAwiyru .] ― -b3- [Hence, A mental image; or a resemblance, of any object, formed, or conceived, by the mind; an idea: a meaning of frequent occurrence in philosophical works &c.] ― -b4- And Species; syn. nawoEN . (K.) ― -b5- And The essence of a thing; that by being which a thing is what it is; or the property, or quality, or the aggregate of properties or qualities, whereby a thing is what it is; syn. HaqiyqapN : (IAth:) [ specific character; ] that whereby a thing is mentally distinguished by particular persons, not by the vulgar, from other things; as the Swrp by which a man is specially distinguished, consisting in reason and thought and other distinctive attributes: (B:) a quality, an attribute, a property; or a description, as meaning the aggregate of the qualities or attributes or properties, of a thing; or the state, condition, or case, of a thing; syn. SifapN : (IAth, Msb, K:) as when you say, Suwrapu AlA^amori ka*aA [ The quality, &c., of the thing is of such a kind ]: (IAth, Msb:) and Suwrapu AlmasoA^alapi ka*aA [ The description, statement, or form, of the question is of such a kind ]: (Msb:) and so in the saying of the Prophet, A^ataAniY All~ayolapa rab~iY fiY A^aHosani SuwrapK [ My Lord came to me to-night in a most goodly state ]; or Swrp may here refer to the Prophet, and may mean external state, or manner of being, or condition. (IAth.) ― -b6- And The mode, or manner, of an action. (IAth.) ― -b7- The pl. is SuwarN (S, M, Msb, K) and SiwarN and SuwrN ; (S, M, K;) the second of which is rare, and by some disallowed. (MF.) ― -b8- The saying of the Prophet xalaqa A@ll~`hu A=dama EalaY Suwratihi may mean that God created Adam in the Swrp [or form &c.] that He, namely, God, originated and ordained; or in the Swrp proper to him, namely, Adam. (M.) ― -b9- SuwrapN signifies also The face: so in a trad. cited voce muHar~amN ; in which it is said that the Swrp is pronounced sacred, i. e. that it is not to be slapped: and in another, in which it is said that the Prophet disliked marking the Swrp with a hot iron. (TA.)

(tropical:) [ The pool of water left by a torrent ] glistened by reason of its fulness. (TA.) ― -b5- [And DaHika vagoruhu (assumed tropical:) His front teeth, or his teeth, glistened by reason of his laughing; meaning he laughed so as to show his front teeth, or his teeth. ] ― -b6- And DaHika Alz~ahoru (tropical:) The flowers [ looked gay, or] were as though they were laughing. (TA.) And DaHikati AlA^aroDu (tropical:) The earth, or land, put forth its plants, or herbage, and its flowers. (TA.) And DaHikati Alr~iyaADu Eani AlA^azohaAri (tropical:) The meadows, or gardens, displayed the flowers. (TA.) ― -b7- And DaHikati Aln~axolapu (tropical:) The palm-tree put forth [or disclosed ] its DaHok ; as also ↓ A^aDoHakat ; (TA;) [i. e.] the spathe of the palm-tree, (Skr, O, TA,) that covered the TaloE [or spadix ], (O,) burst open. (Skr, O, TA.) And DaHika AlT~aloEu (tropical:) The TlE [here app. meaning the spathe of the palm-tree ] split, or clave, open; and so tabas~ama . (TA.) ― -b8- And, as some assert, (ISd, TA,) DaHikato signifies also (tropical:) She menstruated; said of a hare; (ISd, Z, O, Msb, TA;) accord. to some, from the DaH~aAk [meaning the interior] of the TaloEap [of the palm-tree] when it bursts open; (ISd, TA;) and hence, (K, TA,) said also in this sense of a woman, (O, Msb, K, TA,) accord. to Mujáhid, (O, TA,) and some others, (TA,) in the Kur xi. 74, (O, K, TA,) where some read faDaHakato , which is said to be a well-known dial. var.; (TA;) and likewise, accord. to some, said in this sense of the hyena, (O, TA,) when she sees blood, or as IAar says, when she eats the flesh of men and drinks their blood: (TA:) [it is commonly asserted by the Arabs that] the hare menstruates like women: (Kzw:) but with respect to this meaning as assigned to the verb in the Kur xi. 74, Fr says that he had not heard it from any person deserving of confidence; (O, TA; *) and Zj says that it is nought: both say that the meaning there is, she laughed by reason of happiness: (TA:) and some say that there is an inversion in this case, what is meant being faba$~aronaAhaA biA_isoH`qa faDaHikato : (Fr, O, TA:) or the meaning is, she wondered; so says I'Ab; and so Er-Rághib, who adds that it is confirmed by her saying, “ shall I bring forth a child when I am an old woman, and this my husband is an old man? verily this is indeed a wonderful thing: ” and that faHaADato which is inserted by some of the expositors after faDaHikato is not an explanation of this expression, as some of them have imagined it to be, but is the mention of [a fact which was] a sign that the announcement was not that of an event improbable: or the meaning is, she was frightened; so says Fr.: (TA:) and with respect to the meaning of this verb when said of the hyena, mentioned above, it is rejected by AHát and others: (TA:) IDrd says, on the authority of AHát, respecting the following verse of TaäbbataSharrà, taDoHaku AlD~aboEu liqatolaY hu*ayolK wataraY Al*~iy^oba lahaA yasotahil~u that the meaning is (assumed tropical:) The hyena displays her teeth, or grins, on account of the slain [ of Hudheyl ], when she sees them, like as they say of the ass when he plucks out the [plant called] Sil~iyaAnap ; (O, TA;) or, as others say, (assumed tropical:) the hyena snarls, displaying her teeth; and sees the wolf raising his voice in calling the [other] wolves to them, i. e. to the slain: (O, TA:*) Abu-l-' Abbás says that the meaning is, (assumed tropical:) the hyena displays her teeth, because the wolf contends with her over the slain: and some say that the poet means, (assumed tropical:) the hyena rejoices because of the slain. (TA.) ― -b9- One says also, DaHikati Als~amurapu , meaning (assumed tropical:) The smrp [or gum-acacia-tree ] flowed with its gum: from DHkt meaning “ she menstruated. ” (Bd in xi. 74.)

(A.) This is the primary signification. (L.) And Damada raA^osahu , (L,) or biDimaAdK ↓ Dm~dhu , (Lth,) He wound a piece of rag round his head, after anointing it, or wetting it with water: (Lth, L:) and ↓ Dm~d raA^osahu , inf. n. taDomiydN , He bound his head with a fillet, or bandage, (S, A,) or a kerchief, (A,) or a piece of cloth, not a turban. (S.) And Damada AljuroHa , inf. n. DamodN , also signifies He applied a remedy [or dressing ] to the wound, without bandaging it. (L.) And Eayonayohi biAlS~abiri ↓ Dm~d He applied aloes to his eyes. (L, from a trad.) And Damadaha biAlz~aEofaraAni waAlS~abiri He smeared him, or it, over, [or poulticed him, or it, ] with saffron and aloes. (Az, L.) ― -b2- And AuDomudo Ealayoka viyaAbaka Bind thou upon thee thy garments, (Ibn-Málik, A,) and EimaAmataka [ thy turban ]. (A.) (L.) ― -b3- And Damadahu (assumed tropical:) He struck him, or hit him, on his head with a staff or stick: (S, K:) sometimes used in this sense: (S:) or he cut, or wounded, (A, L,) him (L,) or it, i. e. his head, (A,) in the place of the turban, with a sword; syn. Eam~amahu . (A, L.) ― -b4- DamodN also signifies (assumed tropical:) The treating with gentleness, or blandishment; soothing, coaxing, wheedling, or cajoling; or striving, endeavouring, or desiring, to do so. (S, L.) And one says, DamadaAhaA (assumed tropical:) They both associated as friends [or lovers ] with her, or made love to her. (L.) -A2- Damida , aor. , It dried; (Hr, L, K;) said of blood upon the throat of a slaughtered sheep or goat. (Hr, L.) -A3- Also, inf. n. DamadN , He acted wrongfully, or injuriously, or unjustly. And He was angry with him: or vehemently enraged against him and angry with him: or he was enraged against him; i. e. one over whom he had power to vent his rage. (L.)

definition: He, or it, sought, or demanded, Tarab [i.
sourceDefinition: He, or it, sought, or demanded, Tarab [i. e. emotion, or a lively emotion, &c.], (K, TA,) and diversion, sport, or play. (TA.) ― -b2- And They (a party, or company of men,) became affected with intense Tarab . (A, TA.) -A2- AstTrb AlA_ibila He put in motion the camels by urging them with singing. (K.) You say AstTrb AlHudaApu AlA_ibila [ The drivers, singing to them, excited, moved, or stirred, the camels, ] when the camels have become lively, brisk, sprightly, or agile, because of their urging them with singing. (O, TA.) Az cites the saying of Et-Tirimmáh, waA@sotaTorabato ZuEonuhumo lam~aA A@HozaA^al~a bihimo A=lu AlD~uHaY naA$iTFA mino daAEibaAti dadi but in his poem it is waA@sotaTorafato , with faA' [i. e. with the letter f ]: (O:) [this latter reading is, I doubt not, the right; and the meaning seems to be, And their women borne in the camel-vehicles, when the mirage of the early part of the forenoon elevated them to the eye, elicited anew longing desire for their homes, or accustomed places, from jocose, sportful females, lit., from jesting females of sport or diversion: the verse as cited by Az may admit of a similar rendering if we suppose AstTrbt to be there used tropically: the writer of my copy of the TA has endeavoured, in marginal notes in the present art. and in art. dd , but in my opinion unsatisfactorily, to explain it; and has supposed AstTrbt to mean Taribat : his two notes, moreover, are inconsistent:] naA$iTFA in this verse means $awoqFA naAziEFA . (K in art. dd . (A, TA.)

definition: Emotion, or a lively emotion, or excitement, agitation, or unsteadiness, ( xif~apN , S, A, Msb, K,) [ of the heart or mind, ] by reason of joy or grief, (A, K,) or of intense grief or joy, (S,) or of...
sourceDefinition: Emotion, or a lively emotion, or excitement, agitation, or unsteadiness, ( xif~apN , S, A, Msb, K,) [ of the heart or mind, ] by reason of joy or grief, (A, K,) or of intense grief or joy, (S,) or of intense fear or joy: (Msb:) or joy, mirth, or gladness: and the contr., i. e. grief, sadness, or sorrow: (Th, K:) or, as some say, the lodgement of joy, mirth, or gladness, and departure of grief, sadness, or sorrow: so in the M: (TA:) the vulgar apply it peculiarly to joy; (Msb;) [but] the application of it peculiarly to joy is a mistake: (K:) it signifies also motion; syn. HarakapN : (K:) it is said in the M, Th says that AlT~arabu is derived from AlHarakapu ; whence it seems that AlT~arabu is, in his opinion, syn. with AlHarakapu ; but [ISd adds] I know not this: (TA:) [it does, however, obviously imply the signification of motion, either ideal or actual:] also desire, or yearning or longing of the soul: (K:) the pl. is A^aToraAbN . (TA.) A poet says, (S,) namely, En-Nábighah El-Jaadee, using it in relation to anxiety, (TA,) fiY A_ivorihimo ↓ waA^araAniY TaribFA Taraba AlwaAlihi A^awo kaA@lomuxotabalo [ And I perceive myself to be affected with emotion, or a lively emotion, after them, (i. e. after the loss of them,) with the emotion of him who is bereft of offspring or friends, or like him who is insane in mind ]: (S, TA:) AlwaAlih here signifies Alv~aAkil ; and Almuxotabal means mano jun~a fiY Eaqolihi . (TA.) -A2- And [the pl.] A^aToraAbN signifies Choice sweet-smelling plants: (K:) or [simply] sweet-smelling plants: (TA:) and the more fragrant of such plants. (O, TA.)

sourceDefinition: Affected with Tarab [i. e. emotion, or a lively emotion, &c.]: (S, A, O, Msb, TA:) pl. TiraAbN . sourceDefinition: , [aor. ,] inf. n. Tal~N , The sky rained small rain upon the earth, or land. (MA.) And Tul~ati AlA^aroDu , (S, O, K,) inf. n. as above, (TA,) [meaning, as is implied in the S and O, The earth, or land, was rained upon by the weakest of rain; or was rained upon, or bedewed, by the Tal~ , q. v.; or] the Tal~ descended upon the earth, or land: (K:) and Tal~ahaA Aln~adaY [ The rain, or dew, moistened it ]: (S, O, TA:) and Tal~at , with fet-h, signifies [accord. to some] It became moist, or moistened: one says, Tul~ato bilaAduka , and Tal~ato ; the former meaning May thy countries, or tracts of country, be rained upon; and the latter, become moist, or moistened: or, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, [i. e. Zj,] Tul~ato only, with damm; [and he adds,] one says, raHubato bilaAduka waTul~ato , with damm, [i. e. May thy tracts of country be spacious to thee, and be moistened by the Tal~ , (or, as in art. rHb in the TA, A^aroHabato Ealayoka waTul~ato )], not Tal~ato ; because the Tal~ is not from them, [i. e. it is not from the tracts of country,] but they are the objects thereof. (TA.) [Golius mentions, among the significations of Tal~a , as on the authority of Z, i. q. rHb , said of land, or the earth, and followed by ElY relating to a person: but I think it most probable that he inferred this signification from his finding, in a copy of the A, the phrase raHubato Ealayoka AlA^aroSu waTal~ato (for waTul~ato ), without any explanation. And Freytag mentions ↓ A^uTil~a as meaning It was watered by fine rain; from the Deewán of the Hudhalees.] And [it is said that] Tal~ati Als~amaA='u signifies Ai$otad~a waqoEuhaA [i. e. The rain fell vehemently ]. (TA.) -A2- Tal~a damahu , (AZ, S, O, Msb,) said of God, (S,) or of the ruling power, (Msb,) first pers. Talalotuhu , (K,) aor. , (Msb,) inf. n. Tal~N (Msb, K) and TuluwlN , (K,) He made his blood to go for nought, unretaliated, and uncompensated by a mulct; made it to be of no account: (AZ, S, O, Msb, K, TA:) or held it to be of little account, as though it were but [ the rain, or dew, termed ] Tal~ , in its result; this, accord. to Er-Rághib, being the proper meaning: (TA:) and ↓ ATl~hu signifies the same. (AZ, S, O, Msb, K.) And Tul~a damuhu His blood was made to go for nought, &c.; (AZ, S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) as also damuhu ↓ A^uTil~a : (AZ, S, O, Msb, K:) and Tal~a damuhu , (S, O, Msb, K,) with fet-h, accord. to Ks and AO, (S, O, Msb,) aor. [contr. to analogy], (Msb,) or [agreeably with analogy]; (K;) and Tal~a , originally Talila , (Msb, K, *) aor. ; (Msb, K;) [ his blood went for nought, &c.;] but this is disallowed by AZ; (S, O, Msb;) and it is more commonly with damm. (K.) ― -b2- And Tal~ahu Haq~ahu , aor. , He diminished, or impaired, to him his right, or due; or deprived, or defrauded him of it, partly, or wholly: (K, TA:) or, accord. to Khálid Ibn-Jembeh, (TA,) he denied him, or refused him, his right, or due; (K, TA;) and withheld it [ from him ]: (TA:) and he annulled it; or made it to go for nought, as a thing of no account, or as a thing that had perished or become lost. (K, TA.) You say, Tal~uwA fulaAnFA Haq~ahu , aor. , inf. n. Tal~N , They denied, or refused, such a one his right, or due: so says Khálid Ibn-Jembeh. (O.) ― -b3- And Tal~a gariymahu , (K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. Tal~N , (O, K,) He delayed, or deferred, with his creditor, or put him off, by promising time after time to pay him. (O, * K.) ― -b4- And Tal~N signifies also The driving of camels roughly, or rigorously. (K.) You say, Tal~a AlA_ibila , inf. n. Tal~N , He drove the camels roughly, or rigorously! (TK.) -A3- Tal~a , [sec. pers. Talilota , aor. ,] inf. n. TalaAlapN ; like mal~a , [sec. pers. malilota , aor. ,] (K, TA,) inf. n. malaAlapN ; (TA;) [accord. to Freytag, followed by lahu , and in the Deewán of the Hudhalees by A_ilayohi ; and so, accord. to him, ↓ AstTl~ , followed by lahu ;] He, or it, was, or became, pleasing, (K, TA,) and goodly. (TA.) -A4- And Tal~ahu , (K,) inf. n. Tal~N , (TA,) is also syn. with TalaAhu : (K:) so in the phrase Tal~ahu biAlwarosi [ He smeared it, or rubbed it over, with wrs , q. v.]; namely, a thing. (Ibn-'Abbád, O.)

(O.) ― -b2- [Hence, perhaps,] ATl~ Alz~amaAnu (assumed tropical:) The time drew near. (TA.) -A4- An Arab woman of the desert is related to have said, maA A^aTal~a $iEora jamiylK waA^aHolaAhu [ How pleasing is the poetry of Jemeel, and how sweet is it! ]. (TA.)

definition: A portion still standing of the remains of a dwelling or house;
sourceDefinition: A portion still standing of the remains of a dwelling or house; (S, O, Msb, * K;) as also ↓ TalaAlapN : (K:) pl. A^aTolaAlN and TuluwlN , (S, O, Msb, K,) the latter pl. sometimes used: (Msb:) what cleaves to the ground is termed rasomN : (TA:) the people of the towns or villages apply the term A^aTolaAlN to the remains of walls and of places of worship; and the people of the tents to [the remains of ] places of eating and of drinking and of sleeping: (Ham p. 541:) [and] as pl. of TalalN it signifies elevated places: one says, raA^ayotu Talala Alqaroyapi , meaning I saw what was elevated of the land of the town, or village. (Har p. 139.) ― -b2- And The $axoS [or body, or bodily or corporeal form or figure or substance, such as one sees from a distance, ] of a thing, (Msb, K,) whatever it be; as also ↓ TalaAlapN : pl. of the former as above: (K:) the $axoS [as meaning body, or person, ] of a man; as also ↓ TalaAlapN : (S, O:) or, of a man, the erect $axoS . (Msb voce juv~apN .) And ZalaAlapN , with Z , signifies the same. (O and K in art. Zl .) One says, Hay~aA A@ll~`hu Talalaka and ↓ TalaAlataka , meaning [ May God preserve, or save, ] thy $axoS [i. e. body, or person ]. (S, O.) And Hay~aA A@ll~`hu Talalaka and A^aTolaAlaka , meaning maA $axaSa mino jasadika [i. e. May God preserve, or save, what has risen into view of thy body, or person ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A place in the SaHon [or court ] of a house, prepared for the household to sit upon: ADk says that there was a place on which to eat and drink in the finaA=' [or yard ] of every house, called the Talal : (Az, TA:) accord. to ISd, (TA,) the Talal of a house is, or was, like the [ kind of wide bench, of stone or brick &c., generally built against a wall, called ] duk~aAnap [or duk~aAn ], upon which to sit. (K, TA.) ― -b4- And The jilaAl [or deck ] of a ship or boat; (M, Mgh, O, K;) i. e. (Mgh) the covering thereof, which is like the roof (Mgh, Msb) of a house or chamber: (Mgh:) pl. A^aTolaAlN . (Mgh, Msb, TA.) [In the TA it is said to mean the $iraAE of a ship or boat; which is a mistake, as is sufficiently shown by its being there immediately added, “ hence the trad. of Aboo-Bekr, that he used to pray upon the ATlAl of the ship or boat. ”] ― -b5- [Hence, app.,] one says, (of a man, Ibn-'Abbád, O,) ma$aY EalaY Talali AlmaA='i i. e. ElY Zahorihi , (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) which, Z says, means ElY wajohihi [i. e. (tropical:) He walked, or went along, upon the surface of the water: but whether this relates to a pretended miracle or to sliding upon ice, I know not]: and he adds that it is a tropical phrase. (TA.) -A2- Also Anything fresh, or juicy, or [like Tal~N ] moist; syn. TariY~N . (K.) ― -b2- See also Tal~N , first sentence.

definition: , aor. , inf. n. ZaloEN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) said of a camel, (S, O, Msb, K,) and of a man also, (Msb, TA,) and, by Aboo-Dhu-eyb, of a horse, (S, TA,) [and likewise said of a dog, (see ZaAliEN ,)]...
sourceDefinition: , aor. , inf. n. ZaloEN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) said of a camel, (S, O, Msb, K,) and of a man also, (Msb, TA,) and, by Aboo-Dhu-eyb, of a horse, (S, TA,) [and likewise said of a dog, (see ZaAliEN ,)] He limped, or halted, syn. gamaza fiY ma$oyihi , (S, O, Msb, K, TA,) and Earija ; (TA;) or was slightly lame: (Mgh:) what it signifies resembles EarajN [or natural lameness], and therefore it is said to be a slight Earaj . (Msb.) One says, Airoqa EalaY ZaloEika , (S, O, L, K,) a prov., (O, L,) meaning Ascend thou the mountain with knowledge [or because ] of thy limping, or slight lameness, not jading thyself: (L:) or deal gently with thyself, and burden not thyself with more than thou art able to do: (S:) or impose upon thyself, of what is difficult, [ only ] what thou art able to do; for he who ascends a ladder or stair, or a mountain, when he is one who limps, or has a slight lameness, deals gently with himself; i. e. exceed not thy proper limit in thy threatening, but see thy deficiency, and thine impotence to execute it: (O, K: *) and some say AiroqaA^o , with, meaning rectify thine affair first; (O, K;) or as meaning abstain, and restrain thyself; (O;) or, accord. to AZ, abstain thou, for I know thy vices, or faults: (TA:) or the meaning of both is, be silent, because, or in consideration, of the fault that is in thee. (Ks, O, K. *) One says also, Airoqi EalaY ZaloEika , with kesr to the q , [meaning Charm thou thy slight lameness, to cure it, ] from Alr~uqoyapu : and it is said in another prov., Airoqi EalaY ZaloEika A^ano yuhaADaA [app. meaning Charm thou thy slight lameness, that it may become mitigated: see art. hyD : the final A in yhADA being what is termed A^alifu AlA_iTolaAqi , not a radical]. (O, K.) And qi EalaY ZaloEika [ Be cautious, because, or in consideration, of thy limping ]: said when there is a vice, or fault, in a man, and you chide him in order that it may not be called to mind: (O, K: [for ya*okura in the CK, I read yu*okara , as in other copies of the K and in the O:]) and to this he replies, or may reply, waqayotu . (TA. [See also art. wqY .]) And AirobaEo EalaY ZaloEika [ Act gently, or with deliberation, or restrain thyself, because of thy limping ]; meaning thou art weak; therefore refrain from that which thou art not able to do. (O, K. [See also art. rbE .]) And laA yarobaEu EalaY ZaloEika mano layosa yaHozunuhu A^amoruka , meaning He will not mind thine affair (Hr, O, K) whom thy condition does not grieve: (Hr, O:) or, originally, he will not pause because of thy limping, when thou laggest behind thy companions on account of thy weakness, who does not care for thy case. (Hr, O, K. * [See, again, art. rbE .]) ― -b2- Also, said of a man, (tropical:) He stopped short, and lagged behind. (TA.) ― -b3- ZalaEati AlA^aroDu biA^aholihaA (tropical:) The land became straitened with its inhabitants, by reason of their multitude; (A 'Obeyd, S, O, K;) it would not bear them, by reason of their multitude, like the beast that limps with its load because of its heaviness. (Z, TA.) ― -b4- ZalaEat said of a bitch, (tropical:) She desired copulation. (As, O, K, TA.) And ZalaEa said of a dog, (assumed tropical:) He desired to copulate. (TA.) -A2- ZalaEato EayonahaA She (a woman) contracted and inclined her eye. (TA.)

(Msb.) One says, Airoqa EalaY ZaloEika , (S, O, L, K,) a prov., (O, L,) meaning Ascend thou the mountain with knowledge [or because ] of thy limping, or slight lameness, not jading thyself: (L:) or deal gently with thyself, and burden not thyself with more than thou art able to do: (S:) or impose upon thyself, of what is difficult, [ only ] what thou art able to do; for he who ascends a ladder or stair, or a mountain, when he is one who limps, or has a slight lameness, deals gently with himself; i. e. exceed not thy proper limit in thy threatening, but see thy deficiency, and thine impotence to execute it: (O, K: *) and some say AiroqaA^o , with, meaning rectify thine affair first; (O, K;) or as meaning abstain, and restrain thyself; (O;) or, accord. to AZ, abstain thou, for I know thy vices, or faults: (TA:) or the meaning of both is, be silent, because, or in consideration, of the fault that is in thee. (Ks, O, K. *) One says also, Airoqi EalaY ZaloEika , with kesr to the q , [meaning Charm thou thy slight lameness, to cure it, ] from Alr~uqoyapu : and it is said in another prov., Airoqi EalaY ZaloEika A^ano yuhaADaA [app. meaning Charm thou thy slight lameness, that it may become mitigated: see art. hyD : the final A in yhADA being what is termed A^alifu AlA_iTolaAqi , not a radical]. (O, K.) And qi EalaY ZaloEika [ Be cautious, because, or in consideration, of thy limping ]: said when there is a vice, or fault, in a man, and you chide him in order that it may not be called to mind: (O, K: [for ya*okura in the CK, I read yu*okara , as in other copies of the K and in the O:]) and to this he replies, or may reply, waqayotu . (TA. [See also art. wqY .]) And AirobaEo EalaY ZaloEika [ Act gently, or with deliberation, or restrain thyself, because of thy limping ]; meaning thou art weak; therefore refrain from that which thou art not able to do. (O, K. [See also art. rbE .]) And laA yarobaEu EalaY ZaloEika mano layosa yaHozunuhu A^amoruka , meaning He will not mind thine affair (Hr, O, K) whom thy condition does not grieve: (Hr, O:) or, originally, he will not pause because of thy limping, when thou laggest behind thy companions on account of thy weakness, who does not care for thy case. (Hr, O, K. * [See, again, art. rbE .]) ― -b2- Also, said of a man, (tropical:) He stopped short, and lagged behind. (Z, TA.) ― -b4- ZalaEat said of a bitch, (tropical:) She desired copulation. (As, O, K, TA.) And ZalaEa said of a dog, (assumed tropical:) He desired to copulate. (TA.) -A2- ZalaEato EayonahaA She (a woman) contracted and inclined her eye. (TA.)

definition: Limping, or halting;
sourceDefinition: Limping, or halting; [or slightly lame; ] applied to a camel, and a horse, [&c.,] (S,) [i. e.,] to a beast, (TA,) to the male and the female alike, (Lth, O, K, TA,) to the former as a part. n., and to the latter as a possessive noun, (TA,) like gaAmizN ; (Lth, O, TA;) or the fem. of ZaAliEN is ZaAliEapN , (S, O, K, TA,) but one does not say gaAmizapN : (O, TA:) [pl. Zul~aEN .] One says, laA A^anaAmu Hat~aY yanaAma ZaAliEu AlkilaAbi [ I will not sleep until the limping dog sleeps ]; (O, K;) a prov., (O,) meaning, until the dogs become still; (O, K;) because the ZAlE , of dogs, waits until there remains none other, and then copulates, and sleeps: (As, O, K:) ― -b2- or the ZAlE is the dog that is lusting for the female; for such does not sleep; and the saying is applied to him who is mindful of his affair, who does not neglect it: ― -b3- or the bitch that is lusting for the male; because the dogs follow her, and will not let her sleep. (O, K.) ― -b4- Also Inclining, or declining: (O, K:) like DaAliEN . (TA.) ― -b5- And [ Declining from the truth, or from that which is right; (see ZalaEN ;)] committing a sin, crime, fault, or misdeed. (TA.) ― -b6- And Suspected. (S, O, K.) -A2- In the saying of Ru-beh, faA_ino tuxaAlijona AlEuyuwna AlZ~ul~aEaA [ And if ye women vie with the contracted and inclined eyes ], he means AlmaZoluwEapa , [see 1, last sentence,] using the word in the manner of a possessive noun. (TA.)

One says, Eabavati AlmaroA^apu , meaning The woman poured out what was moist of the [ preparation of curd called ] A^aqiT , when it was cooked, on what was dry thereof, upon the [ mat, or cloth, called ] ma$ar~ , or mi$ar~ , [the former accord. to the O and a copy of the S, and the latter accord. to another copy of the S,] in order that what was dry thereof might bear [ and not suffer to pass through the m$r~ ] what was moist. (Aboo-Sá'id El-Kilábee, S, O.) And Eabava AlA^aqiTa , aor. and inf. n. as above, He dried the AqT in the sun: or he mixed it with clarified butter: and gabavahu , with g , is a dial. var. thereof. (TA.) -A2- Eabiva , aor. , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) inf. n. EabavN , (S, Mgh, O, Msb,) He played, or sported; (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K;) and mingled together unprofitable actions; (Mgh;) or and did that in which was no profit; (Msb;) or he played with that which did not concern him and for which he did not care. (TA.) You say, Eabiva bihi He played, or sported, [or amused himself, ] with him, or it; (TA;) and bh ↓ tEb~v [which signifies the same]. (Ham p. 710.) ― -b2- And Eabiva bihi Ald~ahoru (assumed tropical:) [ Fortune made sport with him ]; a phrase alluding to the mutability of fortune. (Msb.) ― -b3- And Eabiva fiY manaAmihi , occurring in a trad., means (assumed tropical:) He moved his hands, or arms, in his sleep, like him who is pushing away or taking, or giving or receiving. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [The preparation of curd called ] A^aqiT whereof what is moist is poured out, when it is cooked, upon what is dry thereof, and mixed with it: (Aboo-Sá'id El-Kilábee, S, O:) or A^aqiTN muEaAlajN [i. e. (TA.) Sometimes a man, (S, O,) of the people of the Time of Ignorance, (S,) made a vow that, if he should see what he loved, he would slaughter such and such of his sheep or goats; and when the performance of the vow became obligatory, he would be unwilling to do so, and would slaughter gazelles instead of the sheep or goats: (S, O:) sometimes he would say, “ If my camels amount to a hundred, I will slaughter for them an Eatiyrap ; ” but when they amounted to a hundred, he would be niggardly of the sheep or goat, and would hunt a gazelle, and slaughter it. (TA.) One says, h`*ihi A^ay~aAmu tarojiybK and taEotaArK [ These are days of the sacrificing of the Eatiyrap ]. (S, O.)

definition: Origin, or original state or condition;
sourceDefinition: Origin, or original state or condition; (S, O, K;) and natural disposition; like EikorN . (O.) One says, huwa kariymu AlEitori He is of generous origin. (TK.) And it is said in a prov., EaAdato A_ilaY EitorihaA lamiysu Lemees [a proper name of a woman] returned to her original state or condition (S, O) and natural disposition: (O:) applied to him who has returned to a natural disposition which he had relinquished. (S, O.) [See also EikorN .] -A2- Also A certain plant, (S, O, K,) used medicinally, like the marozanojuw$ [or marjoram ]; (S;) growing like this latter plant, in a straggling manner; and when it has grown tall, and its stem is cut, there comes forth from it what resembles milk: (TA:) accord. to Aboo-Ziyád, it is a plant of those termed A^aHoraAr [pl. of Hur~N ], having a small round fruit ( juraY~ [dim. of jirowN ]), which is sweet, or pleasant in taste, eaten by men; and it grows like as does the poppy, but is smaller: (AHn, O:) or certain small trees [or plants ], (S, K, TA,) having round fruits ( jiraA=' [pl. of jirowN ]), like those of the poppy: (TA as on the authority of AHn:) AHn says, (O,) some assert it to mean the marozanojuw$ ; (O, TA;) but, he adds, this I have not found to be known: (O:) and some say that it is the Earofaj : (TA:) the n. un. is EitorapN : (S, O:) AHn says, a desert-Arab of Rabee'ah told me that this is a small tree [or plant ], that rises to the height of a cubit, having many branches, and green, round leaves, like the tan~uwm , and round fruits ( jiraA=' ), which are in pairs, near together, hanging down towards the ground, and sweet, or pleasant in taste, their taste being like that of small cucumbers: it seldom, or never, grows singly, but is found in pairs, or in fours, in one place: and some assert that it abounds with milk: (O:) it is also said to be a tree [or plant ] that grows by the burrow of the [ lizard called ] Dab~ , which mumbles it so that it does not increase; whence the saying huwa A^a*al~u mino Eitorapi AlD~ab~i [ He is more vile than the Etrp of the Db~ ]: and it is also said, in the K, to signify the marozanojuw$ , mentioned above as being said to be a signification of EitorN : (TA:) also, the caper. (K, * TA.) It is said in a trad. that there is no harm in a man's treating himself medically with senna and Eitor while in a state of A_iHoraAm : (S, O:) which, some say, means that there is no harm in taking these from the sacred territory for such treatment. (O.) -A3- Also An idol, (O, K,) such as had victims ( EataAy^ir ) sacrificed to it. (O.) ― -b2- See also EatiyrapN .

definition: The stem, or stock, of a tree: on the authority of Aboo-Sa'eed and IAar: (TA:) and the branches of a tree.
sourceDefinition: The stem, or stock, of a tree: on the authority of Aboo-Sa'eed and IAar: (TA:) and the branches of a tree. (A, TA.) ― -b2- [And hence,] (assumed tropical:) The people, or tribe, of a man, consisting of his nearer relations, (A'Obeyd, ISk, S, A, O, Msb, K,) both the dead and the living: (S, K:) or his relations: (Msb:) or his relations consisting of his offspring and his paternal uncle's sons: (A:) or his relations consisting of his offspring and of others: (TA:) or the more distinguished of one's relations: (IAth, TA:) or the people of a man's house, the more near and more distant: (O, TA:) and a man's offspring, or progeny; (IAar, Th, Az, S, O, Msb, K;) which is said to be the only meaning of the word known to the Arabs; (Msb;) or imagined by the vulgar to be its meaning peculiarly. (TA.) Eitorapu Aln~abiY~i means [ The nearer portion of the tribe of the Prophet, consisting of ] the sons of 'Abd-El-Mut- talib: (Aboo-Sa'eed, O:) or 'Abd-El-Muttalib and his sons: (TA:) or the offspring of Fátimeh: (IAar, TA:) or the nearer members of the house of the Prophet, consisting of his own offspring and of 'Alee and his offspring: or the nearer and the more distant in relationship of the house of the Prophet: or, as is commonly held, the people of the house of the Prophet; who are those from whom it is forbidden to exact the poor-rate, and those to whom is assigned the fifth of the fifth mentioned in the Soorat el-Anfál [the eighth chapter of the Kur-án, verse 42]. (TA.) -A2- Also n. un. of EitorN [q. v.]. (S, O.)

(TA.) -A2- tEj~s Alr~ajulu The man went forth in a last portion, before daybreak, (↓ biEijosapK , O, or ↓ biEujosapK , K, [but see what follows,]) of the night: (O, K:) El-Marrár Ibn-Sa'eed El-Fak'asee says, describing his travelling-companions, waA_i*aA humu A@rotaHaluwA bilayolK HaAbisK ↓ AlmutaEaj~isi ↓ A^uxoraY Aln~ujuwmi biEajosapi [ And when they departed in an impeding night, in the last period of the appearance of the stars, in a last portion of the night of him who goes forth at that time ].
