definition: , (S, O, Mgh, Msb, TA,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Mgh, Msb, TA,) aor. yagiybu , (Msb,) inf. n. gayobapN [the most common form] (S, O, Mgh, Msb, K) and gayobN (S, O, Msb, K) and gayaAbN , (S, O,) or giyaAbN , (Msb, K,) and guyuwbN (S, O, Msb, K) and guyuwbapN (O, K) and gayobuwbapN , (O, K,) accord. to some of the measure faEoluwlapN , but accord. to others of the measure fayoEaluwlapN i. e. originally gay~abuwbapN , (MF,) and magiybN (S, O, Msb, K) and magaAbN ; (K;) and ↓ tgy~b ; (Msb, K;) He, or it, was, or became, absent; gaAba being the contr. of HaDara ; (S and K in art. HDr ;) or distant, or remote; (Mgh;) or hidden, concealed, or unapparent; (TA;) [or absent from the range, or beyond the reach, of perception by sense, or of mental perception: see gayobN .] You say, gAb Eanohu , inf. n. gayobapN (S, Mgh, TA) &c., as above, (S, TA,) He, or it, was, or became, [ absent from him; or] distant, or remote, from him; (Mgh;) or hidden, or concealed, from him; [&c.;] as also ↓ tgy~b . (TA.) And A^awoHa$atoniY gayobapu fulaAnK [ The absence of such a one has made me to feel lonely ]: and A^aTalota gayobataka [ Thou hast made thine absence to be long ]. (A.) And ↓ A^anaA maEakumo laA A^ugaAyibukumo [ I am with you: I will not be absent from you ]. (A.) And banuw A^aHoyaAnFA ↓ fulaAnK ya$ohaduwna A^aHoyaAnFA wayatagaAyabuwna (ISk, S, TA) i. e. [ The sons of such a one are present sometimes ] and are absent ( yagiybuwna ) sometimes: but one does not say ↓ yatagay~abuwna [unless with Eano following it]: (TA:) [it seems, however, that ytgy~bwn , here, is a mistranscription for yatagay~abuwnanaA or the like; for] one says, Ean~iY fulaAnN ↓ tgy~b [ Such a one was, or became, absent from me; or absented himself from me ]; (S, K, * TA;) and ↓ tagay~abaniY also in a case of necessity in verse, (S, K, TA,) but not in any other case, (K, TA,) accord. to the generality of authorities except the Koofees: (TA:) Imra-el-Keys says, faZal~a lanaA yawomN la*iy*N binaEomapK faqulo fiY maqiylK naHosuhu mutagay~ibiY [thus in my copies of the S and in the TA; but we should read mutagay~ibi , whether it mean mutagay~ibiY or not, as is shown by what follows: the verse may be rendered, So a delightful day, with ease and comfort, betided us: and say thou, of a place of midday-sleep whereof the ill luck was absent from me, . . .]: but Fr says that the word mtgy~b is marfooa, [i. e. that the right reading is mutagay~ibu , meaning simply absent, ] that the verse is mukofaA^ [or made faulty in the termination], and that it is not allowable to make that word refer to maqiylK , like as it is not allowable to say mararotu birajulK A^abuwhu qaAy^imK . (S, TA. [One might be tempted to suppose that we should read faqilo ; but this would not suit the context, which see in Ahlwardt's “ Divans of the six ancient Arabic poets, ” p. 119.]) ― -b2- [ gAb , inf. n. gayobapN , is also said of the mind ( Alqalob ), meaning (assumed tropical:) It was, or became, absent. The inf. n. ( gayobapN ) is often used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Absence of mind; and particularly, from self and others by its being exclusively occupied by the contemplation of divine things: see an ex. voce $awFY ; and another voce sakiynapN .] ― -b3- maA gaAba Eanohu A@bonu A^abiY quHaAfapa (assumed tropical:) [ Ibn-Abee-Koháfeh was not a stranger to it, i. e. was not unacquainted with it, ] occurs in a trad. respecting a satirical saying of Hassán against [the tribe of] Kureysh; meaning that Aboo-Bekr [the son of Aboo-Koháfeh] was skilled in genealogies and traditions, and that it was he who instructed Hassán. (TA.) ― -b4- And one says also, gAb Alr~ajulu , inf. n. gayobN and magiybN ; and ↓ tgy~b ; The man journeyed; and went away, or far away. (TA.) ― -b5- And gAbt Al$~amosu , (S, Mgh, Msb, TA,) inf. n. giyaAbN and gayobuwbapN (Mgh, Msb, TA) and gayobapN (Mgh) and guyuwbN and guyuwbapN and magiybN ; (TA;) and ↓ tgy~bt ; (Msb;) The sun set: (S, Msb, TA:) and the like is also said of the moon, (Msb,) and of other celestial bodies. (TA.) ― -b6- And gAb Al$~aYo'u fiY Al$~aYo'i , inf. n. giyaAbapN and guyuwbapN and giyaAbN and gayaAbN and giybapN , [ The thing became hidden, or concealed, in the thing. ] (K.) -A2- See also 8, in two places.

definition: [ He spoke evil of him;
sourceDefinition: [ He spoke evil of him; or did so in his absence, i. e. backbit him; (the latter being obviously the primary signification;) not always, though generally, meaning with truth: ] he spoke evil of him in his absence; (TA;) or said of him, in his absence, what would grieve him (S, TA) if he heard it; (S;) with truth: (S, TA:) he carped at him behind the back, or in absence, by saying what would grieve him, ( bimaA ↓ tanaAwalahu biZahori Algayobi yasuww^uhu ,) of what was [ reprehensible ] in him: (TA:) or he spoke of him imputing to him what he disliked, of vices, or faults, with truth: (Msb:) when the charge is false, it is termed buhotaAnN : (S, Msb, TA:) or he attributed, or imputed, to him a vice, or fault, or the like; and mentioned him with what was in him of evil; (K, TA;) or said of him what would grieve him: (TA:) and ↓ gaAbahu signifies the same: (K, TA:) [so does ↓ gy~bhu : (see Ksh in civ. 1:) that AgtAbhu does not always signify he spoke evil of him, or the like, in his absence, appears from several instances, such as the phrases AlmugotaAbu fiY Alwajohi (K in art. lmz ) and AlmugotaAbuwna biAlHaDorapi (IAar, TA in that art.): nor does it always signify he spoke evil of him, or the like, with truth; for the verb is used in the Ksh and by Bd and Jel in civ. 1 having for its object the Prophet:] IAar says that ↓ gAb is syn. with AgtAb , and signifies he mentioned a man with the imputation of good or of evil. (TA.) [It may also mean He expressed, or signified, an evil opinion of him by making signs with the side of the mouth, or with the eye, or with the head, or otherwise; as is indicated in the TA in arts. lmz and hmz .]

definition: Whatever is absent, or hidden, from one;
sourceDefinition: Whatever is absent, or hidden, from one; (S, A, Msb, K, TA;) as though it were an inf. n. used in the sense of the act. part. n. [in which the meaning of a subst. is predominant]; (TA;) and so ↓ gaAy^ibN , which [in this sense] is a subst., like kaAhilN , (K, TA,) or an act. part. n. used in the sense of a subst.: (MF:) anything that is absent, or hidden, from the eyes; invisible, unseen, or unapparent; whether it be, or be not, perceived in the heart, or mind: (IAar, TA:) [or anything unperceivable; absent from the range, or beyond the reach, of perception by sense, or of mental perception; or undiscoverable unless by means of divine revelation; a mystery, or secret, such as an event of futurity; ] a thing that has been hidden from men, and with which the Prophet has acquainted them, of the events of the resurrection and of Paradise and of Hell &c.; thus in the Kur ii. 2; (Zj, TA;) and [hence] Zj explains Algayob as meaning, in the Kur lxxxi. 24, that which has been revealed: (TA in art. Dn :) pl. guyuwbN . (Msb.) [See also the Ksh and Bd in ii. 2.] [Hence, EaAlamu Algayobi The world of the unseen; the invisible world. ] And [hence also] one says, rajama biAlgayobi [and qa*afa biAlgayobi (see art. q*f )] He spoke of that which he did not know: (Ham p. 494:) and qaAla rajomFA biAlgayobi He said conjecturally, [or speaking of that which was hidden from him or unknown by him, ] without evidence, and without proof. (Msb in art. rjm , q. v.) ― -b2- And (assumed tropical:) Doubt, or a doubting: (K:) but some disapprove this: some regard it as tropical: and some pronounce it correct: (MF, TA:) pl. giyaAbN and guyuwbN . (K.) A poet says, A^anota nabiY~N taEolamu AlgiyaAbaA laA qaAy^ilFA A_ifokFA walaA murotaAbaA [ Thou art a prophet, knowing doubts, or things doubted; not saying a lie, nor a thing suspected: or, more probably, the meaning is, the things unseen ]. (TA.) ― -b3- Also A place, in the ground, that hides, or conceals, one: (TA:) a low, or depressed, place in the ground, or in a tract of land: (S, K, TA:) or any place such that one knows not what is in it: and a place such that one knows not what is behind it: (Sh, TA:) pl. guyuwbN . (TA.) Hence the phrase Eano Zahori gayobK in a verse of Lebeed cited voce ZahorN , q. v. (TA.) [Hence also] one says, samiEotu SawotFA mino waraA='i Algayobi i. e. [ I heard a sound, or voice, ] from [ behind ] a place that I saw not. (A, TA.) And tanaAwalahu biZahori Algayobi bimaA yasuww^uhu : see 8. And takal~ama bihi Eano Zahori gayobK (A) or Eano Zahori Algayobi (TA, and A and O in art. Zhr ) [app. He spoke of it by memory; in the absence of a book or the like; as one says in modern Arabic, EalaY AlgaAy^ib . See also ZahorN .] ― -b4- Also The xamoSap [i. e. pit, or depression, as is shown by what here follows, (thus in the A, and in the Ksh in ii. 2, in the TA Huforap , which has a similar meaning,)] that is in the place where the kidney is situate, (Ksh, A, TA,) and which swells up when the beast becomes big in the belly: so says ISh: (Ksh ubi suprà:) or the xamoSap that is next to the kidney: (Bd in ii. 2: [De Sacy doubted respecting its meaning, but conjectured that it might be thus: see his Anthol. Gramm. Arabe p. 55:]) pl. guyuwbN : one says, $aribati Ald~aAb~apu Hat~aY waArato guyuwba kulaAhaA , (ISh, Ksh ubi suprà, A, TA,) meaning huzuwmahaA [i. e. The beast drank until it concealed the pits of its kidneys ]. (A, TA.) ― -b5- And Fat: (K, TA:) i. e. the fat of the varob [q. v.] of a sheep or goat: so called because it is hidden from the eye. (TA.) -A2- See also gaAy^ibN .

definition: is originally [ gayabapN ] of the measure faEalapN , with fet-h to the E .
sourceDefinition: is originally [ gayabapN ] of the measure faEalapN , with fet-h to the E . (Msb.) It signifies A low, or depressed, place, or a hollow in the ground, (El-Hawázinee, K, TA,) before which, or in the way to which, ( duwnahaA ,) is an eminence. (El-Hawá- zinee, TA.) ― -b2- And (K) i. q. A^ajamapN : (S, K, TA:) [i. e.] A bed of canes or reeds: (AHn, Msb, TA:) and [ a thicket, wood, or forest; like A^ajamapN ;] a collection of trees, (AHn, ISd, TA,) densely disposed; so called because it conceals what is in it: (ISd, TA:) or a tall A^ajamap , having high, or very high, extremities [app. to its canes or reeds ]: (TA:) pl. gaAbaAtN (Msb, TA) and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ gaAbN . (S, Msb, TA.) ― -b3- And (assumed tropical:) A long spear (K, TA) that has extremities like those of the A^ajamap [expl. above]: (TA:) [but I think that this addition in the TA correctly applies to gaAbapN signifying a number of spears, like a bed of canes or reeds, or like a forest; agreeably with two of the explanations here following:] or a spear that quivers in the wind: (K, TA:) or (tropical:) numerous spears, like abundant and dense trees: (A:) or an assemblage of spears; app. so called as being likened to a gAbp meaning an A^ajamap of dense trees: (ISd, TA:) pl. gaAbaAt and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ gaAbN . (TA.) One says, A^atawonaA fiY gaAbapK i. e. (tropical:) [ They came to us ] amid numerous spears, like abundant and dense trees: (A:) or gAbp may be used in this case in the sense here following. (TA.) ― -b4- And A company, or congregated body, of men: (Aboo-Jábir ElAsadee, K, TA:) pl. gaAbaAtN and [coll. gen. n.] ↓ gaAbN . (TA.)

[of mult.] fuHuwlN (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K) and fiHaAlN (S, Msb, K) and fuHuwlapN (Mgh, O, Msb, K) and fiHaAlapN (S, O, K) and [pl. of pauc.] A^afoHulN : (K:) and ↓ faHiylN signifies the same as faHolN ; (Kr, TA;) and [particularly] a faHol of the camels. (S, O, TA.) ― -b2- Hence AlfaHolu is an appellation of (tropical:) Canopus ( suhayolN ); because it is aloof from the other stars, like the fHl which, when he has covered, goes aloof from the [she-] camels: (S, O, K, TA:) or, as some say, it is so called because of its greatness. (TA.) ― -b3- rajulN ↓ faHiylN means the same as faHolN [i. e. (assumed tropical:) A masculine, as opposed to an effeminate, man ]. (K.) And ↓ AimoraA^apN faHolapN means (assumed tropical:) A clamorous [or, app., masculine ] woman. (S, O, K.) ― -b4- fuHuwlu Al$~uEaraA='i is an appellation applied to (assumed tropical:) The poets (O, K) who have overcome, (O,) or who overcome, (K,) in satirizing, those who have vied with them therein; (O, K;) like Jereer and El-Farezdak, (O, TA,) who used to be called faHolaA muDara : (TA:) and in like manner (tropical:) any one who, when he vies with a poet, is judged to have excelled him [is called a faHol ]; (K, TA; [for faDala in the CK, I read fuD~ila , as in other copies of the K;]) like 'Alkameh Ibn-'Abadeh; (TA;) who was surnamed AlfaHolu because he took to wife Umm-Jundab when Imrael-Keys divorced her on the occasion of her judging him [i. e. 'Alkameh] to have overcome him [Imra-el-Keys] in poetry. (S, O, K, TA.) ― -b5- faHolN also means [app. (assumed tropical:) A vigorous orator: see haAdirN . ― -b6- And] (tropical:) A relater, reciter, or rehearser, by heart, [of poetry, and of traditions, or narratives learned, or heard, or received, from another or others;] syn. raAwK : pl. fuHuwlN : (K, TA:) so in the M. (TA.) ― -b7- See also fuH~aAlN , in three places. And see mutafaH~ilN . ― -b8- And (tropical:) A mat that is made of the woven leaves of the palm-tree thus called, (Sh, * S, * O, * K, * TA,) i. e., of the palm-tree called fuH~aAl : (S, O, K, TA:) pl. fuHuwlN . (S, O, TA.) ― -b9- And (assumed tropical:) Rain is thus called [in a verse of Et-Tirimmáh Ibn-El-Hakeem, being likened to the stallion-camel, because of its fertilizing the earth]. (Ham p. 110.)

definition: and ↓ faHolN The male palm-tree, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) by means of which the fruitbearing palm-trees are fecundated, (S, * Mgh, * Msb, TA,) and which, when they are on the windward side of the...
sourceDefinition: and ↓ faHolN The male palm-tree, (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K, TA,) by means of which the fruitbearing palm-trees are fecundated, (S, * Mgh, * Msb, TA,) and which, when they are on the windward side of the latter trees, fecundate these: (TA:) [see what follows:] only the former word is mentioned [in this sense] by Lth; and ISd says, (TA,) the former word is used peculiarly as applied to the male palm-tree: (K, * TA:) AHn cites AA as saying that ↓ faHolN is not said except of that which has life, and Aboo-Nasr says the like; but AHn adds that people in general disagree from them as to this: (TA:) the pl. of fuH~aAlN is faHaAHiylu ; (S, Mgh, Msb, K;) and the pl. of ↓ faHolN is fuHuwlN (S, Mgh, O, Msb) and fuHuwlapN (Mgh, Msb) and fiHaAlN ; (Msb;) of the first of which pls. of faHolN , the following saying, (S, O, Msb, TA,) of Oheihah Ibn-El-Juláh, (O, TA,) presents an ex.: taA^ab~ariY yaA xayorapa Alfasiyli taA^ab~ariY mino Hana*K fa$uwliY A_i*o Dan~a A^aholu Aln~axoli biAlfuHuwli [ Receive thou fecundation, O best of young palmtrees: receive thou fecundation from Hanadh, and show that thou hast received it: ( fa$uwliY being from $aAlato bi*anabihaA said of a she-camel, meaning “ she raised her tail, showing thereby that she was pregnant: ”) since the palm-owners have been niggardly of the spadixes of the male palm-trees ]: (S, O, Msb, TA:) the meaning is, that the people of Hanadh were niggardly of the spadixes of their [male] palm-trees, and the east wind blew at the time of the fecundation upon the male trees, bearing off [the pollen of] their spadixes and casting it upon the female trees, so that it served for fecundation: Hanadh is a place about four miles from El-Medeeneh: and it is said to be the town of Oheihah: or to be a water belonging to Suleym and Muzeyneh. (Msb.)

(from a poet) in which firaAx is treated grammatically as a sing. in the first paragraph of art. xlf .] ― -b2- [Hence,] (assumed tropical:) A base, a vile, or an abject, man, who is driven away. (K.) And one says, fulAanN faroxN mina AlfiraAxi , (TA,) or mn Alfuruwxi , (so in two copies of the A,) meaning (tropical:) Such a one is a bastard: (A, TA:) said by El-Khafájee to be a phrase of the people of El-Medeeneh, peculiarly; but accord. to MF, it is a post-classical phrase common in El-Hijáz. (TA.) ― -b3- And (tropical:) A sucker, an offset, or a sprout, of any plant (L, K) or tree &c.: (L:) or a branch of a tree: or, as some say, a branch that is in the middle of a tree: (Ham p. 347:) or [its pl.] firaAxN signifies offsets, or shoots, from the roots or stems of trees: (A:) and this is also said to signify worms that are in herbs. (Ham p. 491.) And (tropical:) Seed-produce, or corn, shooting forth into leaf from the grain, when the latter has cloven asunder: (Lth, TA:) or, ready to cleave open, (S, K,) when it has come up: (S:) or, when it has shoots. (L.) ― -b4- And Alfaroxu signifies (tropical:) The fore part of the brain; (K, TA;) thus called by way of comparison [to the young one of a bird], in like manner as it is called AlEuSofuwru ; (TA;) or the ESfwr is beneath the farox : (TA in art. (S, TA.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, O, Msb, K,) and fazaEa , (K,) aor. , of the former verb, (Msb, K,) and of the latter also, (K,) inf. n. fazaEN , (S, O, Msb, K,) which is of the former verb, (S, * O, Msb, TA,) and [of the latter verb] fazoEN [ fazaEFA in the CK being a mistake for fazoEFA ] and fizoEn (K, TA,) He feared; or was, or became, in fear, afraid, frightened, or terrified; (S, O, Msb, K, TA;) and so ↓ tfz~E : (TA in art. rwE :) you say, faziEa minohu he feared him, or it; or was, or became, in fear, &c., of him, or it: (MA, Msb, TA:) accord. to Er-Rághib, fazaEN signifies a shrinking, and an aversion, that comes upon a man, from a thing causing fear or fright; and is a kind of jazaE [q. v.]; and one should not say faziEotu mina A@ll~`hi like as one says xifotu minohu : or, as Mbr says, in the “ Kámil, ” its primary signification is the fearing, or being in fear or afraid or frightened or terrified: then, by a metonymical application, it signifies a people's going forth quickly to repel an enemy, or the like, that has come upon them suddenly; and this meaning has become [conventionally regarded as] proper. (TA.) ― -b2- fazaEN signifies also The seeking, or demanding, aid, or succour: (Az, K, TA:) and the aiding, or succouring; (Az, S, O, K, TA;) this latter being likewise a signification of ↓ A_ifozaAEN : (S, O:) an ex. of the former word (S, O, TA) in the latter sense (O, TA) occurs in the saying of the Prophet to the Ansár, A_in~akumo latakovuruwna Einoda AlfazaEi wa taqil~uwna Einoda AlT~amaEi [ Verily ye are many on the occasion of aiding, or succouring, and ye are few on the occasion of coveting, or greed ]; (S, O, K) and a dual (S, O) and a masc. and a fem.; (S, O, K;) one says, fulaAnN mafozaEN liln~aAsi Such a one is a refuge to men when an event comes upon them suddenly, and humaAmafozaEN liln~aAsi , and humo mafozaEN , &c.; (S, O;) and ↓ mafozaEapN is the same in signification and in its applications; (K;) expl. by IF as signifying a place to which one who is in fear, or frightened, betakes himself, or has recourse, for refuge, protection, or preservation: (TA:) or mafozaEN signifies one of whom aid, or succour, is sought, or demanded: (K:) and ↓ mafozaEapN , [ a cause of fear or fright; being a word of the class of maboxalapN and majobanapN ; i. e.] a thing that one is made to fear, or at which one is frightened; (S;) or a person whom one is made to fear, or at whom one is frightened; [like fuzoEapN ;] or on account of whom, or for the sake of whom, one is made to fear, or is frightened: (Lth, O, K:) you say, fulaAnN lanaA mafozaEapN [ Such a one is to us a person whom we are made to fear, &c.], and in like manner you say of a female, and of a pl. number. (O.)

sourceDefinition: Cowardly; (Fr, O, K;) as being made to fear, or to be frightened at, everything: (Fr, O:) and courageous; (Fr, O, K;) as being one the like of whom fearful events are made to befall ( bimivolihi tunozalu AlA^afozaAEu ). (Fr, O. [But what here follows suggests another reason, and I think a better, for the latter meaning.]) mufaz~aEapN applied by 'Amr Ibn-Maadee-Kerib as an epithet to his Aisot , in replying to a threat of El-Ash-'ath, who had said to him, lawo danawota laA^uDar~iTan~aka , means Secure from being overcome by fear, or fright, and [ therefore ] not lax so as to break wind [ in consequence of fear ]; being from faz~aEa Eanohu meaning “ he removed fear, or fright, from him; ” or it may be for the same reason as that for which mufaz~aEN is applied to a courageous man. (O.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. , (Msb, K,) inf. n. faqo'N , (S, Mgh, O,) He put out the eye; or blinded it; or made it to sink in its socket; syn. baxaqahaA ; (Lh, S, O, K;) as also ↓ fq~A^hA , (S, O, K,) inf. n. tafoqiy^apN : (S, O:) or, accord. to the Msb, baxaSahaA ; which is said by Es-Sarakustee to mean he put his finger into the eye and pulled it out; and by IKtt to mean he extinguished its light; and by some to mean he slit it, or rent it: (TA:) or he slit, or rent, the portion of the eye that is surrounded by the white thereof: (Mgh:) or i. q. qalahaA ; (K, TA;) i. e. [ he pulled out the eye; or], as some say, he pulled out the portion of the eye which is surrounded by the white, and with which one sees: (TA: [and the like is said in the Mgh in explanation of AlqaloEu , but this is there said to differ from Alfaqo'u :]) or, as some say, he put his finger into the eye and so slit, or rent, it: (TA:) or he broke, or ruptured, the eye; syn. kasarahaA ; and so Albavorapa [ the pimple, or the small, or purulent, pustule ]; and the like of these: (K: [and to all of these the two other explanations mentioned above as from the K are likewise there, improperly, made to relate:]) this last explanation, in the K, is said by MF to be unknown; but it is mentioned in the A and L, and by more than one of the leading lexicologists: (TA:) [accord. to Mtr,] faqaA^otu Albavorapa means I slit the pimple, &c., or rent it [ open ]. (Mgh, Msb.) Among the Arabs in the Time of Ignorance, when a man's camels amounted to a thousand, he put out ( faqaA^a ) an eye of one of them (a baEiyr ), and set it free to pasture where it would, and made no use of it. (TA.) ― -b2- faqaA^a A@ll~`hu Eanoka Eayona AlkamaAli is a tropical saying [app. meaning May God prevent from seeing thee the fatal eye: the term Eyn AlkmAl being applied to an eye believed to have the power of killing by its glance]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- And faqaA^a naAZirayohi , (O, K,) likewise said to be a tropical phrase, (TA,) means (tropical:) He dispelled his anger. (O, K.) ― -b4- And faqaA^Eayonahu also means [sometimes] (tropical:) He struck him; or struck him vehemently with a broad thing, or with anything; or slapped him with his hand: or he was rough, rude, or ungentle, to him in speech. (TA in art. Eyn .) ― -b5- And faqaA^ati AlbuhomaY , inf. n. fuquwo'N , (O, K, TA,) or, accord. to the L, faqo'N , (TA,) The [ barleygrass termed ] bhmY was rendered dusty by rain, or by a torrent, so that the cattle would not eat it until it became clean: (O, K, TA:) and in like manner one says of any plant. (O, TA.) [See also 1 in art. fqA^ .] ― -b6- And, as some say, (TA,) or ↓ tfq~A^t , (S, O, TA,) (tropical:) The envelopes [or glumes ] of the buhomaY burst open so as to disclose (S, O, TA) its fruit [or seeds ], (S, O,) or its flower. (TA.)

definition: A he-camel affected with a disease termed Haqowap [q.
sourceDefinition: A he-camel affected with a disease termed Haqowap [q. v.], in consequence of which he voids not his urine nor his dung; (O, K; *) and sometimes, or often, his veins and his flesh become choked with blood, and swollen; and if slaughtered and cooked, the cooking-pot becomes full of blood; and sometimes, or often, his stomach becomes so much inflated, or swollen, that it rends, or bursts: and it is likewise applied to a she-camel: (O:) and ↓ faqoA^aY signifies the same applied to a she-camel. (K.) ― -b2- Also (i. e. faqiYo'N ) The disease above- mentioned, itself. (O, K.) -A2- See also faqo'N , latter sentence.

definition: The mouth: (MA, KL, &c.
sourceDefinition: The mouth: (MA, KL, &c.:) it is originally fawahN , (S, K, and Msb in art. fwh ,) with two fet-hahs, (Msb in that art.,) or fawohN ; (so in some copies of the S;) the h being cut off from it, the w is not susceptible of declension, because it is quiescent, therefore m is substituted for it; but when you form the dim. or the pl., you restore it to its original state, saying [in the former case] fuwayohN and [in the latter case] A^afowaAhN , and not A^afomaA='N [in some of the copies of the S not A^afomaAmN ]: but when you form the rel. n., you say ↓ famiY~N ; and, if you will, ↓ famawiY~N , combining the substitute and the letter for which it is substituted, like as they say in the dual famawaAni ; this being held to be allowable because of there being therein another letter rejected, i. e. the h , as though they made the m in this case to be a substitute for the h , not for the w : (S, TA:) and one says also famayaAni , which, like famawaAni , is anomalous; (IAar, K in art. fwh ;) but one says famaAni also, as well as famawaAni : (Msb in art. fwh :) it has three forms, famN and fumN and fimN : (S, K, TA:) and some decline it doubly; saying in the nom. case fumN , accus. famFA , and gen. fimK ; (S, TA;) like Aimoruw^N and AibonumN , which have been said to be the only other instances of the kind: (TA:) when it is prefixed to the [pronominal] Y , one says fiY~a and famiY : but when to [a pronoun] other than the Y , it is declined with the letters w and A and Y , so that one says fuwuhu and faAhu and fiyhi ; but one also says famuhu : (Msb. in art. fwh :) and sometimes the m is musheddedeh, (S, K,) in poetry, as in the saying, (S, TA,) of Mohammad Ibn-Dhu-eyb El-'Ománee El-Fukeymee, the rájiz, (TA in this art. and in art. Tsm ,) addressing Er-Rasheed, or, accord. to IKh, said in relation to Suleymán Ibn-'Abd-El-Melik and 'Abd-El- 'Azeez. (TA in art. Tsm ,) yaA layotahaA qado xarajato mino fum~ihi Hat~aY yaEuwda Almuloku fiY A^usoTum~ihi (S, TA) or A^uTosum~ihi i. e. [ O, would that it had gone forth from his mouth, so that the dominion might return ] to its rightful owner; (S in art. sTm , and TA in art. Tsm ;) and it would have been allowable, (S, TA,) accord. to ISk, (S,) or accord. to Fr, (TA,) if he had said ↓ mn fam~ihi , with fet-h to the f : (S, TA:) the pl. of fm , with teshdeed, is A^afomaAmN ; and its dim. is ↓ fumayomN , mentioned by Lh. (TA.) MF says that many of the expositors of the Tes-heel have collected the dial. vars. of this word, compounded and uncompounded, and they have exceeded twenty; that with fet-h, they say, being the most common and the most chaste. (TA.) [See more in art. fwh .] ― -b2- [Hence,] Alfm is metonymically applied to (tropical:) The teeth. (Ham p. 242.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] famu AlHuwti (assumed tropical:) The star [a] in the mouth of Piscis Australis. (Kzw &c.: see art. Hwt .) And famu Alfarasi (assumed tropical:) The star [e] upon the lip of Pegasus. (Kzw.) ― -b4- [And famuAlr~aHimi (assumed tropical:) The mouth of the womb. ] ― -b5- And famu Aln~ahori (assumed tropical:) The mouth of the river. (MA.) ― -b6- And [hence likewise,] famN is also used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Branch; opposed to AisotN meaning “ root. ” (TA in art. sth ; in which see AisotN , last quarter.) -A2- famN mina Ald~ibaAgi means The quantity that is used at one time, of tan; (Fr, K, * TA;) like nafosN minohu . (Fr, TA.)

rawSourceText: The mouth: (MA, KL, &c.:) it is originally fawahN , (S, K, and Msb in art. fwh ,) with two fet-hahs, (Msb in that art.,) or fawohN ; (so in some copies of the S;) the h being cut off from it, the w is not susceptible of declension, because it is quiescent, therefore m is substituted for it; but when you form the dim. or the pl., you restore it to its original state, saying [in the former case] fuwayohN and [in the latter case] A^afowaAhN , and not A^afomaA='N [in some of the copies of the S not A^afomaAmN ]: but when you form the rel. n., you say ↓ famiY~N ; and, if you will, ↓ famawiY~N , combining the substitute and the letter for which it is substituted, like as they say in the dual famawaAni ; this being held to be allowable because of there being therein another letter rejected, i. e. the h , as though they made the m in this case to be a substitute for the h , not for the w : (S, TA:) and one says also famayaAni , which, like famawaAni , is anomalous; (IAar, K in art. fwh ;) but one says famaAni also, as well as famawaAni : (Msb in art. fwh :) it has three forms, famN and fumN and fimN : (S, K, TA:) and some decline it doubly; saying in the nom. case fumN , accus. famFA , and gen. fimK ; (S, TA;) like Aimoruw^N and AibonumN , which have been said to be the only other instances of the kind: (TA:) when it is prefixed to the [pronominal] Y , one says fiY~a and famiY : but when to [a pronoun] other than the Y , it is declined with the letters w and A and Y , so that one says fuwuhu and faAhu and fiyhi ; but one also says famuhu : (Msb. in art. fwh :) and sometimes the m is musheddedeh, (S, K,) in poetry, as in the saying, (S, TA,) of Mohammad Ibn-Dhu-eyb El-'Ománee El-Fukeymee, the rájiz, (TA in this art. and in art. Tsm ,) addressing Er-Rasheed, or, accord. to IKh, said in relation to Suleymán Ibn-'Abd-El-Melik and 'Abd-El- 'Azeez. (TA in art. Tsm ,) yaA layotahaA qado xarajato mino fum~ihi Hat~aY yaEuwda Almuloku fiY A^usoTum~ihi (S, TA) or A^uTosum~ihi i. e. [ O, would that it had gone forth from his mouth, so that the dominion might return ] to its rightful owner; (S in art. sTm , and TA in art. Tsm ;) and it would have been allowable, (S, TA,) accord. to ISk, (S,) or accord. to Fr, (TA,) if he had said ↓ mn fam~ihi , with fet-h to the f : (S, TA:) the pl. of fm , with teshdeed, is A^afomaAmN ; and its dim. is ↓ fumayomN , mentioned by Lh. (TA.) MF says that many of the expositors of the Tes-heel have collected the dial. vars. of this word, compounded and uncompounded, and they have exceeded twenty; that with fet-h, they say, being the most common and the most chaste. (TA.) [See more in art. fwh .] ― -b2- [Hence,] Alfm is metonymically applied to (tropical:) The teeth. (Ham p. 242.) ― -b3- [Hence also,] famu AlHuwti (assumed tropical:) The star [a] in the mouth of Piscis Australis. (Kzw &c.: see art. Hwt .) And famu Alfarasi (assumed tropical:) The star [e] upon the lip of Pegasus. (Kzw.) ― -b4- [And famuAlr~aHimi (assumed tropical:) The mouth of the womb. ] ― -b5- And famu Aln~ahori (assumed tropical:) The mouth of the river. (MA.) ― -b6- And [hence likewise,] famN is also used as meaning (assumed tropical:) Branch; opposed to AisotN meaning “ root. ” (TA in art. sth ; in which see AisotN , last quarter.) -A2- famN mina Ald~ibaAgi means The quantity that is used at one time, of tan; (Fr, K, * TA;) like nafosN minohu . definition: and ↓ faAhN and ↓ fiyhN (K, TA) and, accord.
sourceDefinition: and ↓ faAhN and ↓ fiyhN (K, TA) and, accord. to the copies of the K, fuwhapN , [or, as in the CK, fawohap ,] but correctly ↓ fuw~ahapN , (TA,) and famN , all signify the same [i. e. The mouth ]: (K, TA:) the pl. is A^afowaAhN , (S, K, TA,) pl. of fuwhN , (S, TA,) and as such its case is plain; as pl. of fiyhN , it is like A^arowaAHN as pl. of riyHN ; as pl of faAhN , it is allowable as having w for its original medial radical; but as pl. of fuw~ahapN , it is anomalous: (TA:) and another pl. is A^afomaAmN , (K, TA,) said by some to be pl. of fum~N or fam~N , with teshdeed, of which an ex. occurs in a verse cited in the first paragraph of art. fm ; but some disallow this pl.; and accord. to some, (TA,) it has no sing. (K, TA) agreeable with rule, (TA,) for famN is originally fawahN , (K, TA,) with the w movent by fet-h, or [ fawohN , as in some copies of the S,] with the w quiescent, on the authority of IJ; (TA;) the h is elided, and the w becomes a movent final, therefore it must be changed into A , because of the fet-hah preceding it, so the word becomes fA ; but a noun may not be of two letters whereof one is [the n of] the tenween, (K, TA,) thus the passage is expressed in the M, but MF remarks that correctly we should say whereof one is the A , (TA,) and therefore a hard letter is substituted for it, one similar to it in kind, which is m , for they are both labials, and in the m is a sort of humming sound ( hawiY~N , in the CK huwiY~N ,) in the mouth, [or rather in the nose,] resembling [the sound of] the prolongation of the w : (K, TA:) [several similar disquisitions, added in the TA, respecting the change from fwh to fm , I omit, regarding them as needless: what is said on this subject in the S, in art. fm , I have mentioned in that art.:] in the present art., J says that the m of fm is a substitute for the h , not for the w , of fwh ; but this is a mistake: (IB, TA:) the dual of famN is famaAni and famawaAni (IAar, S, Msb, K) and famayaAni , the second and third of which are anomalous: (IAar, K:) of the second, which occurs in a verse of ElFarezdak, [and respecting which see the first paragraph of art. fm ,] Sb says that it is used by poetic license. (TA.) In using it as a prefixed noun, in the phrase h`*aA fuwhuhu , they deemed the combination of the two h s difficult in respect of utterance; therefore they suppressed the [radical] h thereof [in this case, and then in other, similar, cases], and said, h`*aA fuwhu , and fuw zayodK , and raA^ayotu faA zayodK , and mararotu bifiY zayodK : and when prefixing it to [the pronoun denoting] thyself, thou sayest, h`*aA fiY~a ; and this thou dost alike in using it in the nom. case and in the accus. and in the gen., because the w [of fuw ] is changed into Y and is then incorporated [into the pronominal Y ]: (S, and the like is said in the Msb:) and sometimes, though rarely, they did the like in other cases, when not prefixing it; for instance, faA occurs at the end of a verse of El-'Ajjáj, without an affix, in this case for faAhaA . (S.) ― -b2- In the saying kal~amotuhu faAhu A_ilaY fiY~a , meaning I spoke to him, his mouth being near to my mouth, fAh is in the accus. case as a denotative of state: (S, TA: *) or by reason of the derivative [ mukal~imFA ] meant to be understood: or, as Sb says, it is an instance of one of the nouns that are put in the place of inf. ns., and it is not to be separated from what should follow it, so that you may not say kal~amotuhu faAha [alone], for you tell of your nearness to the person, and that there is not any one between you and him: and if you will, you may use the nom. case, meaning wah`*ihi HaAluhu [ this being his state ], (Sb, TA,) i. e. fuwhu A_ilaY fiY~a [ his mouth was near to my mouth ], the clause [following kl~mth ] occupying the place of a denotative of state. (TA.) -A2- See also fuw~ahapN .

sourceDefinition: : see its syn. fuwhN . ― -b2- [Hence] it signifies also (tropical:) The fam [i. e. mouth ] of a place; likened to the fam [properly so called] as being the first place of ingress, or entrance, to the interior: (TA:) [and so too as being the place of egress, or exit, from the interior: ] it is of a river, or rivulet, (Lth, S, Msb, TA,) and of a valley, or water-course, or torrent-bed, (K, TA,) and of a street, and of a road; (S, Msb, K, TA;) signifying the fam [or mouth ]; as also ↓ fuwhapN , (K, TA,) without teshdeed; mentioned by IAar: (TA:) or it signifies thus in relation to a river, or rivulet; (Lth, Msb, TA;) the foremost part thereof: or, as some say, the place of its pouring into the kiZaAmap [q. v.]: and accord. to Lth, in relation to a valley, or water-course, or torrent-bed, its raA^os [or head, as though in this case having one, or each, of two contr. meanings, unless, as I believe it to be, the mouth, or outlet, of a valley or water-course or torrent-bed be sometimes called its rA^s as being its foremost part ]: (TA:) and of a street, it is the place of egress, or exit; (Msb;) the foremost part thereof: (TA:) and of a road, it is the fam [or mouth ], which is the upper part thereof ( AElAh ): (Msb: [thus in my copy; but I think that AElAh is a mistranscription, in my copy, for A^aw~aluhu , and that the correct meaning is therefore the foremost part thereof, agreeably with what is said above in relation to a road and to a river or rivulet:]) but accord. to some, ↓ fuwhapN , without teshdeed, is not allowable; definition: and ↓ fay~ihN , (S, K,) the latter originally fayowihN , (S,) Eloquent;

(TA.) And one says minoTiyqN mufaw~ahN (K, TA) meaning [ Very ] eloquent in speech: (TA:) and manoTiqN mufaw~ahN (K, TA) Good, or excel-lent, speech, or diction. sourceDefinition: , aor. and , [or the former only accord. to the Mgh., as will be seen by what follows,] inf. n. qadorN , (S, Msb,) is from Alt~aqodiyru , (S,) [or] it signifies the same as ↓ qd~rtu Al$~aYo'a , inf. n. taqodiyrN : (Msb:) [which latter phrase is afterwards mentioned in the S, but unexplained: the meaning is, I measured the thing; computed, or determined, its quantity, measure, size, bulk, proportion, extent, amount, sum, limit or limits, or number: ] Al$~aYo'a ↓ qd~r signifies he computed, or determined, or computed by conjecture, the quantity, measure, size, bulk, proportion, extent, amount, sum, or number, of the thing, ( Hazarahu ,) in order that he might know how much it was. (IKtt.) It is said in a trad., A_i*aA gum~a Ealayokumu AlhilaAlu faA@qodiruwA lahu , and faA@qoduruwA ; (S, Msb; *) or A_ino gom~a Ealayokumo faA@qodiruwA , with kesr to the d ; (Mgh, Msb; *) for faA@qoduruwA , with damm, is wrong; (Mgh;) and Ks. say, that you say qadarotu Al$~aYo'a , aor. A^aqodiruhu , with kesr, and that he had not heard any other aor.: (TA:) the meaning of the trad. is, [ When the new moon (of Ramadán) is hidden from you by a cloud or mist, or if it be so hidden, ] compute ye (↓ qad~iruwA ) the number of the days to it, (Mgh, Msb,) and so complete Shaabán, making it thirty days: (S, * Mgh, * Msb:) or, as some say, compute ye ( qad~iruwA ) the mansions of the moon, and its course in them [ to it, i. e., to the new moon]. (Msb.) See also 5. ― -b2- [Hence, app., the saying,] A^uqoduro bi*aroEika bayonanaA See thou and know thy rank, or estimation, among us. (AO.) ― -b3- Hence also,] maA qadaruwA A@ll~`ha Haq~a qadorihi [Kur., vi. 91, and other places, meaning, And they have not estimated God with the estimation that is due to Him: or] and they have not magnified, or honoured, God, with the magnifying, or honouring, that is due to Him: (S, K:) for qadorN signifies [also] a magnifying, or honouring: (K:) or have not assigned to God the attributes that are due to Him: (Lth:) or have not known what God is in reality. (El-Basáïr.) ― -b4- qadara Al$~aYo'a biAl$~aYo'i , aor. [ and] , (L,) inf. n. qadorN ; (L, K;) and bh ↓ qd~rhu ; (L;) He measured the thing by the thing: (L, K: *) and EalaY mivaAlihi ↓ qd~rhu he measured it by its measure: (S, K, art. qys :) and bayona AlA^amorayoni ↓ qd~r he measured, or compared, the two things, or cases, together; syn. qaAyasa ; (K, art. qys ;) and so bayonahumaA ↓ qaAdara . (L, art. qys .) ― -b5- [Hence, app.,] qadara AlA^amora , (L, K,) and A_ilaY AlA^amori , (L,) aor. (L, K,) and , (L,) inf. n. qadorN ; (L, K;) [and ↓ qd~rhu ;] He thought upon the thing, or affair, (L,) and considered its end, issue, or result, (L, K,) and measured, or compared, one part of it with another; (L;) he measured it, compared one part of it with another, considered it, and thought upon it. (L.) See also 2. ― -b6- qadarotu Ealayohi Alv~awoba , (S, K, *) inf. n. qadorN , (S,) I made the garment according to his measure; adapted it to his measure: (S, K: *) [and qadarotu Ealayohi Al$~aYo'a app. signifies I made the thing according to his, or its, measure; proportioned, or adapted, the thing to him, or it; for wSfth , by which it is explained in the TA, seems to be, as IbrD thinks, a mistake for waDaEotuhu :] and Al$~aYo'a ↓ qd~r signifies, in like manner, he made the thing by measure, or according to a measure; or proportioned it; syn. jaEalahu biqadarK : (IKtt:) the primary meaning of ↓ taqodiyrN is the making a thing according to the measure of another thing. (Bd- xv. 60.) ― -b7- [Hence,] qadara A@ll~`hu *`lika Ealayohi , aor. and , inf. n. qadorN and qadarN , (K,) or the latter is a simple subst., (Lh, Msb,) and maqodarapN ; (S [unless this be a simple subst.];) and Elyh ↓ qd~rhu , (K,) [which is more common,] inf. n. taqodiyrN ; (TA;) and lahu ; (K;) [ God decreed, appointed, ordained, or decided, that against him; and for him, or to him; accord. to an explanation of qadarN in the K: or decreed, &c., that against him; and for him, or to him; adapting it to his particular case; accord. to an explanation of qadarN by Lth, and of qadorN and qadarN in the S, and of qadarN in the Msb: see qadorN , below.] You say also qadara A@ll~`hu lahu bixayorK [ God decreed, &c., for him, good ]. (K.) ― -b8- Also, qadara , (K,) aor. and , inf. n. qadorN , (TA,) He [ God ] distributed, divided, or apportioned, [ as though by measure, ] sustenance, or the means of subsistence. (K, TA. sourceDefinition: A cooking-pot; a vessel in which one cooks: (Msb:) [and it very often means the food contained therein; i. e. pottage of any kind: (see, for an ex., 3 in art. glw :)] of the fem. gender (Msb, K, TA) without p : (TA:) or it is made fem. definition: The bottom, lowest depth, or extremity of the lower part, [ of the interior, ] of a thing;
sourceDefinition: The bottom, lowest depth, or extremity of the lower part, [ of the interior, ] of a thing; (Msb;) i. q. EumoqN , of a well &c.; (S;) the remotest part of anything; (A, K;) [as, for instance,] of a river, (TA,) and of a vessel; (S, A;) pl. quEuwrN . (Msb, K.) You say jalasa fiY qaEori bayotihi , [lit., He sat in the innermost part of his house, ] meaning (assumed tropical:) he kept in his house. (Msb.) And laA A^adoxulu Ealayohi qaEora Albayoti , and ↓ qaEiyratahu , and ↓ qaEoratahu , all signify the same [ I will not go in to him in the innermost part of the house; or (assumed tropical:) I will not be an intimate in his house ]. (TA.) ― -b2- [ Depth, properly and tropically. You say] *ahaba fY qaEori AlA^aroDi [ It (a tree or the like) went into the depth of the earth ]. (TA.) And fulaAnN baEiydu AlqaEori (A, TA) (tropical:) Such a one is deep and excellent in judgment; one who examines deeply. (TA.) And layosa likalaAmihi qaEorN (tropical:) [ His speech, or language, has not depth ]. (A, TA.) ― -b3- The root, or lower or lowest part, of a palm-tree [or the like]. (TA.) ― -b4- A hollow in the ground, such as is called a jawobap , (K, TA,) the descent into which and the ascent from which are difficult; (TA;) as also ↓ qaEorapN . ― -b5- A city, or town; syn. baladN ; (K;) such as El-Basrah or ElKoofeh. (AZ.) You say maA fiY h`*aA AlqaEori mivoluhu There is not in this city, or town, the like of him. (K.) And maA xaraja mino A^aholi h`*aA AlqaEori A^aHadN mivoluhu , like as you say mino A^aholi h`*aA AlgaAy^iTi , There came not forth, of the people of this city, or town, any one like him. (AZ.) ― -b6- A [ bowl, such as is called ] jafonap . (Fr, IAar, K.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor.
sourceDefinition: , (S, Mgh, O, Msb, K,) aor. yaquwtu , (S, O, Msb,) inf. n. qawotN (S, O, Msb, K) and quwtN (Sb, K) and qiyaAtapN , (S, O, K,) the last originally qiwaAtapN , (O,) He fed, nourished, or sustained, (S, Msb, TA,) or fed with what would sustain the body, (S, O, K, * TA,) [or with food sufficient to sustain life, ] or with a small supply of the means of subsistence, (TA,) him, (Msb, TA,) or them, (K, TA,) or his family; (S, O;) he gave him [or them] what is termed quwt [q. v.]: (Msb:) and ↓ AqAthu signifies [in like manner] he gave him his quwt . (TA.) It is said in a trad., kafaY biAlmaro'i A_ivomFA A^ano yuDay~iEa mano yaquwtu i. e. [ It suffices the man as a sin, or crime, that he destroy ] him whom he is bound to sustain, of his family and household and slaves: or, as some relate it, ↓ mano yuqiytuhu ; using a dial. var. [of yqwt ]. (TA.) [And lahu ↓ AqtAt app. signifies, primarily, He supplied to him food. (See this verb below, near the end of the paragraph.)] -A2- And qaAta and ↓ qw~t and ↓ AqAt and ↓ A^aqowata [sometimes] signify He straitened his household, by reason of niggardliness or poverty. (El-Jámi' es-Sagheer, and scholia thereon.) -A4- See also 8, in the middle of the paragraph.

sourceDefinition: signifies He was, or became, fed, nourished, or sustained; being quasi-pass. of qaAta signifying as expl. in the beginning of this art. (S, A, Mgh, O, K, TA.) ― -b2- And it is trans. by means of bi , and by itself: see 5, in four places. One says, humo yaqotaAtuwna AlHab~a [ They feed upon, or eat, grain ]. sourceDefinition: [ A species of tree, of the class Pentandria, order Monogynia, of the Linnæan system; belonging to the natural order of Celastraceæ; mentioned in botanical works under the name of Catha edulis; and fully described by Forskål in his Flora Ægypt. Arab., pp. 63, 64; in the latter page of which he says: “ In Yemen colitur iisdem hortis cum Coffea. Stipitibus plantatur. Arabes folia viridia avide edunt, multum eorum vires venditantes, qui copiosius comederit, vel totam vigilet noctem: asseverant quoque pestem ea loca non intrare ubi hæc colitur arbor: ” &c. ― -b2- And in the same work, p. cxviii., Forskål mentions qAt AlrEyAn (by which is meant qaAtu Alr~uEoyaAni ) as the name of A species of lettuce, lactuca inermis. ― -b3- Respecting the former plant, see also De Sacy's Chrest. Arabe, sec. ed., i. 462, 463.]

sourceDefinition: [ Giving, or a giver of, food, nourishment, or sustenance. (See 1, first sentence.) ― -b2- And hence,] Keeping, preserving, guarding, or protecting; or a keeper, &c.; syn. HaAfiZN [as signifying thus; and app. as signifying also watching; or a watcher ]: (S, A, O, Msb, K:) and witnessing; or a witness; syn. $aAhidN ; (S, O, Msb, K;) or $ahiydN : (A:) and AO says that it signifies, with the Arabs, one acquainted ( mawoquwfN ) with a thing ( EalaY $aYo'K ). (TA.) Th cites the following verses (of Es-Semow'al Ibn-Ádiyà, O): layota $iEoriY waA^a$oEuran~a A_i*aA maA qar~abuwhaA mano$uwrapF waduEiytu A^aliYa AlfaDolu A^amo EalaY~a A_i*aA Huw sibotu A_in~iY EalaY AlHisaAbi muqiytu [meaning Would that I knew, but I shall assuredly know when they shall have set it (namely, the SaHiyfap , or record, of my actions,) near, unfolded, and I am summoned, whether superiority be for me or against me when I am reckoned with: verily I shall be a watcher, or a witness, of the reckoning, or, accord. to some, as is said in the TA, acquainted with the reckoning ]: i. e. I shall know what evil I have done; for [as is said in the Kur lxxv. 14] man shall be a witness against himself: (S, O, TA:) IB says that, accord. to Seer, the correct reading is, rab~iY ElY AlHsAb mqyt [meaning my Lord is able to make the reckoning ] because he who is submissive to his Lord does not describe himself by this epithet: but IB adds that Seer has founded this remark upon the assumption that mqyt is here used as meaning muqotadirN ; and that if it be understood as syn. with HaAfiZN and $aAhidN , the former reading is not objectionable. (TA.) ― -b3- Almuqiytu is one of the best names of God: (TA:) and [as such] signifies The Possessor of power; (Fr, Zj, S, O, Msb, K, TA;) as He who gives to every man his quwt [or food ], (F, S, O, K, TA,) and likewise to everything: (TA:) or (as one of those names, TA) the Preserver, or Protector, (Zj, TA,) who gives to everything such preservation, or protection, as is needful. (TA.) It is said in the Kur [iv. 87], wakaAna A@ll~`hu EalaY kul~i $aYo'K muqiytFA , (S, O,) meaning [ For God is ] a possessor of power [ over everything, or is omnipotent ], (Ksh, Bd, Jel,) so He will requite everyone for what he has done: (Jel:) or a witness, [and] a preserver, or protector, or watcher. (Ksh, Bd.)

sourceDefinition: , (S, K,) aor. , (TA,) inf. n. katiytN , (K,) The cooking-pot boiled: (S, K:) or, made a sound in boiling: (K:) or, made a sound in boiling when the water in it was little; a lower sound than it makes when there is much water boiling in it; as though it said kato kato . (TA.) ― -b2- kat~ , aor. , (inf. n. katiytN , S,) He (a camel, S, K, or, as in the L, a bakor , or young camel,) uttered a gentle cry, (S, L, K,) between that termed k$y$ and that termed hdyr . (TA.) -A3- kat~a , [aor. ,] inf. n. katiytN , (tropical:) He walked gently; at a gentle pace: or he walked with short steps, but quickly; as also ↓ katokata , inf. n. katokatapN ; and ↓ takatokata . (TA.) ― -b2- kat~ , aor. , (inf. n. katiytN , S,) He (a camel, S, K, or, as in the L, a bakor , or young camel,) uttered a gentle cry, (S, L, K,) between that termed k$y$ and that termed hdyr . (TA.) ― -b3- He (a calf) lowed. (Nh.) ― -b4- kat~a , aor. , (inf. n. katiytN , K,) [ He (a man) made a sound like the gentle braying of a camel, ] by reason of rage, or wrath: (S:) or he (a man) made a a sound in his chest like that made by a bakor , or young camel, by reason of vehement rage, or wrath. (TS, K.) ― -b3- faEala bihi maA kat~ahu He did to him what displeased him, or grieved him. (TA.) -A5- kat~a , aor. , inf. n. kat~N , He numbered, counted, or computed, a people. You say A^ataAnaA bijayo$K maA yukat~u He came to us with an army not to be numbered, or counted, (IAar, S,) or computed, or of which the number could not be conjectured, and of which the end could not be reached. sourceDefinition: , (S, Msb, K,) so written in the Bári' and the T, but in some copies of the S, karofasN , [which is wrong,] (Msb,) [The herb smallage; apium graveolens of Linnæus,] a well known herb, or leguminous plant, (S, Msb, K,) of the hottest of leguminous plants ( mno A^aHar~i Albuquwli , TA, [but this is probably a mistake for mino A^aHoraAri Albuquwli of the leguminous plants that are eaten without being cooked, or that are slender and succulent or soft or sweet, ]) the utilities of which are great; diuretic; a disperser of winds and flatulence; a cleanser of the kidneys and liver and bladder, opening obstructions thereof; a strengthener of the venereal faculty, especially its seeds pounded with sugar and clarified butter, wonderful when drunk three days, (K,) upon an empty stomach, with avoidance of hurtful things, (TA,) but injurious to the young in the womb, and to the pregnant, and to those affected with epilepsy: (K:) said by Lth to be a foreign word introduced into the Arabic language, (TA.) and thought to be so by Az: (Msb:) in the O said to be arabicized; and, in the language of the people of Ghazneh, called krfH [or krfj ?] (TA.)

sourceDefinition: [ lab~a , originally labiba ,] sec. per. labibota , (S, K,) the most common form of the verb, (TA,) and [ lab~a , originally labuba , like Hab~a , originally Habuba , q. v.,] sec. pers. labubota , aor. yalab~u , (S, K,) in the dial. of El-Hijáz, deviating from rule as aor. of the latter form of the verb; (TA;) inf. n. labaAbapN (S, K) and lib~N and lab~N ; (TA;) and lab~a , aor. yalib~u , in the dial. of Nejd; like far~a , aor. yafir~u ; (TA;) and [ lab~a ], sec. pers. labibota , aor. yalub~u ; [contr. to analogy;] (Yz;) and [ lab~a ], sec. pers. labubota , aor. yalub~u ; [agreeably with analogy;] (Yoo;) He was, or became, possessed of lub~ , i. e., understanding, intellect, or intelligence. (TA.) ― -b2- lab~ahu , (K,) sec. pers. lababotu , aor. , inf. n. lab~N , (S,) He struck him upon the part called the lab~ap ; (S, K;) i. e., the pit above the breast, between the collar-bones; the place where camels are stabbed. definition: inf. n. of lab~a “ he remained, &c. ” ― -b2- lb~ayoka [ At thy service! lit., Doubly at thy service! ] (S, K, &c.) and lab~ayohi [ At his service: &c. ]. (TA.) [See an ex. voce marohuwbN . It is used...
sourceDefinition: inf. n. of lab~a “ he remained, &c. ” ― -b2- lb~ayoka [ At thy service! lit., Doubly at thy service! ] (S, K, &c.) and lab~ayohi [ At his service: &c. ]. (TA.) [See an ex. voce marohuwbN . It is used in the present day like our phrase At thy service, and may well be thus rendered, or with the addition of time after time. ] lb~yk is derived from A^alab~a [or rather from lab~a as syn. with Alb~ ] “ he remained &c. ”; and means I wait intent upon thy service, or upon obedience to thee: (Fr, S, K;) waiting [ at they service ] after waiting; [i. e., time after time; ] and answering [ thy commands ] after answering: (K:) it [i. e. the noun without the annexed pron.] is put in the acc. case as an inf. n. [used as an absolute complement of its own verb which is understood], as in HamodFA lil~`hi w$ukorFA ; and the right way would be to say lab~FA laka ; but it is put in the dual number for the sake of corroboration; meaning A_ilobaAbFA bika baEoda A_ilobaAbK , and A_iqaAmapF baEoda A_iqaAmapK , [ waiting at thy service, or in attendance upon thee, or in thy presence, after waiting, or time after time ]. (Fr, S.) [See also the similar expression saEodayoka .] Or lab~N signifies the obeying, or serving; or obedience, or service; from the original signification of the “ remaining, staying, abiding, or dwelling, ” [in a place]: the dual, in the nom. case, is lab~Ani ; and in the acc. and gen., lab~ayoni ; and the original meaning of lbyk is I have obeyed thee, or served thee, twice: [or I do obey thee, &c.: ] the n [of lb~yn ] being elided because of its being prefixed to the pron. (IAar.) Or lb~yk is from the saying daAru fulaAnK talub~u daAriY “ the house of such a one faces my house ”; (Kh, S, K;) and the meaning is I present myself before thee, (or repair to thee, K,) doing what thou likest, answering thee [ after answering, or time after time ]: the Y is to form the dual number; and indicates that the noun is in the acc. case as an inf. n. [used as mentioned above]. (Kh, S.) Or it means My love [ is given ] to thee; from the expression AimoraA^apN lab~apN “ a woman loving (and affectionate, TA,) to her husband ”: so in the K: but the expression, as related on the authority of Kh, is A^um~N lab~apN ; which is confirmed by a verse that he cites. (TA.) Or the meaning is A_ixolaASiY laka [ My sincere service, or the like, ( is given ) to thee; ] from the expression HasabN lubaAbN “ pure nobility, or the like. ” (K.) Accord. to Yoo, lb~yk is a noun in the sing. number with the pron. annexed to it: this noun is originally lab~abN , of the measure faEolalN : (not of the measure faE~alN , because this is rare in the language:) the the last b is changed into Y to avoid the reduplication; and thus it becomes lab~aYN : then the Y , being movent, and immediately preceded by fet-hah, is changed into A ; and it becomes lab~aA [or lab~aY , for the Y in this case is called A ]: then, being conjoined with k in lb~yk , and with h in lb~yh , its A is changed into Y ; after the same manner as you say A_ilayoka and Ealayoka and ladayoka . (TA.) [But see what here follows.] ― -b3- lab~aYo yadayoka is a phrase exactly similar to lb~yk , meaning At the service (or, lit. doubly at the service ) of thy hands! and this is said, in the S, art. lbY to be at variance with the opinion of Yoo, given above; for, if lb~Y were similar to A_ilaY &c., being prefixed to a noun, not a pron., it would be lab~aY yadayoka , not lab~aYo .] Accord. to El-Khattá- bee, lb~Y ydyk signifies May thy hands be safe and sound! the desinential syntax being disregarded in the saying ydyk , which rightly should be yadaAka , in order that ydyk may match in sound with lb~yk : but Z says, that the meaning is, I will obey thee, and be at thy free disposal, as a thing which thou shalt dispose of with thy hands in whatever manner thou shalt please. (TA.) ― -b4- In like manner you say lab~aYo zayodK [ At the service (or doubly at the service ) of Zeyd ]. (Msb.) See art. lbY . ― -b5- lab~i , with kesreh for its termination, like A^amos and gaAqi , is also related as having been used: (Sb:) [and it is still used in some parts, as signifying At thy service! ]. -A2- lab~N keeping, or adhering, [to a thing]: remaining, or staying. (K.) ― -b2- A camel-driver who keeps constantly to the work of driving the camels, not leaving them. (TA.) ― -b3- rajulN lab~N A man who keeps to a thing, or affair, or business; as also ↓ labiybN ; (S, K;) a man who keeps to his art, or craft, or trade, not ceasing from it. (TA.) ― -b4- rjlN lab~N Tab~N A man who keeps to business, [ and is skilful, expert, clever, or intelligent ]. (S, TA.) -A3- lab One who renders himself near to people by affection and friendship [or is friendly and affectionate to them ]: courteous, polite, or affable: fem. lab~apN : pl. libaAbN . (TA.) ― -b2- AimoraA^apN lab~apN A woman who renders herself near by affection and friendship [or is friendly and affectionate ], to people; (S;) courteous, polite, or affable: (S, K:) a woman loving to her husband; (K;) affectionate to him: or, accord. to Kh, the expression is A^um~N lab~apN : see lab~N , above. (TA.)

[See also the similar expression saEodayoka .] Or lab~N signifies the obeying, or serving; or obedience, or service; from the original signification of the “ remaining, staying, abiding, or dwelling, ” [in a place]: the dual, in the nom. case, is lab~Ani ; and in the acc. and gen., lab~ayoni ; and the original meaning of lbyk is I have obeyed thee, or served thee, twice: [or I do obey thee, &c.: ] the n [of lb~yn ] being elided because of its being prefixed to the pron. (IAar.) Or lb~yk is from the saying daAru fulaAnK talub~u daAriY “ the house of such a one faces my house ”; (Kh, S, K;) and the meaning is I present myself before thee, (or repair to thee, K,) doing what thou likest, answering thee [ after answering, or time after time ]: the Y is to form the dual number; and indicates that the noun is in the acc. case as an inf. n. [used as mentioned above]. (Kh, S.) Or it means My love [ is given ] to thee; from the expression AimoraA^apN lab~apN “ a woman loving (and affectionate, TA,) to her husband ”: so in the K: but the expression, as related on the authority of Kh, is A^um~N lab~apN ; which is confirmed by a verse that he cites. (TA.) Or the meaning is A_ixolaASiY laka [ My sincere service, or the like, ( is given ) to thee; ] from the expression HasabN lubaAbN “ pure nobility, or the like. ” (K.) Accord. to Yoo, lb~yk is a noun in the sing. number with the pron. annexed to it: this noun is originally lab~abN , of the measure faEolalN : (not of the measure faE~alN , because this is rare in the language:) the the last b is changed into Y to avoid the reduplication; and thus it becomes lab~aYN : then the Y , being movent, and immediately preceded by fet-hah, is changed into A ; and it becomes lab~aA [or lab~aY , for the Y in this case is called A ]: then, being conjoined with k in lb~yk , and with h in lb~yh , its A is changed into Y ; after the same manner as you say A_ilayoka and Ealayoka and ladayoka . (TA.) [But see what here follows.] ― -b3- lab~aYo yadayoka is a phrase exactly similar to lb~yk , meaning At the service (or, lit. doubly at the service ) of thy hands! and this is said, in the S, art. lbY to be at variance with the opinion of Yoo, given above; for, if lb~Y were similar to A_ilaY &c., being prefixed to a noun, not a pron., it would be lab~aY yadayoka , not lab~aYo .] Accord. to El-Khattá- bee, lb~Y ydyk signifies May thy hands be safe and sound! the desinential syntax being disregarded in the saying ydyk , which rightly should be yadaAka , in order that ydyk may match in sound with lb~yk : but Z says, that the meaning is, I will obey thee, and be at thy free disposal, as a thing which thou shalt dispose of with thy hands in whatever manner thou shalt please. (TA.) ― -b4- In like manner you say lab~aYo zayodK [ At the service (or doubly at the service ) of Zeyd ]. (Msb.) See art. lbY . ― -b5- lab~i , with kesreh for its termination, like A^amos and gaAqi , is also related as having been used: (Sb:) [and it is still used in some parts, as signifying At thy service! ]. -A2- lab~N keeping, or adhering, [to a thing]: remaining, or staying. (K.) ― -b2- A camel-driver who keeps constantly to the work of driving the camels, not leaving them. (TA.) ― -b3- rajulN lab~N A man who keeps to a thing, or affair, or business; as also ↓ labiybN ; (S, K;) a man who keeps to his art, or craft, or trade, not ceasing from it. (TA.) ― -b4- rjlN lab~N Tab~N A man who keeps to business, [ and is skilful, expert, clever, or intelligent ]. (S, TA.) -A3- lab One who renders himself near to people by affection and friendship [or is friendly and affectionate to them ]: courteous, polite, or affable: fem. lab~apN : pl. libaAbN . (TA.) ― -b2- AimoraA^apN lab~apN A woman who renders herself near by affection and friendship [or is friendly and affectionate ], to people; (S;) courteous, polite, or affable: (S, K:) a woman loving to her husband; (K;) affectionate to him: or, accord. to Kh, the expression is A^um~N lab~apN : see lab~N , above. (TA.)

definition: (S, K) and ↓ lubaAbN (Msb) of a nut, an almond, and the like, What is in the inside;
sourceDefinition: (S, K) and ↓ lubaAbN (Msb) of a nut, an almond, and the like, What is in the inside; (S;) the heart, or kernel: (K:) of a palm-tree, the heart, or pith, called qalobN or qulobN . (S, K.) Pl. of the former lubuwbN . (S.) ― -b2- lub~N (S, K) and ↓ lubaAbN (TA) What is pure, or the choice, or best, part, of anything: (S, K:) pl. of the former A^alobaAbN . (A'Obeyd.) ― -b3- lub~u AlHinoTapi [ The purest substance of wheat: see faAluw*N :] (T, L, art. fl* &c:) [also called Albur~i ↓ lubaAbu , acc. to Sprenger, “ Life of Mohammad, ” (Allahabad, 1851,) p. 24, note 1.] ― -b4- [Hence,] lub~N of a man, (TA,) (tropical:) Understanding; intellect; intelligence; or mind; syn. EaqolN : (S, K:) the understanding, &c., that is put into the heart of a man: so called because it is the choicest or best part of him: or it is not so called unless it is pure from cupidity, or lust, and foul imaginations; and therefore has a more special sense than Eql : so in the Keshf el-Keshsháf: (TA:) pl. A^alobaAbN , and sometimes A^alub~N ; (S, K;) like as A^abow^usN is pl. of buw^osN , and A^anoEumN of nuEomN ; (S;) and A^alobubN ; (S, K;) the last being used, without incorporating the second b into the first, in case of necessity in poetry. (S.) ― -b5- banaAtu A^alobubK Certain veins in the heart; the sources of tenderness, affection, kindness, or compassion. (S, K.) ― -b6- taA^obaY lahu *`lika banaAtu A^alobubiY [ My tenderness forbids the doing so to him ]: said by an Arab woman of the desert, on the occasion of her reproving her son, to one who asked her why she did not curse him. (S.) ― -b7- A^aloqaY Ealayohi banaAta A^alobubihi He loved it. (L, art. $r .) ― -b8- The following words of the poet, qado Ealimato *aAka banaAtu A^alobubiho signify, accord. to the M, My intellect knew that. (TA.) El-Mubarrad read A^alobabiho in the above words of the poet: (TA:) the meaning of these words, accord. to him, is, The daughters of the most intelligent of his tribe knew this. (S, TA.) ― -b9- If you form a pl. from [the pl.] A^alobubN , it is A^alaAbibu ; and the dim. n. is A^ulayobibN . (S.) ― -b10- *uw lub~K Possessing, having, or a person of, understanding, or intelligence: pl. A^uwluwA A@loA^alobaAbi [ persons of understandings ]. (TA.) See also labiybN and malobuwbN . ― -b11- lub~N (assumed tropical:) The self, substance, or essence, of anything. (TA.) -A2- Poison: (K:) the poison of the serpent is sometimes thus called. (Abu-l-Hasan, L.) -A3- lub~N , in the dial. of El-Andalus and El-'Adweh, A certain beast of prey, resembling the wolf, said by AHei not to exist in other countries. (TA.)

definition: and ↓ lababN The stabbing-place in an animal;
sourceDefinition: and ↓ lababN The stabbing-place in an animal; (S, L, K;) the middle of the breast: (L:) the pit above the breast, between the collar-bones; the place where camels are stabbed: (see lab~ahu :) or the bones [probably a mistake for the part next above the bones ] that are above the breast, and below the throat, between the collar-bones, where camels are stabbed: he who says that it is the pit in the throat errs: (IKt:) [for it is just beneath the throat:] pl. of the former lab~aAtN (S) and libaAbN ; and of the latter A^alobaAbN . (TA.) Also, both words, (the latter ↓ accord. to the S and K, and the former accord. to the TA,) and ↓ mutalab~abN , (TA,) The place of the breast where the necklace or collar lies, or hangs, (S, K,) in anything; (S;) [i. e., in a human being or a beast:] or the pit above it: (TA:) pl. of lababN , A^alobaAbN . (S.) Lh mentions the phrase A_in~ahaA laHasanahu All~ab~aAti [ Verily she is beautiful in the upper part of the breast ]: as though the sing. were applied to each portion of it, and the pl. formed to denote the whole. (TA.)

definition: A large quantity of water, which, when the aperture ( mafotaH , as in the T;
sourceDefinition: A large quantity of water, which, when the aperture ( mafotaH , as in the T; or fatoH , as in MS. copies of the K; in the CK futuH ;) [mean- ing the aperture of the tank or the like] carries off thereof what it can, and the hole by which it runs out ( Sunobuwruhu , meaning the mavoEab of the water, TA,) is too narrow to admit it freely on account of its abundance, whirls round, and becomes like the spout of a vessel. (T, K.) AM says, I know not whether it be an Arabic word or arabicized; but the people of El-'Irák are fond of using it. (TA.) [It appears to be from the Persian luwlaho , as Golius thinks; and is used in modern Arabic in several other senses; namely, A tube through which water flows: the spout of a ewer, of an alembic, and the like: a cock, or tap: a turning pin, or peg; a screw: and the like. Its more appropriate place, I think, would be in an art. composed of the letters llb (accord. to what is said of mulawolabN in the S, K); or rather, (accord. to its derivation from the Pers.,) lwlb .] Pl. lawaAlibu . (TA.)

definition: , (S, Mgh, Msb,) inf.

definition: (IDrd, S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ maroDN : (Msb, K:) see 1: i.
sourceDefinition: (IDrd, S, O, Msb, K) and ↓ maroDN : (Msb, K:) see 1: i. q. suqomN [ Disease, disorder, distemper, sickness, illness, or malady ]; (IDrd, S;) which is the contr. of SiH~apN ; and affects man and the camel [&c.]: (IDrd:) or a certain state foreign to the constitution or temperament, injurious to the intellect; whence it is known that pains and tumours are accidents arising therefrom: or, as IF says, that whereby a man passes beyond the limit of health or soundness or perfection or rectitude, whether it be disease ( Eil~ap ), or (assumed tropical:) hypocrisy, or (assumed tropical:) a falling short of doing what he ought to do in an affair: (Msb:) or a dark and disordered state of the constitution or temperament, after a clear and right state thereof: (O, K:) or ↓ maroDN is (assumed tropical:) [ a disease ] of the heart: (K:) Aboo-Is-hák says, maraDN and suqomN are said to be in the body and (assumed tropical:) in religion, like as SiH~apN is said to be in the body and in religion; and ↓ maroDN is in the heart, applying to (assumed tropical:) everything whereby a man quits a state of soundness or perfection or rectitude in religion: (TA:) and As says, I recited to Aboo-'Amr Ibn-El-'Alà [the words of the Kur, ii. 9, &c.,] fiY quluwbihimo maraDN and he said to me ↓ “ maroDN , O boy ”: (AHát, IDrd, Msb:) and maraDN , or this and ↓ maroDN also, signifies (assumed tropical:) doubt: and (assumed tropical:) hypocrisy: (K:) and (assumed tropical:) weakness of belief: (TA:) and the former, (TA,) or ↓ both, (K,) (assumed tropical:) languor, or languidness, or weakness: (K:) and (assumed tropical:) darkness (IAar, K) in the heart: (IAar:) and (assumed tropical:) defectiveness; deficiency; or imperfection; (IAar, K;) which last is said by IAar to be the primary signification: (TA:) or maraDN in the body is a languor, or languidness, or weakness, of the limbs, or members: and in the eye, (assumed tropical:) weakness of sight: and in the heart, (assumed tropical:) a flagging, or remissness, in respect of the truth: (Ibn-'Arafeh:) or it properly signifies an accidental affection of the body, which puts it out of the right state proper to it, and necessarily occasions interruption, or infirmity, in its actions: and tropically, (tropical:) affections of the mind, which interrupt, or mar, its integrity; such as (tropical:) ignorance; and (tropical:) evil belief; and (tropical:) envy; and (tropical:) malevolence, or malice; and (tropical:) love of acts of disobedience; for these prevent from the attaining of excellences, or lead to the cessation of true eternal life: (Bd, ii. 9:) it is a gen. n.: (IDrd:) and the n. un. is ↓ maroDapN : (A, TA:) it is one of the inf. ns. which have pls., like $ugolN and EaqolN ; the pls. of these three being A^amoraADN and A^a$ogaAlN and EuquwlN . (Sb.) fiY qulowbihimo maraDN , in the Kur, [ii. 9, &c.,] means (assumed tropical:) In their hearts is doubt: (AO:) or (assumed tropical:) doubt and hypocrisy. (TA.) And Al~a*iY fiY qalobihi maraDN , in the same, [xxxiii. 32,] (assumed tropical:) In whose heart is darkness: or (assumed tropical:) flagging, or remissness, in respect of what is commanded and what is forbidden: or (assumed tropical:) love of adultery or fornication: (TA:) or hypocrisy. (A.)

definition: [ Diseased; disordered; distempered; sick; or ill; ] in the state termed maraDN (Msb, K) denoting that change of the constitution or temperament which is described in the explanation of the latter...
sourceDefinition: [ Diseased; disordered; distempered; sick; or ill; ] in the state termed maraDN (Msb, K) denoting that change of the constitution or temperament which is described in the explanation of the latter word above; (K;) as also ↓ mariDN (K,) and ↓ maAriDN , (IB, Msb, K,) the first [and second] being from the verb of which the inf. n. is maraDN , and the third from that of which the inf. n. is maroDN , (Msb,) and ↓ mamoruwDN , and ↓ mutamar~iDN : (TA:) or, applied to a body, it signifies deficient in strength: (IAar:) pl. miraADN (A, K, TA:) and maroDaY (IDrd, Msb, K) and maraADaY (IDrd, K) and muraDaA='u ; (TA;) or miraADN may be pl. of maAriDN (TA) [or of mariDN ]. Accord. to Lh, you say, Eudo fulaAnN faA_in~ahu mariyDN [ Visit thou such a one, for he is sick ]: and laA taA^okulo h`*aA A_ino A^akalotahu ↓ AlT~aEaAma faA_in~aka maAriDN meaning tamoraDu [i. e. Eat not thou this food, for thou wilt be sick if thou eat it ]. (TA.) [ mariyDN has also several tropical significations.] You say also, EayonN mariyDapN (tropical:) An eye in which is languor, or languidness, or weakness: (S, TA:) pl. A^aEoyanN miraADN , and maroDaY . (A, TA.) And A_imoraA^apN mariyDapu AlA^aloHaAZi and mryDpu Aln~aZari (assumed tropical:) A woman weak in sight. (IDrd.) And qalobN mariyDN (assumed tropical:) A heart deficient in religion. [IAar.) And $amosN mariyDapN (tropical:) A sun having a feeble light; (A, K; *) not clear, (S, TA,) and not beautiful. (TA.) And A^aroDN mariyDapN (tropical:) A land in which are frequent seditions, or factions, or conflicts, or dissensions, (A, TA,) and wars, (A,) and slaughters: (TA:) or (assumed tropical:) in a weak condition: (K:) or straitened with its inhabitants: or (assumed tropical:) in which the wind is still, and the heat intense: or that causes disease; meaning (assumed tropical:) corrupt in its air. (TA.) And riyHN mariyDapN (A, K) (tropical:) A weak wind: (K:) or (tropical:) a still wind: or (tropical:) a wind intensely hot, and blowing feebly. (TA.) And layolapN mariyDapN (tropical:) A night in which no star shines; (A;) in which the sky is clouded, so that there is no light. (TA.) And raA^oYN mariyDN (A, TA) (tropical:) An opinion deviating from what is right. (TA.)

sourceDefinition: , aor. , (inf. n. magodN , S, L,) He (a child, and a lamb or kid, S, L, and a young camel, L, K) sucked his mother: he (a young camel) struck his mother in her udder with his head, and sucked her: and he (a lamb or kid) took the teat of his mother in his mouth to suck; (L;) as also maEa*a , with the unpointed E and the pointed * . (IKtt.) ― -b2- magada He sucked, or sucked in, a thing: (K:) he sucked, or sucked in, the inside of Sarabap , i. e., [a piece of] the gum of the TaloH ; for there is sometimes in the inner part thereof what resembles glue and the honey of dates or bees. (S, L.) See also magodN , below. ― -b3- magada , aor. , inf. n. magodN ; (L, K;) and magida , aor. , (L,) inf. n. magadN ; (L, K;) He, (L,) or it, (the body, K,) became full and fat. (L, K.) ― -b4- magadahu , (aor. , inf. n. magodN , S, L.) It (a pleasant, or an ample, and easy, life) nourished him: (AZ, IAar, S, L:) or it (a life, or manner of living) nourished him, and rendered him in a state of amplitude and ease. (K.) ― -b5- magada He (a man, L) and it (a plant, L, K, or other thing, K, or anything, L) became tall. (Aboo-Málik, L, K.) ― -b6- magada fiY Eayo$K naAEimK , (aor. , inf. n. magodN , S, L,) a phrase mentioned by Fr, (S,) He (a man) lived, and enjoyed abundant comforts, or luxury, in a pleasant, or an ample and easy, state of life. (K.) ― -b7- magadahu It (youth) caused him still to flourish, or to be in the flower of age. (En-Nadr, L.) ― -b8- magada He became in the full prime of youth. (L.) -A2- magada , aor. , inf. n. magoda , He plucked out hair: (L:) as also maEada . (L, art. mEd .) ― -b2- magada mawoDiEa Algur~api He plucked out the hair in the place of the blaze, or white mark on the forehead or face, of a horse, in order that it might become gray. (L, K.)

definition: The flower, or flourishing period, of youth.
sourceDefinition: The flower, or flourishing period, of youth. (En-Nadr, L.) ― -b2- Soft; tender; delicate: pleasant; easy and ample: syn. naAEimN : (S, L, K:) applied to the period of youth: (S, L:) and to life, or a manner of living. (L.) ― -b3- Also, (K,) or magodu Aljisomi , (L,) Soft and plump: applied to a camel: (L, K:) or (so in the L; in the K, and) big, or bulky; (L, K;) as also maEodN ; (L;) and tall: (K:) applied to anything. (L.) -A2- magodN , applied to the gur~ap , or blaze, on the forehead or face of a horse; app. an inf. n. used in the sense of a pass. part. n.; Having the hair plucked out in order that it may become gray: (L:) the term magodN is used with relation to the blaze of a horse when it appears as though it were swollen; for the hair is plucked out in order that it may grow white: (S, L:) and with relation to the forelock, when it is as though burnt. (L.) -A3- magodN (L, K) and ↓ magadN (L) The fruit of the [ tree called ] tanoDub : or (so in the L; but in the K, and) the [ plant called ] luf~aAH [q. v.]: (L, K:) or the wild lf~AH : (L:) or, both words, (so in the L; but in the K, and) the [ plant called ] baA*inojaAn : (L, K:) or a plant resembling the nA*njAn , growing at the roots of the EiDah : (L:) and the former word, a fruit resembling the cucumber, (Aboo-Sa'eed, L, K,) which is eaten: (Aboo-Sa'eed, L:) or a kind of tree that twines about other trees, more slender than the vine, having long, thin, and soft, leaves, and producing a fruit like that of the banana, but thinner in the peel and more juicy, which is sweet, and is not peeled [ to be eaten ], with pips like those of the apple; people share this fruit among themselves, taking it by turns, alighting where it grows, and eating it; it appears first green; then becomes yellow; and then, at last, green [ again, or probably red; for I think that yxDr~ , in the L, from which this is taken, is a mistake for yHmr~ ]: the word is a coll. gen. n.: and] the n. un. is with p : (AHn, L:) ISd says, I have not heard magadapN ; but ↓ magadN may be a quasi-pl. n. of magodapN ; like as HalaqN is of HaloqapN , and falakN of falokapN . (L.) ― -b2- magodN i. q. SarabapN , meaning as explained above, at 1: (S, L,) also, the gum of the lote-tree, sidor : (Aboo-Sa'eed, L:) or, of the lok-tree of the desert. (S, L.)

definition: He accepted naSiyHap , (S, K, *) or nuSoH , (TA,) [i.
sourceDefinition: He accepted naSiyHap , (S, K, *) or nuSoH , (TA,) [i. e., sincere, honest, or faithful, advice or counsel, &c. ]. As an ex. of this signification the following is cited yaquwlu A@notaSiHoniY A_in~aniY laka naASiHN [ He says, Accept my sincere advice, for I am to thee a sincere adviser ]: (TA:) and A_inotaSiHN kitaAba A@ll~`hi Accept the sincere or faithful advice or counsel of the Book of God.
